title: Lilly presents first clinical data in platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer for its investigational, next-generation, FRα-targeting ADC at ESMO 2026
source: Eli Lilly and Company - Official RSS
query: https://investor.lilly.com/rss.xml
content_text:
Lilly presents first clinical data in platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer for its investigational, next-generation, FRα-targeting ADC at ESMO 2026
October 24, 2026
PDF Version 
Sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M) in combination with bevacizumab demonstrated a 79% confirmed objective response rate and 100% disease control rate, with similar activity observed across FR α expression levels 
Clinical activity with Sofe-M was maintained even in patients with prior PARP inhibitor exposure, patients who typically experience poor outcomes with platinum-based chemotherapy 
Sofe-M is currently being studied in both platinum-sensitive and platinum-resistant ovarian cancer in multiple Phase 3 studies as part of the FRAmework-01 master protocol 
INDIANAPOLIS , Oct. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Eli Lilly and Company (NYSE: LLY) today announced new Phase 1 data showing that its investigational folate receptor alpha (FRα) antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M) plus bevacizumab achieved a confirmed objective response rate (cORR) of 79% and a disease control rate (DCR) of 100% in patients with platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC). A cORR of 79% or higher was seen in both poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitor (PARPi)-treated and PARPi-naïve patients. These data will be shared in an oral presentation at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Annual Congress in Madrid, Spain .
FRα is expressed in almost all ovarian cancers, at much higher levels than in healthy tissue, making it a target that can help direct treatment to tumor cells. Sofe-M is an FRα-targeting ADC composed of an Fc-silent, FRα-specific humanized monoclonal antibody linked to exatecan, a topoisomerase I inhibitor, via a proprietary cleavable polysarcosine linker. The antibody is designed to bind FRα on the surface of tumor cells, delivering exatecan directly into the tumor cell to disrupt DNA replication.
Jacob Van Naarden , Executive Vice President and President of Lilly Oncology: "The standard of care for platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer has remained unchanged for a decade and demands new treatment options. Results for Sofe-M show a promising efficacy and tolerability profile across both platinum-resistant and platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer, regardless of FRα expression levels or prior treatment. These data give us confidence as we continue to study Sofe-M in our Phase 3 FRAmework-01 program to bring this potential new medicine to the women who need it."
The Phase 1 study is evaluating Sofe-M plus bevacizumab in patients with advanced solid tumors, including a cohort of 33 women with PSOC who received Sofe-M (4 mg/kg) plus bevacizumab (15 mg/kg). Patients received a median of three prior systemic regimens (range 1–6), including prior PARPi (67%) and prior bevacizumab (70%). As of the July 6, 2026 , data cutoff, the cORR among the 29 patients with measurable disease was 79.3% (23/29; 6 complete responses [CR, 20.7%] and 17 partial responses [PR, 58.6%]), and DCR was 100%. Responses were consistent across FRα expression levels and prior PARPi exposure. Median duration of response (DOR) and median progression-free survival (PFS) were not reached at median follow-ups of 6.2 and 10.2 months, respectively.
Chrisann Kyi , MD, Gynecologic Medical Oncologist & Early Drug Development Specialist at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center : "The durable and robust responses we've seen in patients with platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer are important, particularly in a PARPi pretreated population, where the response rate seen with Sofe-M exceeds what has been reported in published platinum re-challenge studies. The observed safety profile and low discontinuation rates, combined with early efficacy results, support the continued investigation of Sofe-M as a potentially meaningful new option for patients."
Sofe-M plus bevacizumab demonstrated a safety profile consistent with the known profiles of each medicine. No new safety signals were observed. The most common treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) across all patients included epistaxis (73%), nausea (73%), anemia (58%), neutropenia (55%), and fatigue (52%). The most common Grade ≥3 TEAEs were neutropenia (42%) and anemia (24%); febrile neutropenia occurred in 3% of patients, and G-CSF prophylaxis was not mandated. Any-grade neuropathy occurred in 9% of patients, with no Grade ≥3 events. Dose reductions occurred in 42% of patients, and 6% discontinued treatment due to an adverse event.
The FRAmework-01 program is evaluating Sofe-M in three global Phase 3 trials across both platinum-resistant and platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer: Part A tests Sofe-M as monotherapy in platinum-resistant disease; Part B tests Sofe-M plus bevacizumab in platinum-sensitive disease that progressed on or within six months of completing a PARPi; and Part C tests Sofe-M plus bevacizumab in PARPi-naïve platinum-sensitive disease. The study is being conducted in partnership with the European Network for Gynaecological Oncological Trial groups (ENGOT - lead groups GINECO/NOGGO e.V.), the GOG Foundation (GOG), and the Asia-Pacific Gynecologic Oncology Trials Group (APGOT).
For more information on Lilly 's oncology pipeline, click here .
Frequently Asked Questions 
What is sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M)? 
Sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M) is an investigational folate receptor alpha (FRα)-targeting antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) being studied for the treatment of ovarian cancer and other solid tumors. It is designed to selectively bind to cancer cells expressing FRα and deliver a topoisomerase I inhibitor payload directly to those cells.
What is an antibody-drug conjugate? 
An antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) is a type of medicine that pairs an antibody with a cell-killing payload. The antibody is designed to recognize and bind to a specific protein found on the surface of cancer cells, and the payload is released once the ADC reaches its target, allowing the medicine to attack cancer cells while limiting exposure to healthy tissue. 1
How is Sofe-M different from other FRα-targeted ADCs? 
Sofe-M is designed to target FRα across a broad range of expression levels, including in tumors with lower FRα expression. In this Phase 1 study, Sofe-M plus bevacizumab showed a confirmed objective response rate of 79.3% in platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC), with consistent activity across FRα expression levels and regardless of prior PARP inhibitor exposure. Earlier studies in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (PROC) also demonstrated responses observed across all FRα expression levels and in patients previously treated with mirvetuximab soravtansine (MIRV). 2 These results are being further evaluated in Lilly 's ongoing Phase 3 FRAmework-01 program, which is studying Sofe-M across both platinum-resistant and platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer.
What are the results with sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M) in the treatment of platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC)?
The Phase 1 study demonstrated encouraging clinical activity, including a confirmed objective response rate (cORR) of 79.3% and a disease control rate (DCR) of 100%, in heavily pretreated patients with platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer. Activity was observed across FRα expression levels and regardless of prior PARP inhibitor exposure. Median duration of response (DOR) and median progression-free survival (PFS) were not reached at median follow-ups of 6.2 and 10.2 months, respectively. Sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M) plus bevacizumab demonstrated a safety profile consistent with the known profiles of each medicine, with no new safety signals observed and a low rate of discontinuation due to adverse events (6%). These findings support continued investigation of Sofe-M in the ongoing Phase 3 FRAmework-01 trial.
In this study Sofe-M was dosed at 4 mg/kg. Why is it dosed at 3mg/kg in the Phase 3 FRAmework-01 trial? 
The 3 mg/kg dose of Sofe-M was selected as the recommended phase 3 dose (RP3D), based on analysis of the safety, efficacy and PK data as monotherapy. The ORR was comparable between the two doses, with ORRs of 59.0% (95% CI 42.1, 74.4) and 58.8% (95% CI 32.9, 81.6), at 4 mg/kg and 3mg/kg doses, respectively. Safety signals were higher at 4 mg/kg versus 3 mg/kg, with Grade ≥3 TRAEs at 56.4% vs 35.3% and dose reductions of 41.0% vs 23.5%.
What are historical clinical trial results for standard of care in platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC)? 
For patients who recur after platinum-based chemotherapy and PARP inhibitor (PARPi) maintenance, published real world data on subsequent platinum re-challenge have shown modest response rates, with an objective response rate (ORR) of 41.9%. 3 Other studies of platinum-based regimens, such as OCEANS, were conducted prior to the routine use of PARPi maintenance and did not include patients previously treated with a PARPi, 4 a population that now represents a majority of patients with recurrent PSOC, including those enrolled in Sofe-M's Phase 1 study.
What is platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC)? 
Platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC) is characterized as ovarian cancer that comes back more than six months after platinum-based chemotherapy. While people with PSOC can often be treated with platinum again, the disease tends to return, and each recurrence can leave fewer treatment options and shorter remissions. 5 
What is the current unmet need in platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC)? 
The standard of care for PSOC has remained largely unchanged for more than a decade, even as understanding of which patients benefit from it has evolved. Approximately 50% of PSOC patients have HRD-positive tumors, meaning their tumors carry a specific DNA-repair deficiency. 6 These patients tend to have longer progression-free survival with upfront platinum-based chemotherapy plus a PARP inhibitor (PARPi). 6 However, when these patients do recur after PARPi maintenance, response rates to subsequent platinum-based treatment are modest. 6 Patients with non-HRD-positive tumors see minimal benefit from PARPi to begin with and generally have a poorer prognosis overall. 6 Despite these different outcomes between HRD-positive and HRD-negative patients, treatment approaches for PSOC have not meaningfully changed to reflect that distinction.
What is the difference between platinum-resistant (PROC) and platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC)?
The difference comes down to timing. If ovarian cancer returns more than six months after platinum-based chemotherapy, it's considered platinum-sensitive, and patients often respond well to platinum treatment again. If the cancer returns within six months, or continues growing during treatment, it's considered platinum-resistant, and platinum-based chemotherapy is generally no longer effective. Because platinum resistance tends to develop gradually, each recurrence can bring a shorter remission, even while a patient's disease is still classified as platinum-sensitive. 6
What is folate receptor alpha (FRα), and why is FRα expression level important in treating ovarian cancer? 
FRα is expressed in almost all ovarian cancers, at much higher levels than in healthy tissue, making it a target that can help direct treatment to tumor cells. 7 FRα expression level refers to the amount of the protein present on a tumor and may influence eligibility for or response to certain FRα-targeted therapies. 7 
How is the FRAmework-01 clinical trial designed? 
FRAmework-01 is a global, three-part Phase 3 trial studying sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M) across both platinum-resistant and platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer in a single program: Part A tests Sofe-M as monotherapy in platinum-resistant disease; Part B tests Sofe-M plus bevacizumab in platinum-sensitive disease that progressed on or within six months of completing a PARPi; and Part C tests Sofe-M plus bevacizumab in PARPi-naïve platinum-sensitive disease. 
The trial's main measure of success across all three parts is how long patients go without their cancer progressing. The study is being conducted in partnership with the European Network for Gynaecological Oncological Trial groups (ENGOT - lead groups GINECO/NOGGO e.V.), the GOG Foundation (GOG), and the Asia-Pacific Gynecologic Oncology Trials Group (APGOT). Enrollment is ongoing globally with first registrational dose in Q4 2025 for PROC and in Q1 2026 for PSOC.
About Ovarian Cancer 
Ovarian cancer is the sixth leading cause of cancer death among women in the United States . 8 While most patients initially respond to platinum-based chemotherapy, approximately 70% will experience recurrence, leading to progressively shorter remission periods with each subsequent treatment. 6 When cancer recurs during or within six months of platinum therapy, known as platinum-resistant disease, patients face limited treatment options. 6,9 
About Sofetabart Mipitecan 
Sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M; LY4170156) is composed of an Fc-silent, folate receptor alpha (FRα) specific humanized monoclonal antibody linked to exatecan, a topoisomerase I inhibitor, via a proprietary cleavable polysarcosine linker (PSARlink). Sofe-M was designed to target FRα across all expression levels with improved therapeutic index. FRα is a cell-surface glycoprotein encoded by the gene FOLR1 that binds to the essential nutrients folic acid and reduced folates, bringing them into cells to facilitate cell division and growth. FRα is overexpressed in many solid tumors such as ovarian and endometrial cancers. Sofe-M has received Breakthrough Therapy Designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (PROC) and is currently being evaluated in the Phase 3 FRAmework-01 program. The study is being conducted in partnership with the European Network for Gynaecological Oncological Trial groups (ENGOT - lead groups GINECO/NOGGO e.V.), the GOG Foundation (GOG), and the Asia-Pacific Gynecologic Oncology Trials Group (APGOT). 
About FRAmework-01 
FRAmework-01 ( NCT07213804 ) is a Phase 3, randomized, open-label, three-part study evaluating sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M; LY4170156) in patients with recurrent epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer. Part A tests Sofe-M as monotherapy in platinum-resistant disease; Part B tests Sofe-M plus bevacizumab in platinum-sensitive disease that progressed on or within six months of completing a PARPi; and Part C tests Sofe-M plus bevacizumab in PARPi-naïve platinum-sensitive disease. The primary endpoint is progression-free survival (PFS), assessed by the investigator in Part A and by blinded independent central review (BICR) in Parts B and C. Key secondary endpoints are overall survival, objective response rate, duration of response, and safety. The FRAmework-01 study is in partnership with the European Network for Gynecological Oncological Trial groups (ENGOT - lead groups GINECO / NOGGO e.V.), the GOG Foundation (GOG) , and the Asia-Pacific Gynecologic Oncology Trials Group (APGOT) .
More information on FRAmework-01 can be found on clinicaltrials.gov .

Charles River, Labcorp, and FDA Collaborate to Validate New Preclinical Methods for Abuse Potential Assessment
PDF Version 
Joint research effort seeks to improve abuse potential assessment tools to support drug development and public health decision-making 
WILMINGTON, Mass. --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 22, 2026--
Charles River Laboratories International, Inc. (NYSE: CRL) today announced a Research Collaboration Agreement (RCA) with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and Labcorp for developing sensitive screening tools to quantify and rank the abuse potential of new drugs, including abuse-deterrent formulations (ADFs) and emerging drugs of abuse. The agreement establishes a joint research framework to enhance objective, standardized metrics for quantifying abuse potential in preclinical models which may inform regulatory assessments of abuse potential under the Controlled Substances Act (CSA).
“Assessing abuse potential is essential for identifying risks and ensuring the safety of new drugs,” said Dr. Namandjé N. Bumpus , Chief Science and Innovation Officer, Charles River. “This collaboration will improve public health safeguards and ultimately amplify our shared efforts to protect patients and communities.”
Evaluating Abuse Potential
Abuse potential assessments are vital components of the safety evaluation of central nervous system-active compounds and are relied upon by FDA and the Drug Enforcement Administration for scheduling control measures.
Enhancing objective, reproducible methods to assess abuse potential is important for advancing regulatory science and supporting evidence-based decision-making. This collaboration will help evaluate approaches that could improve the consistency and sensitivity of abuse potential assessments, ultimately contributing to efforts to protect public health.
Charles River has extensive expertise in assessing abuse potential, having conducted over 100 abuse potential studies and contributed to assessments of the abuse potential of 15 FDA-approved products. As part of its participation in the collaboration, Charles River will leverage behavioral economic models of supply and demand to analyze self-administration data. These models assess the relative reinforcing properties of substances, helping researchers evaluate abuse potential and compare it with that of known drugs of abuse. A recent behavioral economics pilot conducted at Charles River’s Mattawan site provided preliminary proof-of-concept data that demonstrated the promise of this approach.
The collaboration aims to improve sensitivity, accuracy, and consistency across laboratories, ultimately enhancing public health by more reliably and effectively assessing the abuse potential of new drugs.
About Charles River
Charles River provides essential products and services to help pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, government agencies and leading academic institutions around the globe accelerate their research and drug development efforts. Our dedicated employees are focused on providing clients with exactly what they need to improve and expedite the discovery, early-stage development and safe manufacture of new therapies for the patients who need them. To learn more about our unique portfolio and breadth of services, visit www.criver.com .

title: Lilly breaks ground in Richmond to expand American manufacturing of next-generation cancer medicines, advancing its build-out of 10 new U.S. sites since 2020
source: Eli Lilly and Company - Official RSS
query: https://investor.lilly.com/rss.xml
content_text:
Lilly breaks ground in Richmond to expand American manufacturing of next-generation cancer medicines, advancing its build-out of 10 new U.S. sites since 2020
October 22, 2026
PDF Version 
First Lilly site to produce both active pharmaceutical ingredients and finished medicines in a fully integrated facility 
Site will create 650 high-wage jobs 
INDIANAPOLIS , Oct. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Eli Lilly and Company (NYSE: LLY) broke ground today on a new $5 billion manufacturing facility just west of Richmond, Virginia , in Goochland County , one of 10 new U.S . manufacturing sites announced since 2020 and one of five among them that will produce active pharmaceutical ingredients (API). As part of the company's more than $50 billion push to expand medicine production in the U.S ., the Richmond site will be Lilly 's first to produce both API and finished medicines in a fully integrated facility, with dedicated API capacity for bioconjugate and large-molecule medicines.
The facility will produce antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), targeted cancer treatments designed to combine the precision of antibodies with potent cytotoxic medicines to attack diseased cells directly while limiting exposure to healthy tissue. ADCs are also being explored for autoimmune diseases and other conditions.
David A. Ricks , Lilly Chair and CEO: "We are developing a new generation of medicines designed to target cancer cells with greater precision, yielding more powerful treatments with potentially fewer side effects. This $5 billion investment means we can make them right here in America. Lilly Richmond will help make sure this innovative science can reach the people who need it."
Building a talent pipeline in Richmond 
Making advanced medicines in the U.S . requires a highly skilled workforce. Lilly is building that workforce in Virginia , offering long-term careers where people can grow close to home. Lilly has committed $40 million to support the Virginia Center for Advanced Pharmaceutical Manufacturing , a statewide network of industry, government, and higher education partners that will prepare Virginians for those careers. The network will include a pilot-scale, hands-on training center in Goochland County , with a targeted opening in 2028.
Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger : " Lilly 's investment is a powerful vote of confidence in Virginia , our people, and our ability to compete for the industries and good jobs that will shape our future. Today's groundbreaking marks an exciting milestone in this partnership, and we are proud that Virginia will play an important, durable role in Lilly 's continued global growth and innovation."
Lilly is currently hiring in Richmond and expects the new facility to create 650 high-wage jobs like engineers, scientists, operations personnel, and lab technicians – along with approximately 1,800 construction jobs as the site is built and brought online. Visit the Lilly Richmond career page for open positions or join Lilly 's talent community for future opportunities.
Jonathan Christy , Chairman of the Goochland County Board of Supervisors : " Lilly 's groundbreaking marks a significant investment in Goochland County and an exciting step forward for our community. We proudly welcome Lilly and the opportunities this project will create for quality jobs, economic growth, and lifesaving innovation."
By pairing a highly skilled workforce with advanced technologies and specialized manufacturing, the Richmond site will help support a reliable supply of safe, high-quality medicines. It will use state-of-the-art technologies, including machine learning, AI, digitally integrated systems and advanced data analytics, to drive right-first-time execution, with digital automation embedded throughout the site to streamline operations.
The Richmond facility will be built and operated to the highest standards for safety, quality and environmental stewardship, and Lilly is committed to being a good neighbor in Goochland County and a trusted partner across Virginia . The site is targeting a Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) Gold certification, demonstrating Lilly 's focus on sustainable performance as it expands advanced manufacturing in the U.S .
Lilly has announced 10 U.S. sites since 2020:
Five will produce API: 
Richmond, Virginia ; Huntsville, Alabama ; Houston, Texas ; and two sites in Lebanon, Indiana – Lebanon API and Lilly Medicine Foundry, which will also focus on new production methods and making medicines for clinical trials
Four will make injectable medicines and manufacture devices: 
Research Triangle Park and Concord, North Carolina ; Kenosha, Wisconsin ; and Lehigh Valley, Pennsylvania 
One will make genetic medicines in Lebanon, Indiana ; Lebanon Advanced Therapies
Additional quotes for media use 
Ambassador Jamieson Greer , U.S . Trade Representative: " President Trump's America First Trade Policy is accelerating our nation's reindustrialization, incentivizing companies to proudly build, invest, and expand their operations domestically. Lilly 's new Richmond facility will ensure that life-saving medicines are manufactured on American soil. Today's groundbreaking stands as a powerful testament that there is no substitute for the resilience of the American economy and the skill of the American worker."
About Lilly 
Lilly is a medicine company turning science into healing to make life better for people around the world. We've been pioneering life-changing discoveries for 150 years, and today our medicines help tens of millions of people across the globe. Harnessing the power of biotechnology, chemistry and genetic medicine, our scientists are urgently advancing new discoveries to solve some of the world's most significant health challenges: redefining diabetes care; treating obesity and curtailing its most devastating long-term effects; advancing the fight against Alzheimer's disease; providing solutions to some of the most debilitating immune system disorders; and transforming the most difficult-to-treat cancers into manageable diseases. With each step toward a healthier world, we're motivated by one thing: making life better for millions more people. That includes delivering innovative clinical trials that reflect the diversity of our world and working to ensure our medicines are accessible and affordable. To learn more, visit Lilly.com and Lilly.com/news , or follow us on Facebook , Instagram , and LinkedIn . C-LLY

October 22, 2026
JFE Steel Corporation
Mitsubishi Gas Chemical Company, Inc.
Mitsubishi Chemical Corporation
JFE Steel, Mitsubishi Gas Chemical, and Mitsubishi Chemical Commence Demonstration Project to
Develop a Carbon Recycling Supply Chain at Mizushima Complex
— Demonstration ranges from utilizing steelmaking process by-product gas to producing methanol and
propylene —
JFE Steel Corporation (Headquarters: Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo; President: Masayuki Hirose, hereinafter
referred to as "JFE Steel"), Mitsubishi Gas Chemical Company, Inc. (Headquarters: Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo;
President: Yoshinori Isahaya, hereinafter referred to as "Mitsubishi Gas Chemical"), and Mitsubishi
Chemical Corporation (Headquarters: Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo; President: Manabu Chikumoto, hereinafter
referred to as "Mitsubishi Chemical")—collectively referred to as "the Three Companies"—have
commenced a supply chain demonstration project (hereinafter referred to as "the Demonstration Project")
at the Mizushima Complex (Kurashiki City, Okayama Prefecture) in September 2026. This Demonstration
Project is being conducted based on the demonstration plan announced by the Three Companies in March
2025, aimed at achieving a carbon-recycling society.
JFE Steel has commenced the supply of by-product gas generated from its steelmaking processes for the
Demonstration Project. Mitsubishi Gas Chemical has begun producing methanol using this by-product gas
at its newly constructed Carbopath™*1 demonstration plant within its Mizushima Plant. Furthermore,
Mitsubishi Chemical has begun producing propylene using this methanol as raw material at its existing
demonstration facility (utilizing the DTP®*2 process).
＜Roles of the three companies and material flow in the Demonstration Project＞
The Three Companies will continue the Demonstration Project, evaluate its economic viability, and
identify challenges and pathways toward commercialization. Furthermore, the Three Companies will
explore broader opportunities for collaboration with other businesses within the Mizushima Complex.
＜A concept for carbon recycling through cross-industry collaboration in the Mizushima Complex＞
*1, Carbopath™ is a carbon recycling platform utilizing methanol, promoted by Mitsubishi Gas Chemical.
*2, DTP®: Dominant Technology for Propylene production
DTP® is a registered trademark of JGC Corporation.

Amkor Technology and NVIDIA Advance Strategic Partnership for AI Infrastructure
New $1.3 billion agreement supports further expansion in South Korea , building on the companies’ recent Arizona collaboration 
TEMPE, Ariz. --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 21, 2026--
Amkor Technology, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMKR), a leading provider of outsourced semiconductor packaging and test services, today announced additional investments in South Korea for capacity expansion initiatives with NVIDIA. With this latest commitment, Amkor’s multi-year agreements with NVIDIA in Arizona and South Korea total $3 billion . The initiatives support growing demand for next-generation AI and accelerated computing platforms.
Advanced packaging technologies are essential to enabling the performance, power efficiency and integration required for next-generation computing systems. The prepayments align Amkor's manufacturing capacity with NVIDIA’s long-term growth plans and support increasing demand for advanced packaging solutions.
“Our partnership with NVIDIA underscores the critical role advanced packaging plays in enabling next-generation AI platforms,” said Kevin Engel , president and chief executive officer of Amkor Technology . “These investments build on our global manufacturing footprint and strengthen our ability to support customers through our operations in both the United States and South Korea.”
“Growing demand for accelerated computing is increasing the need for advanced packaging capacity,” said Debora Shoquist , executive vice president, operations of NVIDIA. “Our work with Amkor helps us scale production of current and next-generation platforms while strengthening the resilience of our global supply chain.”
This collaboration further strengthens Amkor’s role as a strategic manufacturing partner for NVIDIA and reinforces the companies’ shared commitment to supporting the continued expansion of AI infrastructure.
Amkor will also exhibit at NVIDIA GTC Washington, D.C. from Nov. 30 - Dec. 3 , where the company will showcase its advanced packaging and test capabilities and engage with customers, policymakers and industry leaders.
About Amkor Technology, Inc. 
Amkor Technology, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMKR) is the world’s largest U.S. headquartered OSAT and is a global leader in outsourced semiconductor packaging and test services. With a strong track record of innovation, a broad and diverse geographic footprint and solid partnerships with lead customers, Amkor delivers high-quality solutions that enable the world’s leading semiconductor and electronics companies to bring advanced technologies to market. The company’s comprehensive portfolio includes advanced packaging, wafer-level processing, and system-in-package solutions targeting applications for smartphones, data centers, artificial intelligence, automobiles and wearables. For more information visit amkor.com .

title: Ouster Sensors Play Key Role in Forterra's Lancer Completing 1,426 Missions and 88 Casualty Evacuation Operations in Ukraine

Ouster Sensors Play Key Role in Forterra's Lancer Completing 1,426 Missions and 88 Casualty Evacuation Operations in Ukraine
October 21, 2026
PDF Version 
Expanding a multi-year strategic partnership to enhance soldier safety while increasing force projection, Forterra plans to further advance its AutoDrive platform with Ouster REV8 native color lidar for next-gen defense vehicles 
SAN FRANCISCO --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 21, 2026-- Ouster, Inc. (Nasdaq: OUST), a leader in sensing and perception for Physical AI, and Forterra , the leader in autonomous mission systems for military operations in contested environments, today announced that Forterra's Lancer autonomous ground vehicles have completed 1,426 missions and 88 casualty evacuation operations in Ukraine including Ouster Rev7 OS1 digital lidar at the core of their sensor fusion perception stack. Forterra built and delivered 105 Lancers in under six months, and across more than 7,300 miles they have run routes that would otherwise have put a crew inside the vehicle.
This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261021344872/en/ 
Forterra's Lancer keeps crews out of harm's way, this one lost on a mission in Ukraine with no one aboard.
The Lancers arrived in Ukraine in October 2025 . Built on the Polaris RANGER XP 1500 and modified in theater with Starlink for resilient communications, each vehicle carries up to 750 kilograms of critical equipment to the war fighters. Lancers are operating in high danger zones where persistent drone surveillance makes crewed vehicles high value targets and creates unnecessary risk for personnel. Instead, uncrewed Lancer systems deliver essential supplies and evacuate wounded soldiers without undue risk to additional personnel.
“Forterra exists to take people out of harm’s way, and in Ukraine , Lancer is doing that every day under constant drone surveillance,” said Forterra CEO Josh Araujo . “As we advance AutoDrive toward higher levels of autonomy, Ouster sensors give us the perception foundation required by the next generation of vehicles.”
To date, Forterra has integrated AutoDrive across more than 50 vehicle platforms deployed in over ten countries. This includes the Squad Multipurpose Equipment Transport (SMET) program and the Marine Corps ROGUE Fires platform, which recently entered Block 2 production, making it the most widely deployed autonomous driving system in the defense industry and the first system fielded by the U.S . military to enable autonomous maneuver of ground vehicles.
Forterra’s AutoDrive capability is built upon Forterra’s 24 years of operational experience and over $500 million invested in engineering development and operations. Throughout a multi-year partnership, Ouster digital lidar has been a key part of Forterra’s AutoDrive platform and its operational success.
Ouster's sensors enable 360-degree situational awareness for autonomous ground vehicles operating in complex and unpredictable environments. Each Ouster OS1 sensor covers ground that would otherwise require several narrow field-of-view sensors, which means fewer units for Forterra to integrate, power, and maintain on every vehicle. Additionally, lidar ranges are independent of ambient light, and dual returns report both an obscurant and the surface behind it, so perception holds in fog, dust, rain, and darkness.
"Forterra operates autonomous ground vehicles in some of the most challenging environments on the planet, where reliable perception and safety are critical to the vehicle operators and soldiers," said Angus Pacala , co-founder and CEO of Ouster. "Ouster's technology gives these vehicles a detailed, real-time understanding of their surroundings, helping them navigate complex terrain and operate with greater confidence when GPS, road markings and ideal conditions cannot be relied upon."
Next- Gen Sensing , Built to Automotive Standards 
Ouster's next-generation native color digital lidar, Rev8, is designed for ASIL-B functional safety to ISO 26262, cybersecurity to ISO 21434, and support for automotive ethernet, all requirements that unmanned ground vehicle programs increasingly demand.
Off-road work causes constant vibration and shock and subjects lidar sensors to temperatures that swing from arctic cold to desert heat. Rev8 is the most rugged lidar family Ouster has built yet, qualified from -40 °C to +85 °C and ingress-protected against dust and water, allowing sensing in the harshest conditions. Rev8 also captures color in the same silicon as the 3D data, giving perception software a second channel alongside range for classifying what is in the scene.
About Ouster 
Ouster (Nasdaq: OUST) is a leader in sensing and perception for Physical AI across industrial, robotics, automotive, and smart infrastructure. With a unified platform of high-performance digital lidar, cameras, AI compute, sensor fusion and perception software, and AI models, Ouster delivers solutions that improve quality of life in the physical world. Headquartered in San Francisco, CA , Ouster has a global presence serving thousands of customers with offices in the Americas , Europe , and Asia-Pacific . For more information about our products, visit www.ouster.com , contact our sales team , or connect with us on X or LinkedIn .
About Forterra 
Forterra is the autonomy backbone for distributed, mission-aware, resilient military operations in contested environments. Building the foundational autonomy platforms that coordinates weapons, sensors, and users through distributed mobility, compute, and communications, anywhere, under fire, without risking human life, Forterra empowers its customers to deploy autonomy as a force multiplier, extending reach, readiness survivability and effectiveness across the battlespace and industrial applications. Forterra is headquartered in Clarksburg, Md., with offices in Arlington, Va., Winter Park, Fl., Ketchum, Id. and Palo Alto, Ca. To learn more, go to forterra.com .

title: 3M and AWS collaborate to advance optical connectivity innovation
query: https://investors.3m.com/news-events/press-releases/rss
content_text:
3M and AWS collaborate to advance optical connectivity innovation
Oct 21, 2026 • 10:28 AM EDT 
Download as PDF
AWS is investing in 3M's Expanded Beam Optical technology for its data center infrastructure 
SAINT PAUL, Minn. , Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- 3M  (NYSE: MMM) and  Amazon Web Services (AWS) today announced an expanded strategic collaboration. AWS plans to deploy and scale 3M's Expanded Beam Optical (EBO) platform for its data center infrastructure. Together, the two leading American companies will advance co-innovation and investment in optical connectivity and the critical infrastructure needed for next-generation super intelligence (SI), also known as artificial intelligence (AI). 
"AWS's adoption of 3M's EBO platform demonstrates the potential of our optical connectivity technology to meet the performance demands of next-generation data center infrastructure," said Wendy Bauer, Group President of 3M's Transportation and Electronics Business Group. "By combining AWS's infrastructure expertise and scale with 3M's innovation and materials science capabilities, we can accelerate EBO deployment, advance our transformation and strengthen U.S. innovation and investment." 
"Our work with 3M reinforces our commitment to supporting good jobs here in the U.S.," said Jens Gruenkemeir, Vice President of Supply Chain & Procurement at Amazon. "Beyond powering the services people use every day, from online banking and hospital data records to streaming entertainment and retail purchases, our data center investments are unlocking economic opportunities in the communities where we invest and across the supply chain, including the hundreds of jobs being supported by 3M as a result of its collaboration with Amazon."   
The collaboration and related investments are expected to strengthen the U.S. economy by supporting more than 500 jobs directly and indirectly, including the creation of more than 100 new roles through 2027 across Minnesota, Texas and Wisconsin. These planned roles will support customer co-innovation, technology advancement and supply chain development across 3M's optical networking portfolio and help accelerate industrywide adoption through collaboration with partners. 
3M expects to contribute nearly $0.5 billion to the U.S. economy through its optical connectivity business. This investment will accelerate innovation in optical networking and fiber termination, enable commercialization at scale and drive adoption across the data center industry.
The collaboration builds on 3M's announcement earlier this year that it will double production capacity at its Menomonie, Wisconsin, manufacturing facility, and is expected to support U.S. manufacturing partners involved in equipment and production scale-up throughout the supply chain.

query: https://www.tosoh.co.jp/news/release/
content_text:
TOP 
ニュース 
ニュースリリース 
無架橋発泡体用ポリエチレン「ペトロセンCZ11」の開発 ～中央物産との共同開発により、ポリエチレン発泡体の再資源化と耐熱性を両立～ 
NEWS RELEASE
2026年10月21日
東ソー株式会社
広報・IR室
印刷する
2026.10.21
ニュースリリース
無架橋発泡体用ポリエチレン「ペトロセンCZ11」の開発 
～中央物産との共同開発により、ポリエチレン発泡体の再資源化と耐熱性を両立～
東ソーは、株式会社中央物産（以下、中央物産）との共同開発により、無架橋 ※1 でありながら、高い耐熱性を有する発泡体が得られるポリエチレン「ペトロセンCZ11」を開発いたしました。本製品は、国内初の高い耐熱性を保持した無架橋発泡体用ポリエチレンとなります。主に空調保温材などの用途を想定しており、このたび中央物産の空調保温パイプの発泡層向け材料としての採用が決定いたしました。
自動車内装材や空調保温材などの耐熱性が求められる分野では、軽量かつ加工性に優れるポリエチレンと、耐熱性を付与するための架橋剤を加えて製造する架橋ポリエチレン発泡体が広く使用されています。一方で、従来の架橋ポリエチレン発泡体は、三次元網目構造 ※2 により再溶融が難しく、マテリアルリサイクル ※3 が困難であることから、端材の多くが廃棄されていました。
2050年カーボンニュートラルの実現に向け、資源循環の重要性が高まる中、ポリエチレン発泡体の再資源化と耐熱性の両立は、業界全体の課題となっていました。
今回開発した「ペトロセンCZ11」は、当社が長年培ってきたポリマー設計技術により、ポリエチレン単体で高発泡成形性と高い耐熱性を実現したものです。「ペトロセンCZ11」を使用することで、従来品と同等以上の性能を維持しながら、押出成形 ※4 時に架橋剤を使用しない無架橋ポリエチレン発泡体の製造が可能となります。
架橋剤を使用しないことで再溶融・再加工が可能となり、リサイクル後の物性変化も小さいことから、マテリアルリサイクルの実現に貢献します。さらに、架橋に必要な熱加工工程を省略できることから、製造時の環境負荷低減が期待されます。
今回の採用を皮切りに、当社は空調保温材をはじめ、自動車内装材など、耐熱性が求められる発泡製品分野への展開を進めてまいります。さまざまな発泡製品へ展開することで、複合プラスチックを含む発泡体の水平リサイクル ※5 の促進も期待されます。
当社は、長年培ってきた技術と経験を結集し、イノベーション創出に挑戦し続けることで、持続可能な社会の実現に貢献してまいります。
提供元：中央物産 
架橋剤などにより分子間を結合させる処理を行っていないこと
高分子の分子同士が三次元的に結合した構造
廃棄物を新たな製品の原料として再利用するリサイクル方法
加熱溶融した樹脂を金型から連続的に押し出して成形する方法
リサイクル前と後で用途を変えない資源循環の方法

title: GE HealthCare announces five new global collaborations to advance the next generation of theranostics imaging
query: https://investor.gehealthcare.com/rss.xml
content_text:
GE HealthCare announces five new global collaborations to advance the next generation of theranostics imaging
October 20, 2026
PDF Version 
Leading institutions will evaluate StarGuide GX i across quantitative imaging, dynamic imaging and emerging theranostic applications
Clinical experience from more than 1,000 patient studies was established ahead of the European Association of Nuclear Medicine (EANM) 2026 Annual Meeting in Vienna, Austria 
Insights will help guide the future evolution of GE HealthCare's digital SPECT/CT platform and inform the next generation of nuclear medicine imaging
CHICAGO & VIENNA --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 20, 2026--
GE HealthCare (Nasdaq: GEHC) today announced a global clinical evaluation program spanning three continents and five internationally recognized institutions to assess StarGuide™ GX, i its next-generation digital 4D SPECT/CT system. Participating institutions include Hadassah Medical Center in Israel ; Mayo Clinic in the United States ; Oncopole Claudius Regaud – Institut Universitaire du Cancer de Toulouse in France ; Peking University First Hospital in China ; and Rambam Health Care Campus.
Across the program, participating institutions will evaluate image quality, quantitative performance, dynamic imaging and workflow while providing clinical and research feedback to help inform the future evolution of StarGuide GX.
“Nuclear medicine is entering a new era in which imaging is expected to do more than identify disease – it is increasingly being used to quantify biological processes, support treatment decisions and monitor response to therapy,” said Erez Levy , Executive Director, Molecular Imaging, GE HealthCare . “By working across multiple regions and care environments, we aim to generate clinical and research insights that can help inform innovation as imaging, quantitation and workflow needs evolve.”
Expanding quantitative and dynamic imaging capabilities 
StarGuide GX uses dual-sided cadmium zinc telluride (dsCZT) detector technology and is designed to support high-sensitivity, high-resolution imaging, quantitative imaging and dynamic acquisitions. Its detector configuration allows the detectors to move close to the patient during imaging, while its patented dual-collimator detector design is intended to eliminate the need for manual external collimator exchanges and streamline imaging workflows.
Additionally, the system is engineered to support radionuclides across a broad energy range and, in research settings, it may also be evaluated for imaging radionuclides associated with emerging alpha-emitter research, including Actinium-225, focused on the potential to expand theranostic applications. ii 
“The technological innovations introduced by StarGuide GX are particularly exciting for the future of theranostics,” shared Prof. Frederic Courbon, Head of the Imaging Department , Oncopole Claudius Regaud – Institut Universitaire du Cancer de Toulouse. “The system's ergonomic design and flexibility have the potential to significantly improve workflow while supporting precision in quantitative imaging and high-energy radionuclide applications. Our first experience suggests that StarGuide GX represents a meaningful step forward in enabling advanced theranostic practices.”
StarGuide GX also uses NVIDIA RTX™ accelerated computing to support image reconstruction, and includes a Low-Medium Energy collimator that is designed to provide up to 2.67-times system volume sensitivity. iii 
Global collaborations advance nuclear medicine research 
Five new, global clinical collaborations will evaluate the platform across diverse care settings: iv 
Hadassah Medical Center ( Israel ): Evaluate advanced quantitative capabilities following the system’s recent field upgrade.
Mayo Clinic ( United States ): Evaluate advanced quantitative and dynamic imaging applications.
Oncopole Claudius Regaud – Institut Universitaire du Cancer de Toulouse ( France ): Assess StarGuide GX, the department's general-purpose SPECT/CT platform, across routine oncology imaging and clinical research.
Peking University First Hospital ( China ): Explore novel tracer research and preclinical applications.
Rambam Health Care Campus ( Israel ): Evaluate StarGuide GX imaging workflows through extensive clinical use across a broad range of nuclear medicine applications and tracers.
These new collaborations build on GE HealthCare’s work with University Hospital Essen in Germany , which in June 2026 opened a new state-of-the-art Nuclear Medicine Center featuring the world’s first installation of StarGuide GX SPECT/CT.
To date, these diverse healthcare institutions have scanned more than 1,000 patients.
StarGuide GX received CE Mark in November 2025 and is available for sale in select European Union member states. The system is 510(k) pending with the U.S . FDA and is not currently available for sale in the United States .
For more information about GE HealthCare’s molecular imaging portfolio, visit gehealthcare.com or see the system in the company’s booth at the European Association of Nuclear Medicine’s 2026 Annual Meeting, October 17-21 in Vienna, Austria .
About GE HealthCare Technologies Inc. 
GE HealthCare is a leading global healthcare solutions provider of advanced medical technology, pharmaceutical diagnostics, and AI, cloud and software solutions that help clinicians tackle the world’s most complex diseases. Serving patients and providers for 130 years, GE HealthCare is delivering bold innovations designed for the next era of medicine across its Advanced Imaging Solutions, Pharmaceutical Diagnostics and Patient Care Solutions segments to help clinicians deliver more personalized, precise patient care. We are a $20.6 billion business with approximately 54,000 colleagues working to create a world where healthcare has no limits.
GE HealthCare is proud to be among 2026 Fortune World’s Most Admired Companies™. 
Follow us on LinkedIn , Facebook , Instagram , or visit our website for our latest news and perspectives .

title: BASF signs Letter of Intent with Taiwan’s Ministry of Economic Affairs to advance next-generation semiconductor manufacturing
query: https://www.basf.com/global/en/investors/calendar-and-publications/investor-releases
content_text:
BASF signs Letter of Intent with Taiwan’s Ministry of Economic Affairs to advance next-generation semiconductor manufacturing
Establishing new production capacity for semiconductor materials supporting chip technologies below 2 nanometers  
Expanding BASF’s Kuanyin site with a strengthened Innovation Center and advanced quality analysis capabilities  
Strengthening supply chain resilience and enhancing customer support in Taiwan and beyond  
Taipei – October 20, 2026 – BASF today signed a Letter of Intent (LOI) with Taiwan’s Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), underscoring its long-term commitment to supporting the growth of Taiwan’s semiconductor ecosystem. Through this investment, BASF’s Electronic Materials business is expanding its Kuanyin site in Taoyuan with additional production capacity for advanced semiconductor materials, enhanced quality analysis capabilities, and an expanded Innovation Center. The investment is designed to support increasing global demand for leading-edge semiconductor manufacturing technologies, including advanced nodes below 2 nanometers, while strengthening supply chain resilience and customer proximity.
“Taiwan is a global hub for semiconductor innovation and manufacturing, with leading-edge process technologies and a highly integrated industry ecosystem. Setting the strategic base for BASF’s global Electronic Materials operations in Taiwan in 2025 reflected the strategic importance of Taiwan within the global semiconductor ecosystem and reinforced our confidence in the market’s long-term growth potential,” said Gops Pillay, President, Global Operating Division of BASF.
As the semiconductor industry progresses toward process nodes below 2 nanometers, demand for advanced, high-purity specialty chemical formulations continues to rise. Through the expansion of its Kuanyin site, BASF will strengthen its Innovation Center and broaden its technical and analytical capabilities for leading-edge semiconductor technologies supporting the AI era. The investment will deepen collaboration with key industry partners, enabling the joint development of next-generation materials while reinforcing Taiwan’s position as a global semiconductor innovation hub.
The investment will further strengthen BASF’s local manufacturing, quality assurance and technical service capabilities in Taiwan, enabling the company to provide customers with a more reliable supply of advanced semiconductor materials, faster technical support, and closer collaboration. At the same time, it will enhance supply chain resilience and reinforce BASF’s role as a trusted long-term partner to the semiconductor industry.
“The signing of this Letter of Intent marks another important milestone in BASF’s long-term commitment to the semiconductor industry,” said Jens Liebermann, Senior Vice President, Global Electronic Materials business and Chairman of BASF Taiwan. “As semiconductor technologies continue to advance, innovation in materials must keep pace with our customers’ evolving needs. By strengthening our local manufacturing, innovation, and technical service capabilities, we are deepening collaboration with our customers and accelerating the development of materials solutions for future technology generations, while further enhancing supply chain resilience.”
As a trusted materials partner to the global semiconductor industry, BASF’s Electronic Materials business has maintained a strong presence in Taiwan for more than two decades. The business provides high-performance process chemicals and customized formulation solutions for the advanced semiconductor and display industry as well as specialized metal systems for consumer electronics applications. 
 
About BASF’s Dispersions & Resins division  
The Dispersions & Resins division of BASF develops, produces and markets a range of high-quality polymer dispersions, resins, additives and electronic materials worldwide. These raw materials are used in formulations for several industries, including coatings, construction, adhesives, printing and packaging, electronics and paper. With its comprehensive product portfolio and extensive knowledge of the industry, the Dispersions & Resins division offers its customers innovative and sustainable solutions and helps them advance their formulations. For further information about the Dispersions & Resins division, please visit  www.dispersions-resins.basf.com 
 
About BASF 
At BASF, we create chemistry for a sustainable future. Our ambition: We want to be the preferred chemical company to enable our customers’ green transformation. We combine economic success with environmental protection and social responsibility. Around 95,000 employees in the BASF Group contribute to the success of our customers in nearly all sectors and almost every country in the world. Our portfolio comprises, as core businesses, the segments Chemicals, Materials, Industrial Solutions, and Nutrition & Care; our standalone businesses are bundled in the segments Surface Technologies and Agricultural Solutions. BASF generated sales of around €60 billion in 2025. BASF shares are traded on the stock exchange in Frankfurt (BAS) and as American Depositary Receipts (BASFY) in the United States. title: 10/20/2026 High Performance Polymers Evonik launches new, stiffer VESTAKEEP® PEEK dental grades, widening the possibilities of dental applications for PEEK-based materials Evonik has introduced two new PEEK grades designed for use in long-term dental prosthetics.
query: https://www.evonik.com/en/media.html
content_text:
10/20/2026
Evonik launches new, stiffer VESTAKEEP® PEEK dental grades, widening the possibilities of dental applications for PEEK-based materials
Evonik has introduced two new PEEK grades designed for use in long-term dental prosthetics. 
New grades feature greater rigidity and excellent polishability, suitable for fixed and removable prosthetic restorations
Absorption of masticatory forces remains the same for superior patient comfort
Designed for 100% compatibility with standard CAD/CAM workflows
Darmstadt, Germany. Evonik has introduced two new PEEK grades designed for use in long-term dental prosthetics. One of the latest developments from its High Performance Polymers business line, VESTAKEEP® DC4760 and VESTAKEEP® DC4780 feature remarkable bone-like stiffness, durability, high biocompatibility and excellent processability in dental labs, enlarging the portfolio of metal-free and lightweight dental materials
“The launch of these two new VESTAKEEP® grades are in line with Evonik’s strategy to serve a growing consumer interest in a greater range of metal-free materials for manufacturing dental bridges or long-lasting fixed and removable prosthetic restorations,” said Marc Knebel, head of the PEEK medical applications team at Evonik’s High Performance Polymers business line. “Thanks to their natural color, neutral taste and lightweight properties, PEEK-based dental frameworks are greatly valued by patients looking for an alternative to metal-alloy based materials.”
The new dental grades join an existing range of VESTAKEEP® products for dental applications and are based on a patented formulation that brings high structural rigidity. This property was further defined in an independent study recently published in “Dental Materials.” Conducted by leading members of Charité University Medicine in Berlin and the Einstein Center Digital Future research group, the analysis found VESTAKEEP® DC4760 and VESTAKEEP® DC4780 to have a level of stiffness high enough for use in implant-supported dentures and other high-load dental prosthetics.
“The key feature of these new VESTAKEEP® dental grades is their combination of higher stiffness and their ability to maintain the flexural strength expected for long-term dental prostheses. Thanks to this, VESTAKEEP® can now be used for a broader range of high quality, aesthetic & long-lasting multi-unit frameworks that provide elevated patient comfort” said Jacques-Antoine Raust, Business Manager in Evonik’s Medical Systems team.
Both VESTAKEEP® DC4760 and VESTAKEEP® DC4780 feature excellent polishability for improved machining with established dental laboratory equipment. This allows the benefit of a smooth and immediate integration into daily operations for dental lab technicians and dentists. Evonik’s new PEEK grades continue to retain previous dental grades’ well-established, excellent wear and plaque accumulation resistance for durable hygiene and aesthetics. Additionally, the increased stiffness of both products leads to better modulus matching between acrylic veneers and PEEK, which can increase the longevity of dentures
VESTAKEEP® DC4760 (dentin colored PEEK) and VESTAKEEP® DC4780 (gingiva colored PEEK) are available as rods or CAD/CAM discs with full biocompatibility for long-term mucosal contact. Along with the product, Evonik will provide customers regulatory support for their own MDR registration.
Evonik’s experts will also present their latest solutions for medical applications from November 16 to 19 at the COMPAMED trade show, Hall 8B, Booth D04, in Düsseldorf, Germany.
To learn more about Evonik’s solutions on display at COMPAMED, please visit: https://www.evonik.com/en/events/2026/compamed.html 
For more information on Evonik’s VESTAKEEP® range of products for medical applications, please visit: https://www.evonik.com/en/markets/market_1345345/vestakeep-peek-for-medical-devices.html 
Evonik: Leading beyond chemistry
Evonik goes beyond the boundaries of chemistry with its combination of innovative strength and leading technological expertise. The global chemical company, headquartered in Essen, Germany, is active in more than 100 countries and generated sales of €14.1 billion and earnings (adjusted EBITDA) of €1.9 billion in 2025. The common motivation of the approximately 31,000 employees: to provide customers with a decisive competitive advantage with tailor-made products and solutions as a superforce for industry, thereby improving people's lives. In all markets. Every day.
About Advanced Technologies
The Advanced Technologies segment includes Evonik’s market-leading businesses that leverage technological expertise and process know-how. These businesses feature high-performance polymers and crosslinking agents, hydrogen peroxide and silica, as well as feed ingredients. In 2025, the segment generated sales of €5.9 billion with around 9,200 employees.

title: 3M announces collaboration with GSEO to advance Expanded Beam Optical manufacturing and development

content_text:
3M announces collaboration with GSEO to advance Expanded Beam Optical manufacturing and development
Oct 19, 2026 • 5:31 PM EDT 
Download as PDF
ST. PAUL, Minn. , Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- 3M (NYSE: MMM) today announced a collaboration with Genius Electronic Optical Co., Ltd.  (GSEO, Taiwan: 3406), an optical technology company, to advance technology development and manufacturing for 3M's Expanded Beam Optical (EBO) solutions. In support of these efforts, 3M expects to make a strategic investment to acquire approximately 4.7% of GSEO's common shares as part of the company's private placement of newly issued shares, subject to customary closing conditions.
The collaboration brings together 3M's EBO technology leadership, optical interconnect expertise, materials science, manufacturing scale and customer relationships with GSEO's precision optics manufacturing capabilities and production scale. Together, the companies aim to support EBO commercialization and long-term capacity expansion to meet growing demand from hyperscale data centers and other advanced connectivity applications.
"3M is investing in capabilities and partnerships that can accelerate innovation for our customers," said William Brown, 3M Chairman and CEO. "By selecting GSEO as a manufacturing partner and investing in the company, we are strengthening the path to scale next-generation optical connectivity solutions for high-performance data center infrastructure."
GSEO's existing precision optics manufacturing capabilities and technical development experience are expected to support manufacturing readiness for 3M's EBO ferrules, co-packaged optics solutions and related optical interconnect applications. The collaboration is part of 3M's broader EBO ecosystem strategy, which includes continued work with customers and partners across the optical interconnect market.
"GSEO is pleased to expand its relationship with 3M as we work together to advance optical interconnect solutions for next-generation data center infrastructure," said Micro Kuo, GSEO CEO and President. "This collaboration brings together complementary technology and manufacturing strengths to support continued innovation and help meet the performance demands of high-growth connectivity markets."
3M expects the strategic investment to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to customary closing conditions.

title: GE HealthCare expands general imaging ultrasound portfolio with LOGIQ Focus, elevating everyday ultrasound performance
query: https://investor.gehealthcare.com/rss.xml
content_text:
GE HealthCare expands general imaging ultrasound portfolio with LOGIQ Focus, elevating everyday ultrasound performance
October 19, 2026
PDF Version 
LOGIQ Focus is powered by cSound Architecture and combined with comprehensive digital tools to deliver advanced image quality and premium-level performance for confident, everyday full-body ultrasound
CHICAGO --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 19, 2026--
GE HealthCare today announced LOGIQ™ Focus, a new addition to its LOGIQ family of general imaging ultrasound systems, designed to bring advanced imaging tools to a broader range of ultrasound exams. LOGIQ Focus is a versatile ultrasound system that pairs high-quality LOGIQ imaging with AI-enabled, automation and productivity tools intended to support greater confidence, consistency and efficiency across routine and more complex care areas.
"As demand for imaging grows, clinicians shouldn't have to choose between image quality and efficiency," said Karley Yoder , Chief Executive Officer, Ultrasound Solutions (USS), Advanced Imaging Solutions, GE HealthCare . "LOGIQ Focus builds on more than 30 years of LOGIQ innovation to deliver both, combining advanced imaging and clinician-centered AI-enabled tools that care teams rely on every day."
LOGIQ Focus is built on cSound™ Architecture with advanced speckle reduction imaging and offers a range of multi-purpose and specialty probes. The ultrasound system is also equipped with a High Definition Ultrasound (HDU) display that aims to provide enhanced clarity and crisp images, helping clinicians visualize subtle structures and fine tissue differences, and advanced flow visualization tools designed to provide users with the flexibility to view flow with more clarity.
A third-party study showed that 90 percent of participants rated the overall image quality of LOGIQ Focus as excellent, and the ultrasound system was 26 percent faster than the predicate system. i,ii The Vscan Air™ CL probe is compatible with the LOGIQ Focus, giving clinicians added flexibility with wireless, cable-free scanning.
LOGIQ Focus supports a range of imaging tools and digital solutions designed to streamline workflow, minimize re-work and interruptions while keeping clinicians in control and supporting more informed clinical decisions:
AI-enabled and automation   tools designed to reduce manual steps, save time and improve consistency across users, including Auto Preset Assistant that automatically detects the anatomy being scanned and activates the corresponding preset. Clinicians can save up to five clicks during each exam with this tool and spend up to 25 percent less time on AI-automated tasks. iii,iv 
Productivity tools designed to help standardize exams, produce reproducible images, and streamline reporting like AutoEF, which automatically measures ejection fraction—a widely used measurement to assess heart function—and Scan Assistant, which guides users through exam protocols.
Verisound digital tools include Verisound Collab v for virtual collaboration, allowing clinicians to easily communicate within their network.
Comprehensive liver solutions to improve liver assessments, including Ultrasound-Guided Fat Fraction , enabling more consistent assessment of liver fat burden and 2D shear wave elastography, supporting the evaluation of tissue stiffness changes associated with fibrosis.
"We designed LOGIQ Focus around what clinicians told us they need most: confidence on the first pass, a workflow that keeps pace, and a system they can count on to be there when they need it," said Michael Greene , General Manager, General Imaging, Primary Care and Automated Breast Ultrasound , USS, GE HealthCare . "LOGIQ Focus includes features so care teams spend less time on the system and more time with the patient, on a connected platform designed to evolve with their needs."
LOGIQ Focus is designed to perform consistently over time, simplify clinical operations, and remain serviceable and secure. The system incorporates SonoDefense, a multilayer cybersecurity approach for GE HealthCare ultrasound devices, which uses a defense-in-depth strategy with security controls deployed in multiple independent layers to help keep systems functional and protect patient data.
LOGIQ Focus is part of a wave of innovation across GE HealthCare's portfolio supported by more than $5 billion in innovation investment since 2023. LOGIQ Focus is one of the several new products expected to contribute 1 to 2 percent of revenue growth for the company.
LOGIQ Focus is 510(k) cleared and CE Marked. These ultrasound systems are available in other markets where regulatory approval has been granted. For more information, visit: https://www.gehealthcare.com/en/products/ultrasound/logiq/logiq-focus .

Evonik is expanding its ruminant portfolio with the launch of Lypron®, a rumen-protected lysine solution designed to deliver targeted amino acid nutrition and support efficient, balanced feeding strategies in modern livestock production.
query: https://www.evonik.com/en/media.html
content_text:
Evonik launches Lypron® to complete its amino acid balancing concept for ruminants 
Delivers targeted lysine for precise amino acid balancing 
High and reliable metabolizable lysine that supports consistent performance in ruminants 
Non-GMO solution that enhances nitrogen efficiency for more sustainable production
Essen, Germany. Evonik is expanding its ruminant portfolio with the launch of Lypron®, a rumen-protected lysine solution designed to deliver targeted amino acid nutrition and support efficient, balanced feeding strategies in modern livestock production.
Developed in collaboration with Sipena, a French specialist in coating technologies that will exclusively manufacture the product for Evonik, Lypron® delivers metabolizable lysine precisely where it is needed. This ensures optimal utilisation of nutrients to support high performance in ruminants.
Lysine is one of the most limiting amino acids in ruminant nutrition and plays a critical role in performance. With its high and reliable metabolizable lysine content, Lypron® enables producers to balance diets for amino acids more precisely, boosting profitability by reducing the need for expensive protein sources.
“With Lypron®, we are expanding our ruminant solutions to complement our established products like Mepron®,” said Marion Hax, Head of the Specialty Nutrition Product Line at Evonik Animal Nutrition. “Completing our amino acid balancing concept allows us to support customers in achieving both higher performance and more sustainable feeding strategies.”
By improving the dietary amino acid balance, Lypron® supports the use of low protein diets, optimizing nitrogen utilization. This can contribute to lower nitrogen excretion, helping farms reduce environmental impact while maintaining productivity.
“Lypron® helps nutritionists optimize amino acid supply, increase productivity, and reduce reliance on excess dietary protein, which is increasingly important both economically and environmentally,” said Claudia Parys, Global Head of the Ruminant Business at Evonik Animal Nutrition.
Lypron® enables more flexible feeding strategies, including low protein and soy reduced diets. As a non-GMO solution, it supports market requirements in regions where GMO free production is essential, while maintaining high performance standards.

title: AGC Biologics to Support Development and Manufacturing of Flen Health’s Next-Generation Enzyme Therapy for Diabetic Foot Ulcers
source: Asahi Glass - News releases (newsroom JSON list)
query: https://www.agc.com/en/news/detail/news_all.json
content_text:
AGC Biologics to Support Development and Manufacturing of Flen Health’s Next-Generation Enzyme Therapy for Diabetic Foot Ulcers
－Providing process development and GMP manufacturing services for recombinant enzymes－
AGC Biologics, a global biopharmaceutical contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) within the AGC Group, has entered into an agreement with Belgian biopharmaceutical company Flen Health to provide process development and GMP* manufacturing services for recombinant enzymes for use in a next-generation therapy for diabetic foot ulcers.
At its Heidelberg site in Germany, AGC Biologics will carry out process development and manufacturing activities for lactoperoxidase and glucose oxidase. This work will support Flen Health's planned Investigational New Drug (IND) application and Phase II clinical trial in the United States.
Advancing a Next-Generation Enzyme Therapy for Diabetic Foot Ulcers 
In 2024, approximately 589 million adults worldwide, or about one in nine, were living with diabetes. Its prevalence is projected to rise further. 
Diabetic foot ulcers are chronic wounds that develop on the feet of people with diabetes. More than one in five people with diabetes are estimated to be at risk of developing a diabetic foot ulcer during their lifetime. Effective treatment options remain limited, creating a strong need for new therapeutic approaches. 
To address this unmet medical need, Flen Health is developing a next-generation therapy using recombinant enzymes. The therapy is based on Flaminal ® , Flen Health’s wound treatment gel that combines enzymes and alginate and is marketed primarily in Europe.
Expanding the Collaboration from a Feasibility Program to GMP Manufacturing 
AGC Biologics and Flen Health began a feasibility program in July 2025. At its Heidelberg site, AGC Biologics has since undertaken technology transfer for the manufacturing processes of lactoperoxidase and glucose oxidase. It has also developed cultivation and purification processes and implemented analytical methods. 
Under the new agreement, the collaboration will advance to the next stage, covering process development, scale-up and GMP manufacturing. AGC Biologics plans to manufacture the recombinant enzymes at the 100-liter and 1,000-liter scales.
AGC Biologics Heidelberg Site 
Development Activities at the Heidelberg Site 
Under its medium-term management plan, AGC plus-2026 , the AGC Group has defined three social values that it aims to create through its products and technologies. One of these values is “Well-being.” The Group aims to contribute to safe, secure and healthy living by ensuring the stable provision of products and services essential to daily life and healthcare.
Through its Life Science business, the AGC Group provides CDMO services for biopharmaceuticals and a wide range of other modalities. By supporting customers from early-stage development through commercial production, the Group aims to contribute to the health of people worldwide.
〈Notes〉 
* 
GMP: Good Manufacturing Practice. GMP refers to standards designed to ensure pharmaceutical quality and safety by controlling the entire process from the receipt of raw materials through manufacturing and shipment. 
About Flen Health 
Flen Health is a biopharmaceutical company dedicated to developing innovative therapies for unmet needs in wound care. Founded in 2000 and headquartered in Kontich, Belgium, the company has more than 25 years of experience delivering trusted wound and skin healing solutions across Europe and in more than 40 countries worldwide. Flen Health is now leveraging this expertise to bring its novel therapeutics to the U.S. market. For more information, visit www.flenhealth.com . 
About the AGC Group 
AGC Inc. is a global materials company operating across a wide range of products and industries. Founded in 1907 with flat glass production as its original business, AGC has expanded its operations in line with changing societal needs, providing materials and solutions based on its core material and production technologies. Today, the AGC Group operates in more than 30 countries and regions, with businesses spanning glass, electronics, chemicals, life science, and ceramics. Guided by its purpose, “AGC, an everyday essential part of our world,” the Group provides value to society through the pursuit of innovation.

title: GE HealthCare's MINItrace™ Magni achieves CE Mark; Copper-64 expands PETtrace™ Solid Target Platform beyond Gallium-68
query: https://investor.gehealthcare.com/rss.xml
content_text:
GE HealthCare's MINItrace™ Magni achieves CE Mark; Copper-64 expands PETtrace™ Solid Target Platform beyond Gallium-68
October 15, 2026
PDF Version 
MINItrace Magni combines a compact, self-shielded design with automated operation to help healthcare providers establish and expand local production of radioisotopes used in PET tracers
Copper-64 expands the PETtrace Solid Target Platform beyond Gallium-68, supporting research in both copper-based imaging agents and the potential Copper-64/Copper-67 theranostic pair
CHICAGO --(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 15, 2026--
GE HealthCare (Nasdaq: GEHC) today announced that its MINItrace Magni cyclotron has achieved CE Mark and that its PETtrace Solid Target Platform is expanding beyond Gallium-68 with support for Copper-64 (⁶⁴Cu) production. Together, the developments reflect the company’s focus on helping institutions build the production capabilities behind their molecular imaging programs—from establishing local PET radioisotope production to supporting research into emerging radiopharmaceuticals.
For healthcare providers building or expanding a positron emission tomography (PET) program, access to tracers is an important consideration. Many PET radioisotopes have short half-lives, making proximity between production and use a factor in supply planning. Cyclotrons produce these radioisotopes, which can then be incorporated into radiotracers used in PET imaging. Local production can give providers greater control over supply and scheduling while reducing reliance on external production and transportation.
“The molecular imaging landscape is being reshaped by the expansion of theranostics, the introduction of new PET tracers, and demand across oncology, neurology and cardiology,” said Erez Levy , Vice President of Molecular Imaging at GE HealthCare . “As tracer portfolios broaden, healthcare providers need reliable access to radioisotopes and the flexibility to respond to changing clinical needs. That calls for a longer-term view of radiopharmaceutical production—one that supports established services while allowing institutions to prepare for new clinical and research applications.”
MINItrace™ Magni: supporting local production through compact design and automation
For institutions seeking to establish or expand in-house production, MINItrace Magni brings together a compact, self-shielded design and simplified operation. The cyclotron is designed to produce Fluorine-18 (¹⁸F), Carbon-11 (¹¹C), Oxygen-15 (¹⁵O) and Nitrogen-13 (¹³N) for PET tracers. Its CE Mark represents an important milestone for a system designed around the needs of in-house PET radioisotope production.
Aiming to help extend day-to-day operations, MINItrace Magni features an intuitive user interface and a three-click workflow designed to streamline routine production steps. Automated features are intended to simplify setup and operation, including auto-tuning, which prepares the cyclotron and targets, tunes the beam and manages target irradiation.
Producing the radioisotope is only one part of preparing a PET tracer. When used with GE HealthCare’s TRACERcenter Solutions, MINItrace Magni is designed to support a broader PET radiopharmacy workflow based on an institution’s clinical, operational and tracer-production needs. This approach supports providers in developing tailored local radiopharmaceutical capabilities aligned to the specific requirements of their molecular imaging programs, while considering both current and future departmental needs to create a sustainable holistic solution.
Copper-64: broadening the possibilities for PETtrace production
Alongside decisions about where to produce radioisotopes, institutions must consider which radioisotopes their programs will need. For those seeking to broaden their production capabilities, the addition of Copper-64 extends the PETtrace Solid Target Platform beyond the production of Gallium-68, for which it was introduced in 2022, and Zirconium-89, which was made available in early 2026. The capability broadens the range of isotopes that may be produced using PETtrace cyclotron infrastructure, allowing customers to build on the platform as their isotope needs evolve.
Copper-64’s relevance includes exploring its potential role in connecting imaging with investigational therapeutic applications. It enables PET imaging and is also being studied with investigational Copper-67 agents as a potential diagnostic and therapeutic pair. This research sits within the broader field of theranostics, which connects molecular imaging with targeted radionuclide therapy. Clinical research is evaluating Copper-64-labeled compounds in areas including prostate cancer and HER2-positive breast cancer.
Supporting that work involves more than the cyclotron alone. GE HealthCare’s capabilities in cyclotrons, targetry, radiochemistry synthesis, molecular imaging and services are intended to help institutions establish solid-target production as part of a broader radiopharmacy workflow.
“A molecular imaging program needs a plan for the tracers it uses today and the ones it may want to explore tomorrow,” said Nicolas Durand-Schaefer , General Manager, Molecular Imaging, International, GE HealthCare . “MINItrace Magni’s CE Mark is an important milestone for a compact, versatile cyclotron designed to support local radioisotope production and enable healthcare providers to build radiopharmacy capabilities without the need for large-scale production infrastructure. Adding Copper-64 to PETtrace broadens the platform’s capabilities to support copper-based imaging and theranostics research. Our focus is on helping institutions connect the practical demands of running a radiopharmacy with their longer-term clinical and research ambitions.”
Both developments build on more than 40 years of GE HealthCare experience in cyclotron and PET radiopharmacy technologies, extending the company’s focus on the production capabilities and workflows that support molecular imaging.
For more information about GE HealthCare’s PET radiopharmacy solutions, visit gehealthcare.com or meet with company representatives in the GE HealthCare booth at the European Association of Nuclear Medicine’s 2026 Annual Meeting, October 17-21 in Vienna, Austria .
About GE HealthCare Technologies Inc.
GE HealthCare is a leading global healthcare solutions provider of advanced medical technology, pharmaceutical diagnostics, and AI, cloud and software solutions that help clinicians tackle the world’s most complex diseases. Serving patients and providers for 130 years, GE HealthCare is delivering bold innovations designed for the next era of medicine across its Advanced Imaging Solutions, Pharmaceutical Diagnostics, and Patient Care Solutions segments to help clinicians deliver more personalized, precise patient care. We are a $20.6 billion business with approximately 54,000 colleagues working to create a world where healthcare has no limits.

title: AGC Uses Generative AI to Turn Manufacturing Expertise into Organizational Knowledge
source: Asahi Glass - News releases (newsroom JSON list)
