Rio Tinto Opens Two Argentine Lithium Projects Backed by $1.4 Billion
Rio Tinto has launched two lithium ventures in Argentina, underpinned by a total commitment of $1.4 billion, as the mining group accelerates its push into battery metals. The Fénix 1B expansion and the Sal de Vida operation, both located in Catamarca province, commenced first production during the second quarter of 2026, ahead of schedule, and are currently increasing output.
Once running at full capacity, the pair will contribute 25,000 tonnes of yearly lithium carbonate equivalent capacity, according to the company. At an inauguration event attended by President Javier Milei and Catamarca Governor Raúl Jalil, Rio Tinto chief executive Simon Trott said the developments draw on almost thirty years of lithium output in the province and the skills of the firm's Argentine employees. He also referenced the company's worldwide ambition of reaching 200,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent annual capacity by 2028.
Project Details
The $530-million Fénix 1B expansion contributes 10,000 tonnes of yearly capacity, raising the site's overall target to about 40,000 tonnes. Fénix started producing in 1997, becoming Argentina's first commercial lithium operation. Rio Tinto is evaluating a further expansion, with an investment decision anticipated in 2028 or 2029.
Sal de Vida, a new lithium carbonate facility situated roughly 20 km northeast of Fénix, is designed for 15,000 tonnes per year. Its initial phase required an investment of $374 million.
Both operations belong to an integrated production hub in the Salar del Hombre Muerto, whose combined resource base stands at approximately 19 million tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent. Running the sites jointly enables infrastructure sharing, efficiency gains and efforts to lower water use. Fénix employs direct lithium extraction, whereas Sal de Vida uses conventional evaporation ponds.
Counting Fénix, Sal de Vida and Olaroz, Rio Tinto's nominal lithium capacity in Argentina totals roughly 100,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent per year. Its wider Argentine holdings include a 66.5% interest in Olaroz and complete ownership of the Rincón project, which extends across Catamarca, Jujuy and Salta provinces.
Market Context
Argentina is projected to generate around 172,700 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent in 2026, a 48% rise over the prior year and over five times the 2018 figure. Between January and August 2026, lithium exports brought in $1.467 billion, up 190.5% compared with the same period twelve months earlier.
Rio Tinto intends to direct close to 70% of its planned $4 billion in Argentine lithium growth capital toward local suppliers. The spending dovetails with Milei's push to draw foreign investment via market-friendly reforms and the Large Investment Incentive Regime, which grants tax, legal and foreign-exchange advantages for 30 years to eligible projects exceeding $200 million in value.
Benchmark Mineral Intelligence projects worldwide lithium demand climbing from 2 million tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent in 2026 to 7 million tonnes by 2050, chiefly on electric vehicle and energy storage growth. Argentina's Mining Secretariat anticipates the country may surpass Chile in lithium output by 2029 and achieve yearly production of 573,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent by 2035.

content_text:
Merck outlines 2027 as ‘another year of investment’ despite recent clinical wins
By
Angus Liu 
Oct 29, 2026 11:23am 
Merck 
Earnings 
Keytruda 
sac-TMT 
Merck ramps up R&D and commercial investments to secure its post-Keytruda future. (Photo by Kena Betancur/Getty Images)
Even as a wave of clinical trial wins bolsters its momentum, Merck & Co. is prioritizing ongoing pipeline and commercial expansions over near-term margin growth, hoping to gird its long-term prospects past Keytruda's loss of exclusivity.
For 2027, “we see it as another year of investment, as we invest behind our expansive pipeline and our new product launches to drive long-term growth,” Merck’s CFO Caroline Litchfield said on the company’s third-quarter earnings call Thursday.
Litchfield made the comment in response to a question about whether Merck has seen enough R&D progress recently that the company may start to turn its attention to earnings growth as it looks beyond 2030.
At least for 2027, Merck expects underlying operating expenses to increase at a mid- to high-single-digit rate, “reflecting our conviction in the significant opportunity from our expanding pipeline and the growing portfolio of new product launches,” Litchfield said.
“We will continue to invest in value-creating opportunities that drive both near- and long-term growth,” Litchfield said of Merck’s capital allocation plans. “Business development remains an important priority, and we retain financial flexibility within a strong investment-grade credit rating to pursue additional science-driven, value-enhancing transactions.”
One of the key new clinical programs that Merck plans to invest in next year is advancing its PD-1xVEGF bispecific MK-2010, partnered with China’s SBP Group (formerly Sino Biopharmaceutical), into phase 3.
Following “productive discussions” with the FDA and “the totality of data generated to date,” Merck will initiate phase 3 development for MK-2010, including combinations with Kelun-Biotech-partnered TROP2 antibody-drug conjugate sac-TMT, in first-line non-small cell lung cancer in the first half of 2027, Marjorie Green, Merck’s head of oncology global clinical development, told investors during an Oct. 26 event. This plan was confirmed by Merck’s R&D chief Dean Li, M.D., Ph.D., on Thursday’s call.
The decision comes as sac-TMT, used alongside Keytruda, delivered a 51% progression-free survival benefit against Keytruda-chemo in first-line, PD-L1-negative NSCLC in a China phase 3. In parallel, sac-TMT’s first global phase 3 readout, in endometrial cancer, also showed consistent data with previous China results. 
Beyond sac-TMT, positive phase 3 results from Moderna-partnered mRNA cancer vaccine intismeran autogene and diabetic macular edema candidate remigromig drew some recent investor scrutiny. 
On the mRNA immunotherapy specifically, jacked-up investor expectations have overshadowed the otherwise strong data itself. 
During Thursday’s call, Li called the INTerpath-001 melanoma trial “a landmark study in its own right,” citing a comment from Antoni Ribas, M.D., Ph.D., a leading melanoma clinical researcher from the University of California Los Angeles.
“Because of that, we would hope that upon approval that the NCCN guidelines would potentially define this as a new standard of care,” Li said.
Looking into 2027, Merck expects some top-line pressure, as Litchfield flagged the potential for more “moderate” growth thanks to more than $2 billion of negative impact from generic competition affecting Bridion, the Januvia family and Bayer-partnered Adempas.
Keytruda, while still a major pillar of Merck’s business, will “see growth moderating” as it has reached peak penetration in several indications, she said. Total Keytruda sales, including the subcutaneous Keytruda Qlex, reached $8.6 billion during the third quarter, up 6% year over year.
Merck is locked in a patent fight with Halozyme over Keytruda Qlex. An injunction was recently ordered by a Dutch patent court that affects the subcutaneous drug’s rollout in eight European nations. 
The injunction was put in place until a hearing is held, and it “doesn’t speak to the merits of our belief,” Merck’s CEO Rob Davis noted on the call. “We continue to feel very, very good that we have a position both in the U.S. and in Europe.”
Meanwhile, in the vaccines business, Merck’s HPV vaccine Gardasil enjoyed a rally thanks to “favorable public-sector purchasing patterns and higher net pricing” in the U.S., with 14% year-over-year growth to $2 billion, according to an earnings release.
For vaccines overall, Litchfield said a $250 million buy-in from the CDC this year will unwind in 2027.
On other recent launch progress, pulmonary arterial hypertension med Winrevair nearly doubled sales to $694 million in the third quarter, and kidney cancer drug Welireg grew sales by 56% to $307 million. 
Also in the infectious disease department, sales of Merck’s RSV preventive Enflonsia jumped 138% year over year to $187 million as inventory builds ahead of a new RSV season.
For 2026, Merck narrowed the range of its full-year revenue guidance to between $66.8 billion and $67.3 billion.

Maxon teased what looks like another AI tool for 3D artists in an X video, possibly for Cinema 4D , and the reaction isn’t good, though probably as expected. There's little detail so far, but the prospect of more AI entering creative software is already rubbing some artists the wrong way.
Over on X users bombarded the teaser video with reactions, from the somewhat restrained, “You guys are gulping the whole AI stuff without its users in mind” to the angry, “I’m going to have a good laugh when they use AI to reverse-engineer all your programs, and you go bankrupt. If you’ve got the nerve to screw us artists over, I hope you get a taste of your own medicine,” and the blunt, “A slop generator, cool”.
🐦‍⬛✍️
Coming soon. https://t.co/6rEbIPTWBR October 28, 2026 
Some looked beyond outrage and perhaps gave Maxon some leeway to see where this can help: “If you want to use AI in a 3D program, the most useful feature would be for making UVs. I hate UV'ing; it's like making the model again,” says a user.
Of all the comments, I find this one from ‘Augenhorn’ sums up the situation generally with AI in creative apps, with just the right balance of cynicism, scepticism and grudging concession: “This is not how people will use it. They will feed in AI slop to get out a slop Model and then fiddle around with it tiredly, only to go all the way over to get scammed by Higgsfield. Anyway, nice feature though; it’s all not your fault… love and pay C4D for 14 years now.”
Maxon embraces generative AI
This isn’t Maxon’s first time with AI, and it follows Autodesk's lead in using the tech to make 3D modelling and animation more accessible. In March, Maxon announced a partnership with Tencent Cloud to bring its HY 3D generative AI engine into Cinema 4D , letting artists generate base 3D models and UVs from text prompts or image references. The plan is to let artists take those AI-generated starting points into Cinema 4D's existing tools to sculpt, refine, animate and render them. This could tease a fuller reveal of that integration.
Cinema 4D remains one of the best 3D modelling software packages , and also now supports AI assistants such as ChatGPT and Claude, which can use the software's tools to handle jobs like organising scenes, creating material variations, and setting up renders. The idea is to take some of the more repetitive work off an artist's hands while keeping them in control of the scene.
But there's a difference between an assistant that helps you get through a tedious afternoon of production work and a tool that generates 3D assets from a prompt, and artists have different opinions on where that line should sit, even as brands like Maxon, Autodesk, and Adobe begin to blur it. Maxon's AI plans have already attracted criticism, including its response to Digital Twin, its tool for placing existing 3D product models into AI-generated marketing environments.

The wider creative AI dilemma
With all this in mind, and knowing AI is affecting creative jobs , it's unsurprising that when another AI tease appears, some artists don't exactly reach for the champagne. The bigger concern is how quickly creative software companies are embracing generative AI, and whether the promise of faster workflows is worth the potential cost to the craft and the people who make a living from it.
It's not yet clear whether this latest teaser ties into the planned Tencent integration, Cinema 4D's existing AI assistant tools, or something entirely different. Until Maxon provides more detail, it's hard to judge what the tool will actually do, let alone whether artists should welcome it or worry about it.
Still, Maxon is finding that selling AI features to a creative audience isn't as easy as some software companies might have hoped. Artists want to see what these tools can do, but they also want to know why they're being made, how they'll fit into a real working day and what the company thinks the future of 3D art should look like.

SCHOTT Poonawalla Renamed SCHOTT Pharma India, Reaffirms Long-Term Commitment to Indian Pharma Market 
Written By : sheeba farhat Published On 2026-10-29T15:46:32+05:30   |   Updated On 29 Oct 2026 3:46 PM IST 
New Delhi: SCHOTT Poonawalla Private Limited will become SCHOTT Pharma India Private Limited, marking an important new chapter in the company's journey and strengthening its connection with the global SCHOTT Pharma organization.
The new identity more clearly reflects the India business’s place within SCHOTT Pharma’s global network and its role in advancing high-quality drug containment and delivery solutions for the pharmaceutical and biotech industries. It brings together the company’s strong manufacturing footprint, long-standing customer relationships and deep market expertise in India with SCHOTT Pharma’s global capabilities, innovation and scientific excellence.
For customers, partners and employees, this is a change in name, not a change in commitment. There is no change in ownership, management, employees, business strategy, operations, products, services or existing customer commitments.
The transition reinforces SCHOTT Pharma India’s long-term commitment to customers in India and international markets, while creating a stronger and more consistent connection to the global SCHOTT Pharma brand.
Building on a heritage of more than 140 years, the new identity brings the company’s heritage and future ambition under one global name, reflecting the values that continue to define SCHOTT Pharma: innovation, quality, scientific excellence and trust.
Also Read: TPG to acquire 35% stake in SCHOTT Poonawalla from SII 
SCHOTT Pharma India represents both continuity and progress: the same trusted business, capabilities and relationships, now with an identity that more clearly reflects who we are today and where we are headed.
Roy Joseph, CEO & Managing Director, SCHOTT Pharma India Private Limited, said, “SCHOTT Pharma India represents the next chapter of our journey, combining our strength in India with SCHOTT Pharma’s global innovation and expertise. We see significant opportunity to build on our capabilities, deepen collaboration with pharmaceutical and biotechnology partners, and advance drug containment and delivery solutions. As we move forward, our focus remains on growing with our customers and contributing to the safe and reliable delivery of critical therapies to patients worldwide.”
“SCHOTT Pharma India plays a critical role in patient care. With more than 3 billion containers produced annually, this company enables around 7,000 injections to reach patients every minute,” said Dr. Christian Mias, CEO of SCHOTT Pharma AG & Co. KGaA, SCHOTT Pharma India’s major shareholder. “The name change from SCHOTT Poonawalla to SCHOTT Pharma India reinforces our strategic partnership and confirms our long-term commitment to India as a key pharma hub.”
The new identity builds on the company’s strong foundation in India. During the COVID-19 pandemic, its pharmaceutical vials supported more than 4.3 billion vaccine doses worldwide, including 3 billion doses in India. As India’s only manufacturer of glass pre-fillable syringes and sterile formats, the company also strengthens local supply capabilities. Furthermore, the company continues to invest significantly towards manufacturing capacity expansions of pre-fillable syringes and cartridges, strengthening their ability to support the rapidly evolving needs of biologics, biosimilars, GLP-1 based treatments and other advanced injectable therapies.
Looking ahead, SCHOTT Pharma India will focus on expanding capabilities across pharmaceutical drug containment and drug delivery solutions, driving innovation through closer customer collaboration, and strengthening operational excellence and sustainability. These priorities will support the company as it responds to the evolving needs of pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies while contributing to India’s growing role in the global pharmaceutical value chain.
SCHOTT Pharma India is a manufacturer of advanced drug containment and delivery solutions, serving pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies across global markets. Based on innovation in specialty glass and advanced materials, the company offers a comprehensive portfolio of injectable drug containment and delivery products, including vials, cartridges, syringes and ampoules. Manufactured to stringent international quality standards, SCHOTT Pharma India’s solutions enable safe storage of vaccines and biologics. Through continued investment in innovation and operational excellence, and a strong focus on quality, reliability and customer partnership, the company addresses evolving healthcare needs and supports better patient outcomes worldwide.

World's fourth-largest mining giant opens $1.4 billion lithium plants in South America as it commits $6.7 billion to projects in Guinea and South Africa
Olamilekan Okebiorun 
28 October 2026 11:32 PM
Rio Tinto, one of the world's largest publicly listed mining companies, has inaugurated two lithium plants worth $1.4 billion in Argentina, expanding its international operations alongside multibillion-dollar mining investments in Guinea and South Africa.
Ghana’s first lithium project at risk amidst global price slump: GETTY IMAGES 
Rio Tinto inaugurated two new lithium plants worth $1.4 billion in Argentina, boosting annual production capacity by 25,000 metric tonnes.
The investments strengthen Rio Tinto's position in the growing global lithium market, essential for electric vehicles and batteries.
Rio Tinto's global investment strategy also includes a $6.2 billion commitment to Guinea's Simandou iron ore project and a $473 million restart of mineral sands in South Africa.
Together, these initiatives expand Rio Tinto's presence across key commodity markets, including lithium, iron ore, and mineral sands in Argentina, Guinea, South Africa, and Madagascar.

The Anglo-Australian group officially opened the Sal de Vida plant and Fénix 1B expansion in Argentina's Catamarca province on October 28, 2026, adding a combined 25,000 metric tonnes of annual lithium carbonate equivalent production capacity.
According to Reuters, the investment strengthens Rio Tinto's position in the global lithium market as demand increases for minerals used in electric vehicles and battery storage systems.
The company ranked fourth among publicly listed mining groups by market capitalisation in October 2026, with an estimated valuation of $139.4 billion.
ADVERTISEMENT
Rio Tinto expands lithium production in Argentina
Sal de Vida is expected to produce 15,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent annually, while the Fénix 1B expansion will contribute another 10,000 tonnes once both facilities reach full capacity.
Rio Tinto is also developing its Rincón project in Argentina's Salta province, targeting annual production capacity of 60,000 tonnes as part of its broader ambition to reach 200,000 tonnes of global lithium capacity by 2028.
Speaking at the inauguration, chief executive Simon Trott outlined the company's production ambitions.
"We live in an era in which the world needs more lithium. At Rio Tinto, we have set ourselves the goal of reaching 200,000 tons of annual production capacity, with opportunities to raise that figure much higher," Trott said.
ADVERTISEMENT
The expansion relies partly on direct lithium extraction technology, which can shorten processing times compared with conventional evaporation methods, although questions remain about operating costs and commercial scalability.
Rio Tinto's investments extend across Africa
Beyond Argentina, Rio Tinto is advancing its estimated $6.2 billion funding commitment to Guinea's Simandou iron ore project, one of Africa's largest mining and infrastructure developments.
The investment forms part of an $11.6 billion programme covering the SimFer mine and associated railway and port infrastructure.
Simandou is designed to support annual exports of up to 120 million tonnes of iron ore at full capacity, with Rio Tinto's SimFer joint venture responsible for blocks three and four, targeting 60 million tonnes.
ADVERTISEMENT
The development recorded its first iron ore shipment in December 2025, with further construction continuing in 2026.
Meanwhile, Rio Tinto approved a $473 million investment in March 2026 to restart the Zulti South mineral sands project at Richards Bay Minerals in South Africa.
The project, suspended since 2020, is expected to extend operations until 2050, with initial commercial production scheduled for late 2028.
Beyond Guinea and South Africa, the mining group also maintains mineral sands operations in Madagascar through QIT Madagascar Minerals, which produces ilmenite for international industrial markets.
The investments span different commodity markets, with Rio Tinto's Argentine operations focused on lithium for battery manufacturing, while its African projects supply iron ore and minerals used in construction, manufacturing and other industries.

title: French firm Safran helps build aircraft wings of the future in UK factory - France 24
query: ("Safran" OR "Safran Group") (Korea OR Korean) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
French firm Safran helps build aircraft wings of the future in UK factory
Wolverhampton (United Kingdom) (AFP) – For the French aerospace company Safran the future runs through a century-old factory in Britain where it aims to manufacture mechanisms key for the folding wings that will enable the next-generation of Airbus planes to meet ambitious fuel reduction targets. 
Issued on: 28/10/2026 - 17:26 
3 min Reading time 
Share 
French firm Safran is looking to the future with its state-of-the-art production at a UK factory © STEPHANE DE SAKUTIN / AFP/File 
These new thinner and folding wings will require twice as many small motors, or actuators, that control the movement of an aircraft's movable surfaces.
Behind the red-brick facades at the plant in Wolverhampton, western England -- once typical of the UK's industrial heartlands -- Safran is developing its new business of actuation systems.
Previously better known as an aircraft engine manufacturer, the pivot follows its 2025 acquisition of the flight controls and actuation activities of US-based Collins Aerospace for $1.8 billion.
Actuation refers to the mechanisms that control the movement of wings and surfaces, allowing an aircraft to climb, descend, bank, or turn. 
Their proper functioning is essential for maintaining the aircraft's trajectory and ensuring flight safety.
"It was the last critical piece of equipment which Safran was lacking," said Franck Saudo, president of Safran Electronics & Defense.
Safran also manufactures landing gear, aircraft seats, and lavatories.
The Wolverhampton plant, opened in 1903 and which employs more than 1,500 people, is a key site among the 11 facilities acquired by Safran from Collins Aerospace.
In the defence sector, the site manufactures actuation systems for missiles and for the weapons-bay doors of the F-35.
According to Saudo, this technology helps preserve the stealth capabilities of the American fighter jet.
Less fuel
Airbus plans to launch the successor to its best-selling A320 family of single-aisle medium-haul aircraft around 2030 with 20 to 30 percent better fuel efficiency than current models.
Safran is seeking to contribute to this fuel savings with its wing actuators.
These mechanisms are used, among other things, to deploy wing flaps during the plane's landing approach, helping to slow the aircraft.
"When a bird lands, it spreads its feathers to increase the size of its wings. An aircraft does exactly the same thing," Saudo explained.
For the so-called wing of tomorrow -- a longer, folding wing being developed by Airbus in Britain -- twice as many actuators will be needed, he noted.
Flight tests of this experimental new wing, which is longer and lighter to maximise aerodynamic efficiency and reduce fuel burn, are scheduled to begin this year.
Another challenge is the limited space. Since the wing is thinner, there is less room for actuators, which must therefore be smaller.
This innovative wing structure means the aircraft would exceed the current maximum wingspan limit set by airports of 36 meters (118 feet) by 4.5 meters on each side.
Actuators would therefore also be needed to fold the wing tips while the aircraft is taxiing on the ground.
Today actuators are predominantly hydraulic. But in the next generation of aircraft about half are expected to be electric, making them lighter.
The acquisition of Collins, a hydraulic systems specialist, has allowed Safran to combine that expertise with its own strengths in electrical systems.
Open fans
To prepare for increased production rates, a robot installed a year ago now assembles gearbox units.
Other robots are used in the manufacture of metal parts, but many assembly operations are still performed by hand.
The innovative Rise open fan a joint production by Safran and GE Aeronautics which cuts fuel burn and carbon emissions © Thomas SAMSON / AFP/File 
"Humans are more agile," Eric Valentin, head of actuation, told AFP.
For the aircraft of tomorrow, Safran is also developing an "open fan" engine free of the nacelle or encasing, which traditionally encloses and protects the fan blades.
The company says this technology could reduce fuel consumption by 20 percent, but development on these fans is less advanced, with flight testing not expected until around 2029.
"Historically in aviation, the main driver of fuel-burn reduction was the engine," Bruno Fichefeux, Airbus head of future programs, told AFP at the Farnborough Airshow in July.
"Today, we realise that the engine remains a major contributor, but it's no longer the dominant contributor," he said.
"Wing shape delivers an equivalent contribution in terms of fuel-burn reduction."

content_text:
What NXP Semiconductors (NXPI) Said on Its Q3 Earnings Call
4 min read 
NXPI 
Why NXP Semiconductors Could Be the AI Stock Everyone Is Missing 
NXP Semiconductors NXPI reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $3.79 billion, up 19% from a year earlier and 8% sequentially, as automotive, industrial and data-center-related demand supported growth across its business. Revenue increased 22% year over year excluding the MEMS sensor business. 
President and CEO Rafael Sotomayor said every region posted double-digit year-over-year growth. Automotive and industrial, which together represent roughly one-third of company revenue, were key contributors, alongside continued strength in data-center infrastructure. 
These 3 AI Stocks Just Crushed Earnings: Still Time To Buy? 
Non-GAAP operating margin rose 330 basis points from a year earlier to 37.1%, while non-GAAP earnings per share increased 35% to $4.20. The company generated $1.21 billion in free cash flow during the quarter, equal to approximately 32% of revenue. 
Automotive crosses $2 billion 
Automotive revenue surpassed $2 billion for the first time in the quarter. Revenue in the segment was up 17% year over year excluding sensors, driven by content gains in software-defined vehicle, or SDV, products despite what Sotomayor described as a “flattish” vehicle-production environment. 
Why NXP Semiconductors’ Post-Earnings Dip Could Be a Buying Window 
NXP said SDV revenue was running at an annualized rate above $1.5 billion in the third quarter and remains on track to reach its $2 billion target in 2027. The company expects the transition from domain-based vehicle architectures to zonal and centralized computing to increase semiconductor content per vehicle by two to three times compared with current architectures. 
The company plans to begin shipping its next-generation SDV processors, including the S32K5 zonal and S32N central-compute platforms, in 2027. Sotomayor said RV Tech, the Volkswagen-Rivian joint venture, had standardized its zonal platform on NXP’s S32K5 across both companies. NXP also expects its first S32K5 shipments in China as early as the first quarter of 2027. 
During the quarter, NXP secured its first S32K5 design win in humanoid robotics with what Sotomayor described as a leading U.S. global technology company. He said the same components used in software-defined vehicles—including central compute, sensing, networking and secure control—are moving into robotics and other intelligent edge systems. 
In response to analyst questions, management said it had not seen broad-based automotive restocking. Sotomayor said customer visibility had improved as lead times extended and automakers became more directly involved in providing demand guidance. CFO Bill Betz added that NXP serves about 40% of automotive distribution directly, giving the company close visibility into that channel. 
Industrial and data center momentum 
Industrial and IoT revenue was $802 million, up 39% from a year earlier. The industrial portion of the business grew nearly 50%, led by data centers, factory automation and healthcare, and now accounts for about 70% of industrial IoT revenue, according to the company. 
NXP said AI-enabled processors are expected to represent approximately 15% of industrial IoT processor revenue in 2026, more than double the prior year’s level. Its Ara discrete neural processing unit is gaining traction in industrial automation and automotive AI applications, with volume production anticipated in 2028. 
Communication infrastructure and other revenue rose 54% year over year to $503 million, supported by data-center and secure-card demand. NXP now expects its data-center revenue to exceed the more than $500 million outlook it previously gave for 2026 and to surpass $1 billion in a couple of years. 
Sotomayor said NXP is focused on the data-center control plane, including top-of-rack switches, controllers, processors, secure elements and interfaces. The company views networking, security and processing requirements as increasing alongside higher-performance data-center infrastructure. 
Mobile revenue was $411 million, down 4% from a year earlier. 
Margins, cash returns and fourth-quarter outlook 
Third-quarter non-GAAP gross margin was 58.6%, up 160 basis points year over year, reflecting improved factory utilization and revenue growth, Betz said. The company ended the period with $3.94 billion in cash and $10.98 billion in debt, resulting in a net leverage ratio of 1.3 times. 
Inventory days declined to 148 from 156 in the second quarter, including about 13 days of pre-built inventory associated with planned front-end factory consolidations. NXP expects to have about 15 days of pre-built inventory at the end of 2026. 
The board authorized an additional $5 billion for share repurchases, bringing total authorization to approximately $6.3 billion. NXP returned $1.7 billion to shareholders through dividends and buybacks over the trailing 12 months and said it plans to accelerate repurchases in the fourth quarter and in 2027. 
For the fourth quarter, NXP forecast revenue of $3.85 billion, plus or minus $100 million, representing growth of 15% year over year and 2% sequentially. The outlook implies 18% annual growth excluding the MEMS sensor business. 
Automotive revenue is expected to rise in the low-double-digit percentage range year over year and low-single digits sequentially. 
Industrial and IoT revenue is projected to increase in the high-20% range from a year earlier. 
Mobile revenue is expected to decline in the mid-teens percentage range year over year. 
Communication infrastructure and other revenue is forecast to rise more than 50% year over year. 
NXP expects fourth-quarter non-GAAP gross margin of 59%, plus or minus 50 basis points, and non-GAAP operating margin of 37.5% at the midpoint. It forecast non-GAAP earnings per share of $4.36 at the midpoint, up 30% year over year. 
Looking into 2027, Betz said the company expects to continue delivering double-digit revenue growth, expand gross margin to 60%, and increase capital expenditures to about 5% of revenue as it adds back-end capacity and develops a new assembly and test facility in Malaysia for production in 2028. NXP also plans to realign its end-market revenue reporting beginning in 2027 and will host an investor day on March 3 in Boston. 
About NXP Semiconductors NXPI 
NXP Semiconductors N.V. is a global semiconductor company that develops technologies for automotive, industrial, communications infrastructure, mobile, and Internet of Things applications. The company provides processing, connectivity, security, sensing, and power-management solutions that help enable connected and automated systems. 
Its product portfolio includes microcontrollers and application processors, automotive networking and radar solutions, secure identification and authentication technologies, near-field communication products, radio-frequency power amplifiers, analog and mixed-signal devices, and wireless connectivity solutions.

A long-term shareholder who rules out any governance ambitions
BE Semiconductor Industries (Besi) took note, on October 27, 2026, of a press release published the previous day by Applied Materials. In this statement, Applied announced that it had increased its strategic stake in the Dutch semiconductor assembly equipment manufacturer. According to the press release, Applied concluded an agreement intended to raise its stake to approximately 20% of Besi's outstanding shares, whose headquarters are located in Duiven, Netherlands.
Applied accompanied this announcement with three clarifications that frame its position. The group considers its investment in Besi as a long-term commitment. It does not intend to seek board representation in the company. It currently has no plans to acquire additional shares.
These statements have concrete significance for reading the shareholding structure. A stake expected to reach approximately one-fifth of the capital would make Applied Materials a significant shareholder in Besi's ownership structure. By forgoing a board seat and indicating it does not wish to increase further, Applied presents itself as a stable shareholder rather than as a player seeking to influence Besi's decisions.
Besi's press release reiterates these elements by explicitly citing Applied's statement as a source. Besi's ordinary shares are listed on Euronext Amsterdam under the symbol BESI, while its depositary receipts (Level 1 ADR) are traded on over-the-counter American markets under the symbol BESIY. Applied's new position therefore concerns a group whose value is tracked in both Europe and the United States.

The capital link is supported by an established industrial partnership. Besi and Applied have been working together since 2020 on the development and commercialization of integrated hybrid bonding production systems, intended for leading semiconductor manufacturers. This collaboration combines Applied's expertise in wafer-level chip manufacturing, upstream in the supply chain, with Besi's technologies in chip placement, interconnection, and assembly.
The partnership was recently expanded. Besi joined Applied's EPIC Center as an innovation partner. The joint work focuses on the next generation of three-dimensional integrated circuits, the integration of logic and memory, the scaling up of thermocompression bonding, as well as new wafer-to-wafer, chip-to-chip, and chip-to-panel assembly platforms.
Besi's Chief Executive Officer, Richard W. Blickman, welcomed this decision favorably. "We welcome Applied's increased strategic investment as further confirmation of Besi's strategy in hybrid bonding and wafer-level assembly," he stated, according to a translation of the press release. He added that the transaction highlights future areas of potential collaboration between the two companies, targeting next-generation artificial intelligence and photonics systems for leading customers in the industry.

This capital increase comes a few days after the publication of third-quarter results. On October 22, 2026, Besi reported revenue up 113.6% and quarterly net income of €107.2 million. Earnings per share came in at €1.33, against an average expectation of €1.30 from analysts, with the fourth quarter expected to remain stable.
On the market, the share has experienced a sharp decline in recent weeks. On October 15, 2026, the stock showed a decline close to 35% over one quarter. On October 23, 2026, it fell below its 150-day low, at €155.55, as several brokers, including JP Morgan and BofA, had lowered their price targets during the month.

content_text:
Applied Materials Raises BE Semiconductor Stake to 20%, Deepening AI Advanced Packaging Push; Deal Awaits U.S. Antitrust Review
Add preferred source 2 
Applied Materials announced it will raise its stake in Dutch packaging equipment maker BE Semiconductor Industries from 9% to approximately 20%, having signed an accelerated share purchase agreement, with the deal still pending U.S. antitrust review. Applied Materials became BE Semiconductor's largest shareholder after first taking a stake in April 2025, and the increased holding is aimed at AI chip advanced packaging. The two companies have collaborated on hybrid bonding technology since 2020 and have jointly developed the Kinex integrated die-to-wafer system. Applied Materials said it does not intend to push its stake above 20% or seek board seats. BE Semiconductor holds roughly 70% of the global hybrid bonding equipment market, with third-quarter orders up 96% year over year, and hybrid bonding equipment orders in the first nine months of 2026 already more than double the full-year 2025 level.
Key Elements 
Applied Materials BE Semiconductor Industries hybrid bonding EPIC Center Prabh Raja ASML Kinex Piotech 
U.S. semiconductor equipment giant Applied Materials announced Monday that it will raise its stake in Dutch packaging equipment maker BE Semiconductor Industries (BESI) from the current 9% to approximately 20%, deepening cooperation between the two companies in advanced packaging for artificial intelligence (AI) chips. The increased holding has been signed under an accelerated share purchase agreement but still requires U.S. antitrust review.
Applied Materials became the largest shareholder of the Dutch company after first taking a 9% stake in April 2025. At that time, BE Semiconductor had a market value of about $13 billion. Under the plan, the stake will approach 20% once the increase is completed. However, Applied Materials made clear that at this stage it does not intend to push its holding above 20% or seek seats on BE Semiconductor's board, indicating that this is a long-term strategic investment centered on technology cooperation rather than a move toward a full acquisition.
The expanded cooperation focuses on next-generation chip interconnection and packaging technology, with the goal of supporting the next generation of AI semiconductors. The two companies have jointly invested in hybrid bonding process development since 2020, a technology regarded as a key link in advanced packaging and mainly used for high-performance chips.
Hybrid bonding is characterized by directly bonding copper interconnects and dielectric layers without the need for traditional bumps, allowing a substantial increase in connection density between chips. The two companies have jointly developed the Kinex integrated die-to-wafer hybrid bonding system, combining Applied Materials' expertise in etching, planarization, deposition and inspection with BE Semiconductor's technology in high-precision die placement and assembly. BE Semiconductor also recently formally joined Applied Materials' newly established chip equipment research organization, the EPIC Center.
Prabh Raja, president of Applied Materials' Semiconductor Products Group, said in a statement: "We look forward to further deepening our strategic collaboration with Besi to deliver the innovative products and technologies customers need to scale AI systems."
From a market structure perspective, BE Semiconductor holds a critical position in the advanced packaging equipment sector. According to market data, BE Semiconductor accounts for about 70% of the global hybrid bonding equipment market. Its flagship model, the Datacon 8800 CHAMEO ultra plus AC, achieves alignment accuracy of up to 100 nanometers and a throughput of up to 2,000 cycles per hour, with volume production potential.
Demand-side momentum is also strengthening. BE Semiconductor's third-quarter orders surged 96% year over year to €342.6 million (approximately $382.0 million); hybrid bonding equipment orders in the first nine months of 2026 were already more than double the full-year 2025 level. The company's latest financial report shows that its hybrid bonding customer base has expanded to 23 companies, with cumulative equipment demand exceeding 215 units.
It is worth noting that last week the market briefly worried that Dutch semiconductor equipment leader ASML might become a competitor to BE Semiconductor in the hybrid bonding arena, which BE Semiconductor has denied. Against the backdrop of advanced packaging becoming key to the AI chip computing power race, alliances and competitive-cooperative relationships among equipment makers are rapidly intensifying.
On the other hand, Chinese equipment makers are also catching up in hybrid bonding technology. China's Piotech recorded hybrid bonding equipment revenue of CNY 136 million (approximately $20.4 million) in 2025, up 41.92% year over year, and has secured repeat orders for wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding systems, meaning that this niche market previously dominated by a small number of vendors is gradually seeing new suppliers emerge.
For investors, the most direct significance of this deal is that Applied Materials is betting its resources on the "back-end" packaging link of AI chips. As advancing Moore's Law becomes increasingly difficult, improvements in chip performance increasingly depend on advanced packaging and heterogeneous integration, and hybrid bonding is one of the highest-barrier technologies in this area. By tying up with BE Semiconductor through a stake purchase rather than an acquisition, Applied Materials can share technology and customers while avoiding the operational risks and regulatory resistance of full integration.
However, the deal still must pass U.S. antitrust review, and the timetable and conditions remain uncertain. Applied Materials has also stated that it will not pursue board seats or increase its stake further, and whether the cooperation can be translated into substantive orders and revenue contribution will be a key focus for the market going forward.

News: Microelectronics 
27 October 2026 
Infineon establishing first high-volume fab for GaN power semiconductors on 300mm wafers in Europe
Infineon Technologies AG of Munich, Germany is establishing the world’s first high-volume manufacturing facility for gallium nitride (GaN) power semiconductors on 300mm wafers in Europe. As part of the project, the firm will invest about €1.1bn in its existing cleanroom facilities at the site in Villach, Austria by 2034. Leveraging both the existing and upgraded infrastructure will enable efficient and cost-effective expansion of manufacturing capacity, it is reckoned. Production is scheduled to start by the end of 2027. 
Infineon’s investment addresses the rapidly growing demand for high-performance power supply solutions, as gallium nitride enables significant efficiency gains in applications such as AI data centers, energy infrastructure, e-mobility, robotics and consumer electronics. 
Picture: Infineon’s site in Villach, Austria. 
Two years ago, Infineon achieved the milestone of processing the world’s first 300mm GaN wafers. Compared with 200mm wafers, the 300mm diameter enables the production of 2.3 times as many chips per wafer. Infineon is now transferring this more efficient technology to the first high-volume manufacturing facility serving customers. 
“This substantial investment shows our clear commitment to strengthening the European semiconductor ecosystem and Europe’s technological sovereignty. By establishing high-volume manufacturing on 300mm wafers, we will be the first company in the world to bring gallium nitride power electronics into volume production,” says Infineon’s CEO Jochen Hanebeck. “In doing so, we are paving the way for the widespread use of gallium nitride in a wide range of key applications in areas such as artificial intelligence, energy infrastructure, e-mobility and robotics,” he adds. 
“We are witnessing one of the largest single investments in the history of Austria’s high-tech industry,” states Christian Stocker, Federal Chancellor of the Republic of Austria. “This is not only a strong commitment to Austria as a business location but also helps ensure that the future of the semiconductor industry will not be shaped solely in Asia or the USA, but also in Austria and Europe,” he adds. 
“Europe currently accounts for only around 10% of global chip production… We must also manufacture this key technology in Europe,” says Wolfgang Hattmannsdorfer, Austrian Federal Minister for Economic Affairs. “Austria is already a leader in energy-efficient chips. Relative to our population, we rank first in the EU in business R&D spending in the semiconductor sector. With our industrial strategy, we intend to build on this lead and not only research new technologies but also manufacture them on an industrial scale,” he adds. “Every job in the chip industry can provide six additional jobs across the broader economy. That is why we intend to support Infineon’s new chip production with up to €319m — subject to clear funding criteria for the location. This will ensure that public funds strengthen value creation and jobs in Austria over the long term.” 
The investment is being supported under the European Chips Act. The European Commission has approved the €319m in state aid. The formal funding commitment by the Austrian Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs, Energy and Tourism is expected within the stipulated time limits.
“Competitiveness and technological sovereignty emerge where excellent research is translated into industrial value creation. This is precisely where our flagship project comes in. From Austria, we are bringing innovation into industrial application, strengthening our technological leadership and securing highly skilled jobs,” says Infineon Technologies Austria AG’s CEO Sabine Herlitschka. “The entire Austrian semiconductor ecosystem benefits — from research organizations and universities to industrial partners. We are thus sustainably strengthening Europe’s competitiveness and strategic autonomy in microelectronics.”
Infineon reckons that the investment strengthens Villach’s role as a global competence center for power electronics and new semiconductor materials. Infineon Austria currently employs about 5800 people, including 4800 at the Villach site (as of end-September 2025). Together with universities, research institutions, start-ups and industry partners, Infineon forms the core of a microelectronics ecosystem in southern Austria. The establishment of the new 300mm GaN manufacturing facility is also expected to create synergies with the power electronics R&D activities in Villach.

title: HyProMag USA Pre-Feasibility Study Outlines Future Expansion Options to Quadruple Planned U.S. Rare Earth Magnet Capacity Indicating an Incremental Post-Tax NPV of up to US$2.1 Billion - Yahoo Finance
query: "HyProMag" ("press release" OR "investor relations" OR earnings OR announcement OR investment OR expansion OR acquisition OR partnership OR Korea) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
HyProMag USA Pre-Feasibility Study Outlines Future Expansion Options to Quadruple Planned U.S. Rare Earth Magnet Capacity Indicating an Incremental Post-Tax NPV of up to US$2.1 Billion
ACCESS Newswire · HyProMag USA 
HyProMag USA 
October 26, 2026 15 min read 
Independent Pre-Feasibility Study completed by PegasusTSI Inc. and BBA USA Inc. supports three new plants with a centralized finishing hub - in addition to the Company's first plant at Northlake, Texas - indicating an estimated incremental post-tax NPV of US$1.85 billion to US$2.06 billion, a post-tax IRR of 31% to 36%, competitive manufacturing costs and higher value, low-carbon finished magnet production. 
DALLAS-FORT WORTH, TX / ACCESS Newswire / October 26, 2026 / HyProMag USA LLC ("HyProMag USA" or the "Company") is pleased to announce the completion of an independent Pre-Feasibility Study ("PFS" or the "Study") undertaken by PegasusTSI Inc. and BBA USA Inc. evaluating the potential expansion of its proposed U.S. rare earth magnet manufacturing platform beyond its first plant in Northlake, Texas (the "Northlake Texas Facility"), which is in detailed engineering, with Phase 1 commissioning expected in mid-2028. 
The PFS evaluates a three-planti phased expansion strategy: three new regional production plants, supported by a centralized manufacturing, finishing and technology hub (the " Central Texas Hub "), to produce commercial neodymium iron boron ("NdFeB") magnet products in the United States from both end-of-life recycled feedstock and primary alloy material. Together with the Northlake Texas Facilityii, the platform targets total salable material production of approximately 6,000 metric tons per year by 2034, an increase of 4,474 metric tons per year above production from the Northlake Texas Facility. 
Annual total magnetic material production in 2034 from the Company would comprise approximately 4,192 metric tons of magnets, 1,305 metric tons of magnetic NdFeB alloy powder and 503 metric tons of other salable material. The PFS economics listed below cover the three new plants, including the Central Texas Hub only; they do not include the Northlake Texas Facility, whose value is not included in the PFS results. 
The Study builds upon the engineering and development work completed for the Northlake Texas Facility and outlines a pathway for HyProMag USA to develop from a Hydrogen Processing of Magnet Scrap ("HPMS")iii enabled magnet recycler into a fully integrated producer of commercial rare earth magnet products for U.S. customers. 
The Company believes the platform combines the cost advantages and operational flexibility of both end-of-life recycled feedstock and primary alloy feedstocks, providing a flexible and scalable pathway to magnet manufacturing. 
HyProMag USA may also benefit from potential future access to primary sourced feedstock from Mkango Magnetic Materials Limited ("Mkango") pursuant to certain Mkango supply rights to the Company. 
Story Continues 
Highlights 
The PFS evaluated two development options, both based on modular production systems: 
Case 1 - Recycled feedstock only: HPMS recycling of magnet scrap to produce NdFeB alloy powder, sintered magnet blocks, finished and packaged magnets; and 
Case 2 - Recycled and primary feedstock: as Case 1, with the additional capex to support primary NdFeB alloy as a feedstock to produce NdFeB alloy powder, sintered magnet blocks, finished and packaged magnets. 
Project economics with a post-tax NPViv,v of US$1,854 million ( Case 2 ) to US$2,062 million ( Case 1 ) for the three new plants (excluding the Northlake Texas Facility), post-tax IRR of 31% ( Case 2 ) to 36% ( Case 1 ) and a Profitability Index (post-tax NPV divided by capital cost) of approximately 2.8x to 3.3x, based on forecast pricesvi and a Class 3 AACEvii capital cost estimate of approximately US$656 million ( Case 2 ) to US$623 million ( Case 1 ), respectively, with a payback of 3 years ( Case 2 ) and 2.3 years ( Case 1 ). 
Competitive Manufacturing Costs. For the first PFS Plant in 2030, the PFS estimates an All-In Sustaining Cost ("AISC") of approximately US$41.6 per kg ( Case 2 ) to US$37.4 per kg ( Case 1 ) of finished NdFeB products sold. AISC includes all downstream processing and finishing costs, including plating and epoxy coating. Based on forecast market prices and the forecast product mix, the weighted average realized all-in selling price in 2030 is estimated at approximately US$100.5 per kg, supporting strong margins and attractive project returns. 
Combined HyProMag USA platform value: The combined post-tax NPV range of the proposed Northlake Texas Facility and the potential PFS plants is estimated at US$2.6 billion to US$2.8 billion. 
The staged approach for the Northlake Texas Facility: viii Updated post-tax NPV of approximately US$723ix,x,xi,xii million based on forecast prices and a capital cost estimate of approximately US$167 millionxiii, increased due to the phased construction approach and the finalization of equipment orders. The reduction from the post-tax NPV of approximately US$797 million announced on June 22, 2026, reflects the later construction timetable, the higher capital costs and updated operating cost assumptions consistent with the PFS. 
Potential fourfold increase in U.S. magnet producing capacity: from approximately 1,048 metric tons per year of salable NdFeB magnets at the Northlake Texas Facility to approximately 4,192 metric tons per year across four plants by 2034. Phase 1 of the Northlake Texas Facility is expected to be commissioned in mid-2028. 
Integrated alloy processing and centralized finishing. The Central Texas Hub is expected to incorporate Vacuum Induction Melting ("VIM") and strip-casting operations, allowing the platform to process NdFeB alloy, provide magnet plating, passivation, coating, quality assurance and customer qualification for all plants. 
Higher-value magnet production: The production configuration would incorporate grain boundary diffusion ("GBD") capability, which would significantly increase the proportion of higher-value NdFeB magnet products. High-grade magnet production would increase from approximately 10% to 20% of total magnet output, supporting enhanced product mix, market access and project economics. 
Low-carbon production supported by a previously completed carbon footprint of approximately 2.35 kg CO₂-eq per kilogram of NdFeB sintered block product for the Northlake Texas Facilityxiv. 
Commercial qualification pathway: Product performance data and customer validation are underway with potential U.S. offtake customers, with the support of the HyProMag Group. 
Additional revenue opportunities: The platform would provide future opportunities for third-party magnet finishing activities, supporting enhanced utilization of manufacturing infrastructure and potential additional revenue streams. 
The platform is expected to play a key role in re-establishing domestic NdFeB magnet manufacturing in the United States, creating approximately 300 jobs across Texas, South Carolina, and Nevada, in addition to the 100 positions at the Northlake Texas Facility. 
Independent PFS: completed by PegasusTSI Inc. and BBA USA Inc. with support from HyProMag's international teams and the University of Birmingham, UK. Subject to ongoing review, the expansion strategy is expected to progress to a Feasibility Study at the appropriate time. 
Julian Treger, CoTec CEO commented : "This Pre-Feasibility Study confirms the opportunity to establish a significant domestic rare earth magnet manufacturing platform in the United States. The Study demonstrates robust economics and a pathway to producing higher-value NdFeB magnet products for strategically important sectors including advanced manufacturing, energy, defense and AI-driven technologies. Importantly, the platform is designed with the flexibility to utilize primary alloy feedstock alongside recycled materials, providing greater supply chain resilience and supporting long-term operational competitiveness. The results highlight the platform's potential to create substantial long-term value while strengthening the U.S. rare earth magnet supply chain." 
Will Dawes, Mkango CEO, commented: "The Study indicates the scalability of the HyProMag business model and provides a framework for disciplined growth in the United States using HyProMag USA's first plant in Northlake. Together with ongoing development activities in the United Kingdom and Germany, it strengthens the foundation for establishing a significant domestic rare earth magnet manufacturing capability for HyProMag. It also highlights the significant potential synergies between HyProMag USA and Mkango, including increased security of feedstock supply and enhanced supply chains into USA markets, respectively." 
Professor Allan Walton, Founder of HyProMag and Head of the Magnetic Materials Group at the University of Birmingham, commented: "The objective of the HyProMag platform has always been to demonstrate that HPMS technology can recover rare earth magnetic materials and convert them into high-performance commercial magnet products. The PFS outlines a pathway to scaling that capability through an integrated manufacturing platform incorporating magnet production, finishing and product qualification. Importantly, the enhanced production configuration would support the manufacture of a broader range of commercial magnet products for demanding industrial applications, while the inclusion of finishing, quality assurance and product development capabilities provides a foundation for continued product optimization and customer qualification." 
Platform Configuration 
The PFS assessed three new production plants in South Carolina, Nevada and a second location in Texas, which would operate alongside the Northlake Texas Facility. Each plant is intended to process feedstock, operate HPMS and produce unfinished sintered NdFeB blocks. 
The Central Texas Hub, located within the second Texas plant, is expected to incorporate alloy processing (VIM and strip-casting), GBD, machining, plating, passivation, epoxy coating, quality assurance, product qualification and technology development capabilities. 
Under the proposed configuration, unfinished sintered blocks produced from South Carolina, Nevada and the second facility in Texas would be transferred to the Central Texas Hub for advanced manufacturing and finishing. The Central Texas Hub is also designed to support future partnerships with specialist manufacturing and finishing providers, enabling the efficient scaling of advanced magnet production capability. 
Higher-Value Magnet Production 
A key outcome of the PFS was the optimization of the manufacturing configuration to increase production of higher-value NdFeB magnet products. This enhanced product mix would be supported by further incorporation of GBD technology, which enables the production of higher-performance magnet grades required for demanding applications across medical, industrial automation, robotics, energy infrastructure and advanced manufacturing markets. 
The increased proportion of higher-value magnet products would broaden exposure to premium end-use applications and is expected to support improved revenues, stronger operating margins and enhanced overall project returns. 
Recycling of Magnet End Cuts By-Products 
The PFS plants are designed to recover and reprocess manufacturing residues, including magnet machining end cuts, through the HPMS process, maximizing the use of rare earth materials. This integrated approach would support both production flexibility and the circular manufacturing characteristics of the HyProMag platform. 
Integrated Manufacturing Platform 
The Central Texas Hub is expected to create operating synergies through shared infrastructure and integrated processing capabilities. The Study indicates that the combination of integrated alloy processing, magnet manufacturing, finishing operations and flexible feedstock sourcing has the potential to support a competitive cost position for domestically manufactured rare earth magnet products. The Company believes these advantages will support the supply of U.S. manufactured magnets at competitive prices while providing customers with the benefits of domestic supply-chain security, traceability and low-carbon production. 
The Central Texas Hub is also expected to evolve into an advanced manufacturing, product qualification and technology development center serving the broader manufacturing platform. In addition to supporting HyProMag USA production, the facility would provide future opportunities to support third-party magnet finishing activities, creating the potential for additional revenue streams and improved utilization of manufacturing infrastructure. 
The proposed technology and product development center would leverage expertise from the wider HyProMag Group and the University of Birmingham's Magnetic Materials Group, supporting development, qualification and optimization of commercial magnet products. 
Flexible Feedstock Platform 
A key outcome of the independent PFS is the flexibility of a manufacturing platform capable of utilizing both recycled NdFeB materials and primary alloy feedstocks. This flexible sourcing model is expected to enhance supply-chain resilience, support production growth and provide the ability to optimize raw material inputs in response to market conditions and customer requirements. HPMS technology provides the foundation for processing recycled magnetic materials and integrating them into the broader manufacturing platform. 
Advancing Commercial Magnet Qualification with HyProMag Group 
Commercial magnet qualification activities continue across the wider HyProMag Group in the United Kingdom and Germany. These activities are expected to support qualification of future U.S.-produced magnet products, accelerate customer onboarding and reduce commercialization risk as the U.S. manufacturing platform expands. The Company believes this provides a meaningful advantage by allowing future U.S. operations to build upon existing technical and commercial progress rather than initiating qualification programs from a standing start. 
About HyProMag USA 
HyProMag USA is developing advanced rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing operations to establish a secure domestic U.S. supply chain for NdFeB magnets, essential components for AI infrastructure, defense systems, robotics, electric vehicles, and advanced electronics. Leveraging the revolutionary HPMS technology, developed over 15 years with over US$100 million in R&D investment, HyProMag USA is designed to deliver faster magnet-to-magnet short-loop recycling that uses 88% less energy and reduces carbon emissions by 85% compared to conventional methods. HPMS accepts a wide range of magnet-bearing feedstocks - including end-of-life EV motors, data-center and industrial equipment, consumer electronics, and manufacturing scrap - enabling recovery of magnet-grade material without chemical processing.

HyProMag USA LLC is owned 50:50 by CoTec Holdings Corp. (TSXV: CTH; OTCQX: CTHCF) ("CoTec") and HyProMag Limited. HyProMag Limited is 100% owned by Maginito Limited which is owned on a 79.4%/20.6% basis by Mkango Magnetic Materials Limited (AIM/TSX-V: MKA) and CoTec.

content_text:
Sumitomo Chemical Q2 Results: Net profit falls 12% as revenue and EBITDA decline
October 26, 2026 
Share Article Copy Link 
L eading agrochemical company Sumitomo Chemical India Ltd on Monday reported a 12.4% year-on-year decline in net profit to ₹156 crore for the second quarter, compared with ₹178 crore in the corresponding period last year. Revenue declined 2.5% YoY to ₹891 crore from ₹914 crore in the year-ago quarter.
Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation fell 15.7% to ₹183 crore from ₹217 crore. The EBITDA margin contracted to 20.56% in the September quarter from 24% in the corresponding quarter last year. Japan's Sumitomo Chemical said its wholly owned South Korean subsidiary, Dongwoo Fine-Chem, has signed an agreement with Samsung Electro-Mechanics to establish a joint venture to manufacture glass-core substrates for advanced semiconductor packages.
The new company is expected to be incorporated in 2026, subject to regulatory approvals. Glass core substrates are emerging as a key technology for advanced semiconductor packaging. They offer superior rigidity, dimensional stability, lower thermal expansion and reduced warpage, making them well-suited for increasingly powerful AI chips, high-performance computing and data centre applications.
The partners aim to establish a commercial supply system by the second half of fiscal 2027, after which the venture plans to gradually expand manufacturing capacity for glass core substrates. The announcement aligns with Sumitomo Chemical's strategy to expand its semiconductor materials business, with ICT-related businesses identified as a key long-term growth driver, according to a press release.
The group has been strengthening both its front-end semiconductor materials portfolio, including photoresists and specialty chemicals, and its back-end business through investments in advanced package materials, substrate materials and next-generation process technologies.

Enphase Energy and Infineon Announce World’s First 900 V GaN Bidirectional Switch Devices for AI Data Center Solid-State Transformers
Enphase Energy, Inc.

Enphase Energy, Inc. FREMONT, Calif., Oct. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Enphase Energy, Inc. (NASDAQ: ENPH), a global energy technology company, and Infineon Technologies AG (FSE: IFX / OTCQX: IFNNY) today announced that Enphase will deploy the world's first 900 V gallium nitride (GaN) monolithic bidirectional switch (BDS) devices, designed to operate in Enphase solid-state transformer power modules. The devices extend GaN technology to 900 V while retaining the high-frequency switching capabilities that enable compact, efficient power conversion. 
Enphase has pioneered the system-level development and demonstration, building on more than 10 years of in-house research into GaN power conversion, with device technology and engineering expertise from Infineon. Enphase is among the first to bring 650 V GaN BDS devices into volume production power electronics, and GaN HEMT technology is already operating in Enphase IQ9™ Microinverters deployed in the field. Extending that work with Infineon beyond 650 V, using Infineon's CoolGaN™ bidirectional switch portfolio, opens the door further to medium-voltage systems. 
The 900 V GaN devices allow Enphase to continue using components rated below 1 kV, expanding the design options towards high-performance power conversion typically governed by silicon carbide (SiC). This supports a single-stage architecture with high-frequency switching, low electromagnetic interference (EMI), and fewer points of failure. Switching at such high frequency shrinks the transformers and other magnetics needed in the power stage, cutting size, weight, and cost. 
Higher-voltage switches within that low-voltage envelope change the economics of power conversion. In a solid-state transformer, a medium-voltage input can be handled by fewer inverters connected in series while retaining the low switching losses and intrinsic bidirectionality of GaN BDS. Fewer building blocks means lower system-level losses at the same input current, fewer components in the power path, and a lower total switch count. On the DC side, higher-voltage unidirectional switch (UDS) devices allow power to be generated at a unipolar 800 volts rather than split +/-400 V buses, and support future 1,500 VDC bus architectures through split +/-750 V generation with fewer switches and lower bridge losses. 
The technology is particularly relevant to the Enphase IQ ® Solid-State Transformer (IQ SST), the company's solid-state transformer platform for AI data centers, where power density, efficiency, and uptime drive the economics of every megawatt deployed. The same devices are expected to benefit commercial solar inverters by enabling three-phase, line-to-line designs for 480 V applications in the United States and 400 V applications elsewhere, again with fewer switches, lower losses, and lower cost. 
Story Continues 
"Enphase asks more of our technology than almost anyone, and medium-voltage solid-state transformers are exactly where high-voltage GaN proves its value," said Johannes Schoiswohl, senior vice president and head of GaN Systems Business Line at Infineon. "Moving past 650 V lets system designers strip cost and loss out of the architecture rather than optimizing around it." 
"GaN is not new to us. It has been running in Enphase IQ9 Microinverters in the field, and that field data is why we trust it in a megawatt-class system," said Hans van Antwerpen, senior vice president and chief technology officer at Enphase Energy. "Moving to 900 V gives us more voltage headroom without giving up high-frequency switching, and it allows us to stay with components rated below 1 kV while reducing the number of converters in the system. Fewer parts in the power path means higher efficiency and fewer things that can fail." 
The 900 V GaN BDS devices have been successfully tested and are now being integrated into IQ SST development builds, with production qualification expected to follow. Learn more about the use of GaN in Enphase products in its white paper. 
About Enphase Energy, Inc. 
Enphase Energy is a global energy technology company advancing intelligent power systems for homes, businesses, and next-generation AI data centers. The company designs semiconductor-based energy technologies spanning solar, batteries, EV charging, energy management, and virtual power plants, and is developing solid-state transformer technology to address the rapidly growing power demands of AI data centers. Based in Fremont, California, Enphase is the world's leading supplier of microinverter-based solar and battery systems. The company revolutionized the solar industry with its microinverter technology and has shipped approximately 89.4 million microinverters, with approximately 5.3 million Enphase-based systems deployed in more than 165 countries. Enphase products enable people to harness the sun to make, use, save, and sell their own power, all controlled through the Enphase App. For more information, visit https://enphase.com/ .

MELBOURNE, October 23, 2026 — Rio Tinto will invest US$1.9 billion in Queensland’s Kangwinan bauxite project, replacing aging production while expanding capacity at its Weipa operations.
The miner’s October 23 announcement targets first output in 2029 and full production by 2032. Kangwinan is designed for 20 million tonnes of annual capacity, but Weipa’s overall capacity is expected to reach about 44 million tonnes, against current production of around 38 million.
The project will replace Andoom as that mine approaches the end of its life and help compensate for Gove’s planned production closure in 2029. The capital estimate includes $150 million of early works approved in 2025 and sits within Rio’s existing medium-term capital guidance.
Construction is expected to ramp up in 2027 and support more than 1,300 construction jobs. Rio forecasts an internal rate of return of approximately 22%, based on third-party market forecasts, rather than a guaranteed return.
Reuters reported that the development follows Rio’s agreement last month to acquire the adjacent Aurukun project from Glencore and Mitsubishi, subject to regulatory approvals.
