title: Thermo Fisher Q3 Revenue Hits $12.14 Billion as Shares Touch Record $705 - BigGo Finance
query: ("Thermo Fisher" OR "Thermo Fisher Scientific") (Korea OR Korean) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
Thermo Fisher Q3 Revenue Hits $12.14 Billion as Shares Touch Record $705
Add preferred source 
Thermo Fisher Scientific reported third-quarter revenue of $12.14 billion, up 9% year over year, with GAAP operating income of $2.263 billion, up 17%, and adjusted operating income of $2.968 billion, up 15%. After the results, the stock touched an intraday record of $705.79, and investment banks including Goldman Sachs and Rothschild raised their target prices to an average of $736.17. Consumables and other laboratory products remain the company's largest revenue source at 52% of sales. Thermo Fisher also opened its first AI automation innovation center in South Korea, where AI is used in cryo-electron microscopy products to cut some manual setup time by about 90%. The company disclosed the Precure research initiative with Mayo Clinic and is advancing clinical-side integration following its $8.875 billion acquisition of Clario.
Key Elements 
Thermo Fisher Scientific Nvidia Clario Mayo Clinic Marc Casper Orbitrap Isora Ion 560 Oracle AstraZeneca Tempus AI 
Thermo Fisher Scientific, the global leader in scientific services, this week delivered its third-quarter report card: quarterly revenue of $12.14 billion, up 9% year over year, and adjusted operating income of $2.968 billion, up 15%. After the results were released, the company's shares opened lower on Oct. 21 local time before rallying sharply, touching an intraday high of $705.79 to set a record. International investment banks including Goldman Sachs and Rothschild subsequently raised their target prices in unison, with the average target now around $736.17.
On the profit side, GAAP operating income for the quarter was $2.263 billion, up 17% year over year, growing faster than revenue, indicating simultaneous improvement in product mix and cost control.
Metric Amount Year-over-year growth 
Quarterly revenue $12.14 billion 9% 
GAAP operating income $2.263 billion 17% 
Adjusted operating income $2.968 billion 15% 
Note: Data from Thermo Fisher Scientific's third-quarter earnings report.
Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Marc Casper attributed the growth to the company's ongoing growth strategy and the launch of a batch of high-impact innovative products. On the product front, the company introduced the Orbitrap Isora mass spectrometer — the first Orbitrap system designed specifically for isotope ratio analysis, aimed at extending high-end mass spectrometry applications from life sciences to environmental research. In gene sequencing, it released the Ion 560 sequencing chip, with sequencing capacity nearly double that of previous products, which can improve sample throughput for genomic analysis in oncology research. Mass spectrometry and sequencing are both core tools of wet-lab work in precision medicine, and together they form one of the company's current high-growth curves.
However, as a "pick-and-shovel" supplier upstream in the pharmaceutical supply chain, Thermo Fisher's largest revenue source remains laboratory products such as consumables, culture media and single-use bioprocessing, which account for as much as 52% of total revenue. The company explained its business logic at its 2024 investor day: a long-accumulated installed base of instruments will continue to drive consumables purchases, and consumables and services are the core components of revenue.
AI push extends from instruments to the clinical side 
Artificial intelligence has been the area the company has focused on most over the past two years. The third-quarter report disclosed that the company has opened its first AI automation innovation center in South Korea, integrating analytical technology, automation and AI to help customers shorten R&D cycles. Management said AI technology has been used in cryo-electron microscopy products such as Krios 5 and Glacios 3, cutting the time required for some manual setup steps by about 90%.
In January this year, Thermo Fisher and Nvidia announced a strategic collaboration aimed at using AI to advance the evolution of scientific instruments and improve overall laboratory performance. Gianluca Pettiti, executive vice president of Thermo Fisher, said in the announcement: "AI combined with laboratory automation will reshape how research is done. We can help customers improve experimental efficiency and accuracy, extract more value from every experiment, and ultimately accelerate scientific discoveries of major value." Kimberly Powell, vice president of healthcare at Nvidia, said the industry is entering the era of "lab-in-the-loop," where AI, agents and instruments come together to scale scientific discovery at industrial speed.
The collaboration points to underlying infrastructure: building automated laboratories for customers that can connect to AI systems, supporting high-throughput experimental iteration and new drug development.
But Thermo Fisher is clearly not content to be just a pick-and-shovel supplier. The third-quarter report also disclosed the Precure research initiative jointly launched with Mayo Clinic. The project will integrate longitudinal clinical sample data from more than one million patients and conduct multi-omics research relying on Orbitrap mass spectrometry and the Olink proteomics platform to capture biological signals in the early stages of disease, connecting molecular markers to real-world patient clinical phenotypes and serving early disease screening, target discovery and diagnostic solution development.
On merger integration, Casper provided an update on Clario: the business is operating smoothly, integration is proceeding as expected, revenue synergies are gradually being released, and the company will subsequently fold Clario's capabilities into its own clinical development services system. Clario is a leading global provider of clinical trial endpoint evidence services, covering digital endpoint solutions such as centralized blinded imaging review, patient outcome data collection and cardiac safety assessment. In March this year, Thermo Fisher completed its acquisition of Clario for $8.875 billion, aiming to extend its capabilities from the wet lab to the clinical side and form a closed loop.
Competitive focus shifts toward the clinical stage 
At the industry level, the competitive focus of global innovative drug R&D is extending from front-end target discovery to the clinical stage, and the combination of AI and real-world data has become the latest battleground. On Oct. 20, Oracle and AstraZeneca announced a collaboration to explore the use of AI and real-world data to identify patients eligible for clinical trials, accelerate medical evidence generation and embed research results into daily clinical workflows. On Oct. 8, AI healthcare company Tempus AI announced multi-year collaborations with Moderna and MSD, under which Tempus will handle tumor sample collection, NGS sequencing and patient molecular typing to screen subjects suitable for therapies, supporting vaccine development and commercialization.
Brokerage views point in the same direction. AVIC Securities believes that from a commercialization perspective, the main constraint on healthcare AI is shifting from model capability to clinical evidence and system integration capacity, and companies able to connect data, models, workflows, physician confirmation and continuous monitoring are more likely to form replicable delivery models. Orient Securities said the real bottleneck in new drug R&D lies in finding a biological mechanism whose intervention can change the course of a patient's disease; AI represented by virtual cells and virtual humans is expected to solve this problem — AI finds mechanisms that hold true in both human and cellular data, achieving a correct closed loop in drugmaking and growing stronger with each iteration, ultimately bringing a systemic restructuring of R&D productivity and turning drug discovery from a craft highly dependent on individual scientists' intuition into a scalable, iterable and predictable industrial process.
For investors, Thermo Fisher's valuation support is shifting from the stable cash flow of "instruments + consumables" to a growth narrative of "AI-automated laboratories + clinical data services." If the dry-wet loop and clinical-side integration land smoothly, the company is expected to occupy a more forward position in pharmaceutical customers' R&D outsourcing chain. However, AI-related revenue has not yet been disclosed separately, and the pace of scaling the clinical data business, as well as integration costs after large acquisitions, remain key variables that subsequent earnings reports will need to verify.

Graco’s ETM and ABB Partner on Motor Technology for Data Center Cooling
The partners aim to install TFM-based direct-drive systems in data centers by the end of 2029, targeting reliability and simpler maintenance.
October 23, 2026 
Created by Refindustry using AI 
Electric Torque Machines (ETM), a wholly owned subsidiary of Graco Inc., has signed a technology license agreement with ABB to develop motor solutions for data center cooling towers and heat rejection systems. The agreement covers ETM’s patented Transverse Flux Motor (TFM) technology and expands an existing collaboration between the companies in industrial applications.
ETM’s TFM architecture is designed for high-torque, low-speed applications requiring efficient direct-drive operation. The technology can reduce mechanical complexity and the number of drivetrain components in cooling systems, potentially simplifying maintenance and supporting reliability requirements in data center environments.
Under the agreement, ABB and ETM will develop TFM-based products for cooling towers, heat rejection equipment, and related thermal management applications. The companies are targeting their first installations in data center environments by the end of 2029.
The collaboration will include product development, application engineering, customer qualification, and market development. ABB will contribute its market reach, distribution channels, and customer relationships, while ETM will provide its motor technology.
“Our work with ETM has shown the potential of direct-drive motor systems, and we are pleased to expand that work into cooling applications where performance and uptime matter,” said Jesse Henson, President, NEMA Motors, ABB.

content_text:
[News] Infineon and NVIDIA Expand GaN Power Collaboration for AI Data Centers
2026-10-23 
Emerging Technologies 
editor 
On October 21, Infineon Technologies announced an expanded collaboration with NVIDIA in AI data center power delivery during NVIDIA’s GTC developer conference in Berlin. The two companies will jointly develop high-voltage intermediate bus converter (IBC) solutions based on gallium nitride (GaN) power devices for 800V direct current (800V DC) architectures.
The expanded collaboration builds on the companies’ 800V DC power delivery initiative launched in 2025. It focuses on power conversion for high-power AI racks and will also support hot-swappable server rack maintenance.
The high-voltage IBC is a key component in the AI data center power delivery chain. Leveraging its CoolGaN product portfolio, Infineon will address multiple conversion configurations, including 800V-to-50V and 800V-to-12V, using high-frequency switching technology. The solutions are intended for NVIDIA’s MGX open modular reference architecture for AI factories.
The power architecture is designed for AI computing systems with power consumption of up to 1 MW per rack, with deployment expected to begin gradually in 2027.
Infineon and NVIDIA first announced their collaboration on 800V DC data center power delivery in May 2025. The initial initiative covered both silicon carbide (SiC) and GaN technologies.
The latest expansion places greater emphasis on GaN for intermediate bus conversion. The solutions aim to increase power density, reduce power losses across the delivery chain, and lower cooling hardware requirements. They are also designed to enable controlled pre-charging and discharging of server motherboards, as well as hot-swapping while the rack remains operational, helping reduce the risk of service disruptions during data center maintenance.
Beyond GaN-based IBCs, Infineon is supplying SiC devices, power protection components, and other power products for NVIDIA’s 800V DC ecosystem, covering the power delivery chain from the grid to AI processors.
NVIDIA’s 800V DC architecture is intended to simplify the multiple AC-to-DC and DC-to-DC conversion stages used in conventional data centers, reducing the number of conversion stages and associated components.
The ecosystem brings together power semiconductor suppliers, power system manufacturers, and data center infrastructure providers. Infineon is among the suppliers participating in the ecosystem with portfolios spanning SiC, GaN, and silicon-based power devices.

content_text:
Correction: Norsk Hydro: Solid results and strong performance
October 23, 2026 04:22 ET 
  | Source:
Norsk Hydro 
Norsk Hydro 
Hydro’s adjusted EBITDA for the third quarter of 2026 was NOK 9,089 million, up from NOK 5,996 million in the same quarter last year. Higher all-in metal prices and higher alumina prices contributed positively in the quarter, along with improved earnings in Recycling and Extrusions. The strong performance was partially offset by higher anode and energy costs in Aluminium Metal, increased energy costs in Bauxite & Alumina due to gas supply disruptions, a stronger NOK vs USD, and negative price area differences in Energy.
Alunorte resumed regular operations following temporary gas supply disruptions 
Free cash flow of NOK 1.4 billion impacted by higher metal prices and associated working capital requirements and prepayments
First metal produced at HalZero test facility, marking important milestone for carbon-free technology track
Commercial momentum continues for Hydro's low-carbon and recycled aluminium portfolio
New PPAs secured, further strengthening Hydro's long-term power position
Hydro delivered strong profitability in the quarter, with adjusted earnings per share increasing from NOK 1.0 in the third quarter of 2025, to NOK 2.3 in the third quarter of 2026. Free cash flow was NOK 1.4 billion, as strong adjusted EBITDA was partly offset by higher net operating capital, primarily driven by increased metal prices and associated working capital requirements and prepayments. While this development reflects the current market environment, improving cash conversion and working capital efficiency remains a clear priority going forward. Consequently, Hydro has updated its year-end capex guiding to around NOK 12.5 billion, down from NOK 13.5 billion, and net working capital guiding to around NOK 32 billion, up from NOK 30 billion. The twelve month adjusted RoaCE ended at 12.5 percent.
“Hydro’s third quarter results reflect strong operational performance amplified by market tailwinds. Record high liquid metal production from our Norwegian smelter system, combined with strong pricing throughout the quarter drove solid earnings and strong profitability. Operational excellence enables us to capture more of the upside when markets are strong and, more importantly, builds resilience when markets turn,” says Eivind Kallevik, President and CEO of Hydro. 
During the third quarter, disruption in natural gas supplies to Alunorte temporarily reduced production at the refinery. Through mitigating actions, including securing alternative LNG supply, Hydro maintained operational continuity and successfully restored alumina production.
Aluminium Metal benefited from higher all-in metal prices and strong operational performance, while Recycling and Extrusions delivered improved earnings supported by strong recycling margins. Hydro's Norwegian smelters increased liquid metal production to record levels, reinforcing Hydro's position as a reliable supplier of low-carbon aluminium to European customers.
In parallel, Hydro experienced continued momentum for its low-carbon and recycled products, with leading brands like CHANEL Fragrances and Beauty, General Motors, and Mercedes-Benz integrating Hydro’s solutions in their product lines.
“We continue to see strong demand for our low-carbon and recycled offerings from some of the world’s leading consumer brands. When brands like CHANEL Fragrances and Beauty and Mercedes-Benz choose Hydro, they place their trust in our quality, reliability, and ability to help them achieve their ambitions. That trust has commercial value and reinforces our confidence in the long-term opportunities for low-carbon and recycled aluminium,” says Kallevik. 
Hydro reached an important milestone in the development of its HalZero technology by producing aluminium for the first time, demonstrating the core electrolysis technology beyond laboratory scale. The achievement marks an important step toward Hydro’s long-term ambition of eliminating emissions from electrolysis and anode production. Further testing, piloting and technology development remain before any potential industrial application. Enova awarded NOK 82 million in funding to support the concept development and planning of an industrial concept pilot.
“This is an important milestone and a significant step forward in the development of HalZero. Producing the first metal demonstrates that the electrolysis technology works and paves the way for the continued development of a game changing technology with the potential to enable emission-free aluminium production in the future,” says Kallevik . 
During the quarter, Slovalco began the restart of primary aluminium production following the agreement announced in July on long-term framework conditions with the Slovak government. The restart commenced in late August, marking the return of capacity curtailed during the European energy crisis in 2022. The first phase targets an annual production capacity of 75,000 tonnes by the end of February 2027. The restart reflects the importance of competitive power, predictable regulatory frameworks, and effective industrial policy in maintaining and rebuilding Europe's industrial base.
Results and market development per business area 
Adjusted EBITDA for Bauxite & Alumina decreased compared to the third quarter of last year, to NOK 283 million from NOK 1,290 million, mainly driven by lower alumina sales prices, natural gas supply disruptions resulting in higher LNG sourcing costs and unfavourable BRL/USD exchange rate effects.This was partly offset by lower raw material costs and lower fixed costs.
PAX traded up throughout the third quarter 2026 to USD 370 per mt at the end on the quarter, diverging from Chinese alumina prices moving down. Despite lower alumina production at certain refineries in Indonesia because of raw material supply challenges, the World ex-China alumina market was oversupplied in the quarter. China's alumina market became increasingly oversupplied during the quarter as new refinery capacity came on line. Chinese alumina prices were close to the marginal cash production cost. Approximately half of China’s alumina production depends on bauxite imported from Guinea. The government of Guinea is considering the possibility of restricting annual bauxite exports volume, but no formal announcement has been made.
Adjusted EBITDA for Energy decreased in the third quarter compared to the same period last year, to NOK 411 million from NOK 828 million. The decrease is mainly due to a loss on price area differences compared to a gain in the same period last year.
Average Nordic power prices increased in the third quarter compared with both the previous quarter and the same quarter last year. The increase was mainly driven by weak hydrological conditions and higher power prices in Continental Europe. Price area differences between the south and north of the Nordic market were above the previous quarter and below the same period last year. The price difference between central Norway and northern Sweden widened significantly compared with both the previous quarter and the same quarter last year.
The Nordic hydrological balance at the end of the quarter was 13 TWh below normal, compared to 15 TWh below normal at the end of last quarter and 1 TWh below normal at the same time last year. Norwegian hydropower reservoirs were around 67.8 percent of full capacity at the end of the quarter, which is below the normal for this time of year of 82.8 percent. The distribution was uneven, with lower than normal levels in the southern and central Norway, and higher than normal levels in the north.
Adjusted EBITDA for Aluminium Metal increased in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025, to NOK 7,031 million from NOK 2,732 million, due to higher all-in metal prices, partly offset by lower sales volume, higher energy and carbon cost, and weaker USD to NOK. Global primary aluminium consumption was slightly higher compared to the third quarter of 2025, driven by a 3.0 percent increase in Asia. Primary consumption in the World ex. China is estimated to be down compared to the third quarter of 2025. The Middle East crisis continued to affect the aluminium market and prices during the third quarter. Following indications that the conflict might be nearing an end at the end of the second quarter, tensions increased again in the third quarter, directly contributing to higher aluminium prices. Throughout the quarter the market traded in a range between USD 3,100 per mt and USD 3,300 per mt. Consequently, the three month aluminium price increased slightly throughout the third quarter of 2026, starting the quarter at USD 3,076 per mt and ending at USD 3,170 per mt. 
Adjusted EBITDA for Metal Markets decreased in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same period last year, to NOK 125 million from NOK 154 million, due to lower results from sourcing and trading activities, partly offset by higher results from recyclers.
Adjusted EBITDA for Extrusions increased in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same quarter last year, to NOK 1,189 million from NOK 1,107 million, driven by higher recycling margins in combination with increased sales volume, partly offset by higher maintenance cost, higher SG&A cost and negative currency effects mainly from stronger NOK/USD.
CRU estimates that European extrusion demand increased by 1 percent in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same quarter last year, following weaker market conditions in the first half of the year. Automotive demand remained positive, supported by continued growth in battery electric vehicle production. Non-automotive transportation also turned positive after a weak start to the year, while building and construction remained broadly stable in the quarter.
CRU estimates that North American extrusion demand remained broadly unchanged in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same quarter last year, following a decline in the first half of the year. Commercial transportation continued to grow, supported by improving truckload rates, with further growth expected going forward. The industrial segment also remained solid, supported in part by continued datacenter investments. Automotive demand remained subdued, reflecting persistent headwinds in electric vehicle production.
Other key financials 
Compared to the second quarter of 2026, Hydro’s adjusted EBITDA increased to NOK 9,089 million from NOK 8,923 million, mainly due to higher all-in metal and alumina prices and lower fixed costs in the third quarter of the year. This was partially offset by higher energy costs in Bauxite & Alumina due to gas supply disruptions and seasonally lower Extrusion volumes and margins.
Net income (loss) amounted to NOK 5,263 million in the third quarter of 2026. Net income (loss) included unrealized derivative losses, mainly on LME related contracts of NOK 204 million, environmental cost of NOK 111 million, rationalization charges and closure costs of NOK 81 million, and impairment charges on fixed assets of NOK 70 million. The tax effect on these adjustments reflected a standardized tax rate for taxable gains and tax deductible losses. Adjusted net income (loss) for the first quarter ended at NOK 4,372 million.
Hydro’s net debt decreased from NOK 16.3 billion to NOK 15.4 billion during the third quarter of 2026. The net debt decrease was mainly due to positive EBITDA contributions, partially offset by net operating capital build, investments and negative other operating cash flow.
Adjusted net debt decreased from NOK 22.8 billion to NOK 21.9 billion, mainly driven by the decrease in net debt.
Reported earnings before financial items and tax (EBIT), and net income include effects that are disclosed in the quarterly report. Adjustments to EBITDA, EBIT, and net income (loss) are defined and described as part of the alternative performance measures (APM) section in the quarterly report.

Applied Materials Korea President Park Kwang-sun Receives Industrial Service Medal
Award recognizes contributions to South Korea's semiconductor competitiveness
Lee Jun

Park Kwang-sun, president of Applied Materials Korea, poses for a commemorative photo at the 19th Semiconductor Day ceremony held at the Grand InterContinental Seoul Parnas in Gangnam, Seoul, on Oct. 21. (Photo: Applied Materials Korea) 
Applied Materials Korea received an Industrial Service Medal in recognition of its contributions to strengthening South Korea's semiconductor industry competitiveness.
Park Kwang-sun, president of Applied Materials Korea, received the medal at the 19th Semiconductor Day ceremony held at the Grand InterContinental Seoul Parnas in Gangnam, Seoul, on Oct. 21.
Applied Materials Korea said the award recognized its efforts to expand the global technology innovation ecosystem and strengthen collaboration on next-generation semiconductor research and development (R&D). Park has promoted cooperation among domestic customers and suppliers and led efforts to build industry networks.
Applied Materials Korea is establishing the Applied Collaboration Center Korea in Osan, Gyeonggi Province, as a regional hub. The center will expand collaboration with major domestic customers and suppliers, supporting activities from early-stage R&D to mass-production validation. It aims to develop local talent and strengthen the competitiveness of South Korea's semiconductor ecosystem.
The company also invests in domestic startups. Applied Materials Korea works with approximately 100 local suppliers. It has established a $50 million fund with Korea Venture Investment Corp. (KVIC) to support promising domestic startups. The company also organizes technology symposiums and site visit programs for university students and provides semiconductor simulation software to university research laboratories.
Semiconductor Day was established by the Korea Semiconductor Industry Association in 2008. Each year, the association recognizes individuals who have contributed to strengthening the competitiveness of South Korea's semiconductor industry.

content_text:
Renishaw says first-quarter revenue jumped 47% to a record £251.8 million on chip and defence demand
Proactive 
22 October 2026 2 min read 
RSW.L 
Renishaw says first-quarter revenue jumped 47% to a record £251.8 million on chip and defence demand Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock Renishaw PLC (LSE:RSW) , the precision measuring and manufacturing systems maker, reported revenue of £251.8 million for the three months to 30 September, up 47% from £170.8 million a year earlier, or 48% at constant exchange rates. 
Revenue was 3% above the final quarter of the previous financial year, following a weak comparison a year earlier. 
At constant exchange rates, which exclude forward contract gains and losses and adjust for currency movements, revenue rose 48%, with all three business segments and all three regions recording year-on-year growth. 
Position Measurement revenue rose 84% to £96.0 million, driven by strong demand for optical and laser encoders used in semiconductor manufacturing equipment. 
Renishaw is investing in additional production capacity for those product lines, and its order book expanded further during the quarter. 
Industrial Metrology revenue rose 28% to £130.8 million, supported by demand for 5-axis co-ordinate measuring machines and shop-floor gauging systems, while its order book grew. 
Specialised Technologies revenue rose 50% to £25.0 million, led by additive manufacturing systems for customers in the aerospace, defence and medical sectors. 
Revenue in the segment was lower than in the exceptionally strong final quarter of the previous financial year, although its order book strengthened. 
The divestment process for the company's neurological business is continuing, while spectroscopy revenue was marginally lower than a year earlier, although its order book strengthened. 
Renishaw expects strong progress in revenue and operating margin for the 2027 financial year as a whole. 
It said it was working to scale up its supply chain and production capacity while remaining mindful of the cyclical nature of demand over the medium term.

content_text:
Sumitomo Chemical deepens India semiconductor push with Tata Electronics pact 
Sumitomo Chemical has signed an MoU with Tata Electronics to explore collaboration in semiconductor fabrication and materials supply, including a possible chemicals facility in India. The move reflects growing interest from upstream suppliers in India’s chip ambitions, where reliable access to high-purity chemicals and photoresists could shape future manufacturing capacity. 
ETChemicals 
Published On Oct 21, 2026 at 12:04 PM IST
Read by 2863 Professionals
Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook 
Bookmark 
India’s semiconductor ambitions are increasingly drawing in global materials suppliers, not just chip designers and fabricators. In a move that underlines that shift, Sumitomo Chemical has signed a memorandum of understanding with Tata Electronics to examine a possible collaboration in semiconductor fabrication and the supporting supply chain , according to specchemonline.com . 
The agreement is significant because semiconductor manufacturing depends on a tightly controlled ecosystem of chemicals, photoresists and high-purity inputs. Any serious effort to localise chip production in India will need those upstream materials to be available reliably, at scale and with consistent quality. That is the business opportunity Sumitomo Chemical appears to be targeting through the Tata partnership. 
What the agreement is meant to cover 
The companies plan to study specific steps that could help create a stable materials supply system for semiconductor manufacturing. One possibility being explored is the establishment of a semiconductor chemicals facility in India, which would give the Japanese supplier a local foothold in a market that is still building out its chip ecosystem. 
The MoU does not amount to a final investment decision, but it signals intent. For Tata Electronics , which is building its semiconductor ambitions in India, a dependable materials partner could be as important as equipment, talent and policy support. For Sumitomo Chemical, the arrangement offers a way to align with a customer base that may grow as India pushes harder into advanced electronics manufacturing. 
Why materials matter more than ever 
Semiconductor fabrication is often discussed through the lens of fabs, foundries and government incentives, but the industry is equally dependent on specialist materials. Photoresists and high-purity chemicals are essential in the patterning and processing steps that allow chips to be manufactured at advanced nodes. Supply disruptions in these inputs can quickly ripple through production schedules and yield outcomes. 
That is why localisation efforts are increasingly extending beyond assembly and packaging. Countries seeking to build semiconductor resilience are now looking at the full stack, including the chemicals that enable chipmaking in the first place. A domestic or regional supply base can reduce logistics risk, shorten lead times and improve control over quality assurance. 
Sumitomo Chemical is betting on semiconductor growth 
The semiconductor materials business has been positioned as a priority inside Sumitomo Chemical’s ICT and Mobility Solutions segment, which the Japanese group views as one of its growth engines. The company has built a reputation in advanced photoresists and semiconductor chemicals, particularly high-purity products used in demanding fabrication environments. 
Over the past few years, the company has expanded semiconductor chemicals capacity in Japan and South Korea while also setting up a new base in Texas. Earlier this year, it acquired Asia Union Electronic Chemical , which operates facilities in Taiwan and Nevada. The company has also started work at advanced high-purity chemical centres in Japan and South Korea, where it is developing new processes and recycling technologies. 
That sequence of investments suggests a broader strategy: deepen presence in major semiconductor geographies while improving supply resilience and technical capabilities. The India move fits that pattern, especially as chip manufacturing becomes more geographically diversified in response to geopolitical and supply chain concerns. 
India’s chip ecosystem is attracting upstream players 
India has spent the past few years trying to move from policy ambition to industrial execution in semiconductors . The country’s appeal is no longer limited to final-stage electronics assembly. Global suppliers are beginning to evaluate whether India can support the specialised materials and process infrastructure needed for chip fabrication. 
That shift matters because semiconductor projects are rarely built in isolation. A viable ecosystem requires chemical suppliers, gas suppliers, wafer handling, cleanroom services, logistics providers and a skilled technical workforce. The presence of a company such as Sumitomo Chemical would be a signal that India is moving closer to that broader industrial base. 
For Tata Electronics, the partnership could help strengthen its supply chain planning at a time when semiconductor manufacturing is becoming a strategic priority for large industrial groups in India. For Sumitomo Chemical, the arrangement could open a pathway into a market that combines scale potential with policy support for electronics manufacturing. 
Regional competition is also intensifying 
The India discussion comes as Japanese chemical companies continue to expand in other Asian semiconductor hubs. Another Japanese player, Nissan Chemical , has separately set up a wholly owned subsidiary in Zhangjiagang in Jiangsu province, China. That unit will manufacture anti-reflective coatings used in photoresists and multilayer semiconductor materials. 
Nissan Chemical has said demand for semiconductors in China has continued to rise, helped by digitalisation and other structural factors, while customers are also seeking more resilient supply chains. The parallel expansion by Japanese suppliers in China and India highlights a broader industry trend: materials companies are following chip manufacturing demand wherever it is likely to concentrate next. 
For India, the challenge will be to convert interest into durable industrial capacity. A materials facility, if it goes ahead, would not by itself create a complete semiconductor supply chain. But it would be an important marker of confidence, showing that upstream global suppliers are willing to commit capital and know-how to the country’s chip ambitions. 
The Tata Electronics tie-up therefore sits at the intersection of manufacturing policy, supply chain resilience and long-term industrial strategy. If the exploratory talks lead to a concrete project, it could become one of the more telling examples of how India’s semiconductor push is beginning to draw in the chemicals businesses that underpin the sector’s real economics.

Merck opens Korean chip materials plant to meet advanced memory demand
Published : Oct. 22, 2026 - 10:27:43
Add The Korea Herald on Google
Link copied!
Moon Joon-hyun 
Tech Reporter
Covers Korean companies at the center of global chips, AI and consumer technology, from Samsung and SK hynix to Apple suppliers
Subscribe + 
Merck Electronics CEO sees Korea as key market as company braces for potential doubling of chip materials demand
Benjamin Hein, CEO of Merck's Electronics business, speaks during a press conference in Seoul on Wednesday. (Merck Korea) 
German science and technology company Merck opened a new semiconductor materials plant in South Korea on Thursday, expanding local production of molybdenum as chipmakers adopt the metal for increasingly advanced memory chips.
The facility in Eumseong, North Chungcheong Province, will produce molybdenum dioxide dichloride, a chemical used to deposit ultrathin metal films during chip manufacturing. It will supply customers in Korea and elsewhere in Asia.
Benjamin Hein, CEO of Merck's Electronics business, described Korea as among the top three markets for semiconductor materials during a press conference in Seoul on Wednesday.
"What if the demand for semiconductor materials and solutions doubles within the next five years? Are we ready? We want to be ready," Hein said.
The plant will initially focus on materials for advanced 3D NAND flash memory, which increases storage capacity by stacking memory cells vertically.
Merck's Eumseong plant in North Chungcheong Province, where the German company opened a new molybdenum production facility for advanced semiconductor manufacturing on Thursday (Merck Korea) 
Samsung Electronics began using molybdenum in its ninth-generation V-NAND in 2024, while SK hynix has reportedly been preparing to introduce the metal in its next-generation 375-layer NAND.
Molybdenum offers an alternative to tungsten, whose electrical resistance becomes increasingly problematic as chipmakers shrink components and stack more layers. It can also reduce the need for barrier films that occupy valuable space inside microscopic structures.
Bing Han, executive vice president and head of Merck's Thin Films business, said adoption was beginning with NAND, with DRAM and logic chips expected to follow. "Eventually more of the smaller features will all move to Moly," Han said, while acknowledging that the pace of adoption depends on individual customers.
Merck will combine precursor production in Eumseong with chemical delivery systems manufactured at its Ansan facility in Gyeonggi Province. The company says the integrated system can use more than 99 percent of the material loaded into its containers, potentially reducing waste and manufacturing costs.
"Local for local is everything," Han said. "You can have the best offering, but you have to have your best offering in the right location."
The expansion forms part of Merck's 600 million euro ($674 million) investment program announced in 2021. Merck disclosed plans for the molybdenum facility in February, but declined to reveal its investment cost or production capacity.
Hein also identified advanced packaging, which combines multiple chips into increasingly complex systems, as another growth area. He said manufacturers face an immediate shortage of packaging capacity, with further technological changes expected over the next three to five years.
"On advanced packaging, short term, there is simply not enough capacity," he said. "So on the immediate, it is about debottlenecking."

The chemical company is working to expand and scale the R&D and manufacturing of its Expanded Beam Optical products, which it expects will generate $40 million by the end of 2026.

3M has reached agreements with Amazon Web Services and Genius Electronic Optical Co. to scale manufacturing and research and development of its expanded beam optical interconnect technology used within AI data centers.
Courtesy of 3M
Listen to the article
4 min 
This audio is auto-generated. Please let us know if you have feedback .
3M reached two agreements to scale manufacturing and research and development of its expanded beam optical interconnect products, the company announced this week . 
The effort will come through an expanded collaboration with Amazon Web Services and a formed partnership with Taiwan-based Genius Electronic Optical Co., the chemical maker said. 
The deals build on 3M’s strategy to invest an undisclosed amount toward expanding its EBO manufacturing capacity that it announced in March. The plan includes adding manufacturing equipment and production space to meet the global demand for high-speed interconnects in artificial intelligence data centers. 
3M anticipates EBO portfolio revenue in the $40 million range in 2026 and expects it to increase “considerably” next year between $80 million and $100 million, CEO and Chairman Bill Brown said during 3M’s third-quarter earnings call on Tuesday. 
The company has doubled its EBO manufacturing capacity to a little over 10 million ferrules per year, which Brown said will increase over time. 
3M is part of an alliance focused on advancing an open, interoperable specification for EBO connectivity products in the AI end-market called the Expanded Beam Optics Multi-Source Agreement Group . The MSA seeks to streamline EBO connectors for wide-scale adoption, according to the website. It also assists in connecting vendors with the supply industry. 
3M joined the MSA in May and as of Oct. 15, the group has 63 members, including Microsoft, AMD, Foxconn, Nvidia, Oracle and Meta. 
3M teamed up with MSA member Microsoft in July to collaborate on AI data center infrastructure and transforming enterprise technologies. 
Amazon Web Services 
AWS plans to deploy and ramp up 3M’s EBO platform for its data center infrastructure, according to a press release on Thursday . 
The two companies will collaborate to develop data-transfer technologies and critical infrastructure required for artificial intelligence. 
3M issued AWS a call warrant to buy up to about 3.2 million of the chemical maker’s shares at a purchase price of $164.89 over seven years, according to an Oct. 19 securities filing . 
Amazon will gain full ownership of a certain number of shares once “sales of optical connectivity and other data-center related products” reach $6 billion, Brown said. The securities filing said the remaining warrant shares will be subject to reaching certain goalposts. 
The partnership and related investments are expected to support over 500 direct and indirect jobs, and create over 100 jobs through 2027 across 3M’s operations in Minnesota, Texas and Wisconsin, according to the press release. 
The jobs will also support customer collaboration, advance technology and supply chain development across 3M’s optical networking portfolio and accelerate industry-wide EBO product adoption. 
Genius Electronic Optical 
3M’s partnership with GSEO will combine the chemical company’s optical interconnect expertise, materials science, manufacturing and customer relationships with the Taiwan-based entity’s precision optics production capabilities and scale, according to the Oct. 19 press release . 
3M and GSEO’s joint effort aims to support EBO commercialization and long-term capacity expansion to meet growing demand for data centers and other connectivity applications, according to a separate press release on Monday . 3M also plans to buy 4.7% of the Taiwan-based optical technology company’s shares, with the deal expected to close in the fourth quarter. 
GSEO’s manufacturing capabilities and technical development experience are expected to help 3M prepare its manufacturing process for its EBO ferrules connector , packaged optics, and other related optical interconnect products. 
While 3M is scaling up EBO production in-house, Brown said the company would not be able to meet market demand. GSEO has that capacity, and other manufacturing sources may help satisfy the “diversity of supply” over time, the CEO added.

WILMINGTON, N.C. (WECT) - Corning Inc. will invest $585 million at its Wilmington campus and add 414 jobs over the next five years, expanding one of the world’s largest optical fiber manufacturing plants.
The New York-based company announced the expansion Wednesday after the Wilmington City Council and New Hanover County Commissioners approved a package of incentives earlier this week to expand its operations. 
“We’re proud to expand our presence in Wilmington, where Corning made history with the world’s first optical fiber manufacturing plant and where our people continue to make the fiber that is critical to next-generation networks,” said John McGirr, senior vice president and general manager of Corning Optical Fiber and Cable.

The new jobs are expected to pay an average salary of more than $85,000 a year, and the company said the expansion will add more than $35 million in annual payroll for the region.
“Corning has been part of New Hanover County for decades, and when a company with that track record is ready to grow, this Board wants that growth to happen here,” said LeAnn Pierce, Chair of the New Hanover County Board of Commissioners. “Those are good paychecks for families in our community. The grant is tied to those jobs and that investment, and that is exactly how it should work.”
The company has maintained a civic commitment to the Wilmington area for 60 years, partnering with Cape Fear Community College on the Corning Technician Pipeline Program and investing in STEM education in local schools.
“It’s impossible to overstate how important this company is to Greater Wilmington,” said Scott Satterfield, CEO of Wilmington Business Development.

content_text:
Toray develops polyester-nylon fiber with recycled content
The company says both the polyester and nylon components of its new fiber incorporate recycled materials.
Photo courtesy of Toray 
Posted by
Chris Voloschuk, Associate Editor 
Published October 21, 2026
Listen to article 
/ 
Toray Industries Inc. recently announced it had developed a polyester-nylon fiber containing at least 93 percent recycled content by mass, based on the total weight of the raw yarn.
The Japan-based company says the percentage applies to the newly developed raw yarn and does not represent the recycled content of the finished fabric or garment. It says the breakthrough drew on technologies the company cultivated through its &+ (and plus) recycled fiber brand, adding that the polyester and nylon components of the fiber incorporate recycled materials.
Composite fibers can provide added functionality, sophisticated textures and subtle visual effects, Toray says, but combining different polymers makes it difficult to use high proportions of recycled materials while maintaining consistent quality. The company says it tapped into its expertise in polymer design and composite spinning to overcome the challenge and achieve a product containing at least 93 percent recycled content by mass, and it plans to verify the technology’s viability for mass production and continue research to increase recycled content in composite fibers.
“The fashion industry is showing increasing interest in material containing recycled content,” Toray says. “Materials for high-end and luxury applications must also deliver exceptional aesthetic qualities, including appearance, tailoring and drape, texture and durability.”
These considerations prompted Toray to create Artirosa CX, which it says incorporates the newly developed fiber. The company notes that the recycled content in each Artirosa CX fabric may vary depending on its composition.
The company says Artirosa CX features a “dense, finely textured surface and a crisp, sophisticated feel,” adding that fabric design and finishing also can impart practical properties like waterproofing, durable water repellency and wind resistance. 
“Rather than emphasizing the distinctive appearance typical of conventional functional materials, Artirosa CX refines that look into an elegant, sophisticated texture,” Toray says. “The result is a cleaner, more contemporary urban aesthetic.”
Toray says it intends to market Artirosa CX for wide-ranging applications, including men’s and women’s outerwear, urban outdoor wear and premium casual wear. The company expects to launch the product in late-2027 and is targeting initial year sales of 200,000 meters (around 218,722 yards) of material.

content_text:
Thermo Fisher posts higher third-quarter revenue and earnings as margins improve
Published: 09:04 21 Oct 2026 EDT
Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc (NYSE:TMO, XETRA:TN8) increased third-quarter revenue by 9% to $12.14 billion, while adjusted earnings per share rose 15% to $6.68.
Revenue for the three months ended September 2026 increased from $11.12 billion a year earlier, with organic revenue growth, which excludes the effects of acquisitions, disposals and currency movements, reaching 6%.
Adjusted operating income rose 15% to $2.97 billion, while adjusted operating margin increased to 24.5% from 23.3% in the same period last year.
The company’s generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) diluted earnings per share increased 9% to $4.64, while GAAP operating income rose 17% to $2.26 billion.
GAAP operating margin improved to 18.6% from 17.4%, indicating that the company retained a larger share of revenue as operating profit.
Thermo Fisher chief executive Marc Casper said the company’s growth strategy and its Practical Process Improvement (PPI) Business System supported its performance during the quarter.
The company launched several products during the period, including a mass spectrometer designed for isotope ratio analysis, an electron detector for advanced materials research and a new autoimmune screening test cleared by the US Food and Drug Administration.
Thermo Fisher also partnered with Mayo Clinic to launch Precure, an initiative combining data from more than one million patient samples with its proteomics technologies to support disease research, earlier detection and precision medicine.
In South Korea, the company opened its first artificial intelligence and automation innovation centre to help customers improve research and development productivity.
Thermo Fisher also opened a highly automated distribution centre in Kentucky to improve supply chain speed and flexibility across North America.
The company completed the previously announced sale of its microbiology business during the quarter as part of its capital deployment strategy.
Thermo Fisher said it would provide updated financial guidance for 2026 during its third-quarter earnings conference call.
Shares were down around 2% in early Wednesday morning trading.

Qualcomm boosts Korea startups and robot tech at industrial AI expo 
입력 2026.10.21. 15:31 
조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 
A view of the QAIPI Pavilion, an exhibition space Qualcomm prepares at the Industry AI Expo 2026 to showcase technology from domestic artificial intelligence (AI) startups./Courtesy of Qualcomm 
U.S. semiconductor corporation Qualcomm showcased industrial AI technology with six Korea-based artificial intelligence (AI) startups.
Qualcomm said on the 21st that it would take part in Industrial AI Expo 2026 and operate the Qualcomm AI Innovators Program (QAIPI) Pavilion, an exhibition space for Korea-based AI startups. QAIPI is a program Qualcomm launched last year to support AI technology development and commercialization by startups in the Asia-Pacific region.
This exhibition features six Korea-based startups: ENERZAi, Withrobot, Undermilli, Clica, FladLabs, which were selected for QAIPI this year, and Sagak, which was selected last year. Five partners in the industrial and embedded Internet of Things (IoT) field—ICbanQ, Sapphire Stream Technology Korea, XSLAB Incorporation, MathWorks, and OSCO—also joined.
Qualcomm is supporting participating corporations with the Qualcomm AI Hub, an AI development tool, along with technical training and mentoring. The goal is to help startups use the Qualcomm platform to develop AI services for mobile, computing, and IoT and apply them in real industrial settings.
It will also unveil technologies developed in collaboration with Korea-based robotics corporations. In the Qualcomm Robotics Zone inside the exhibition hall, Rainbow Robotics' quadruped robot equipped with Qualcomm's industrial processor Dragonwing IQ-9075 will be demonstrated. An autonomous mobile robot (AMR) from auto parts company SL Corporation will also be unveiled. The robot uses Arduino's VENTUNO Q platform.
A quadruped robot from Rainbow Robotics is on display at the Qualcomm Robotics Zone, Qualcomm's exhibition space at the Industry AI Expo 2026./Courtesy of Qualcomm 
Qualcomm is expanding high-performance, low-power computing and On-device AI technology to industrial robots and automated equipment. On-device AI is technology that processes AI computations on the device itself without relying on external servers. It can be used for robots in industrial sites that must recognize and make judgments about their surroundings in real time.
Qualcomm will also hold the QAIPI-APAC 2026 Demo Day in Tokyo, Japan, on Dec. 2. Startups from the Asia-Pacific region, including Korea, will introduce their developed technologies and business results and seek opportunities to enter global markets.
Kim Sang-pyo, president of Qualcomm Korea, said, "As AI spreads across industries, the ability to apply innovative technologies in real environments and commercialize them is becoming even more important," and added, "Qualcomm will support startups from technology development to commercialization through QAIPI, and continue cooperating so that Korea's innovative corporations can create new growth opportunities in global markets."

Wilmington council backs $2 million deal to sweeten odds of landing Corning expansion 
The Wilmington City Council voted unanimously Tuesday night to approve $2 million in incentives for Corning Inc. to expand its operations in the city. 
By Hudson Steiner 
Published : Oct. 20, 2026 at 10:20 PM EDT 
Share 
Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google 
WILMINGTON, N.C. (WECT) - The Wilmington City Council voted unanimously Tuesday night to approve $2 million in incentives for Corning Inc. to expand its operations in the city, following suit with New Hanover County.
The council’s incentive package will provide annual payments of $400,000 a year for five years. In exchange, Corning would invest $585 million and create 414 new jobs.
The vote comes one day after New Hanover County commissioners voted to offer their own incentive package during a meeting Monday, putting up to $600,000 a year for five years from the county’s general fund, which is made up of taxpayer dollars.
PREVIOUS STORY: NHC Commissioners approve incentive for Corning Inc. to expand in Wilmington 
Corning is a glass products manufacturer based in Corning, New York.
“Based in Corning, New York, this multinational technology company specializes in glass, ceramics, and related materials,” Scott Satterfield, CEO of Wilmington Business Development, said during the county’s meeting. “For over 60 years Corning has been a vital employer here.”
Corning officials told commissioners that Wilmington is one of several locations under consideration for the expansion.
If the area is selected, the project would bring new jobs with salaries averaging more than $85,000 a year, along with the $585 million capital investment.
With both the city and county incentives now approved, the combined incentive package totals $5 million. Corning officials are now left to decide whether to proceed with the Wilmington expansion or pursue alternative locations.

content_text:
METiS Enters Collaboration with Eli Lilly for Next-Generation Tissue-Specific LNP Delivery Technologies
Author(s) Nicholas Jacobus 
METiS TechBio enters a collaboration with Eli Lilly to develop next-generation, tissue-specific lipid nanoparticle delivery technologies using METiS’s AI-driven lipid discovery platform.
Advertisement
METiS TechBio announced a strategic collaboration with Eli Lilly and Company focused on researching and discovering novel lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-based delivery solutions designed to enable tissue-specific delivery of therapeutic modalities.
Under the agreement, METiS is eligible to receive an upfront payment in the low double-digit millions of dollars, upwards of approximately $1.1 billion in development, regulatory, and commercial milestone payments, and single-digit tiered royalties on annual net sales of any resulting products. 1 
What will each company contribute?
METiS is expected to apply its proprietary, AI-driven ionizable lipid discovery and optimization platform, AiLNP, to develop next-generation delivery technologies aiming at improving the targeting and biodistribution of LNP-based delivery systems. 1 Eli Lilly is set to contribute its drug discovery, development, and commercialization expertise to advance the collaboration.

Roundup: TRexBio & Retension Pharmaceuticals Announce IPO Pricing 
Roundup: Shionogi Inc. Acquires IntraBio, Gate Bioscience extends Collaboration with Eli Lilly, Alector Enters Global License Agreement with Genentech 
The companies say combining METiS’s generative and predictive AI capabilities for rational LNP design with Eli Lilly’s scientific and development infrastructure is intended to yield novel LNP architectures with improved tissue specificity, enhanced therapeutic performance, and broader applicability across multiple disease areas. 1 
Why does delivery technology matter here?
Lipid nanoparticles have become a central modality for delivering therapeutic payloads to target tissues and cells, underpinning everything from mRNA vaccines to gene-editing therapies. 2 As the industry moves into more complex modalities, the ability to direct payloads precisely to intended tissues, while minimizing off-target exposure, has become a key bottleneck in translating novel therapeutics into approved products. METiS positions AiLNP as an answer to that bottleneck, using generative AI models, including one referred to as PhatGPT, to generate and optimize lipid candidates computationally rather than through traditional trial-and-error screening. 1,2 
What is METiS saying about the deal?
METiS frames the collaboration as validation of its AI-driven approach and an opportunity to scale its platform through a partner with substantial development reach. “Delivery remains a critical determinant of therapeutic success, particularly as the industry expands into increasingly sophisticated modalities,” says Chris Lai, chairman and CEO of METiS TechBio. “We are excited to collaborate with Lilly, a global leader in the discovery and development of innovative medicines. By combining METiS’ AI-powered platform with Lilly’s scientific expertise and development capabilities, we aim to unlock a new generation of tissue-targeted delivery technologies that have the potential to transform how medicines reach patients.”
What’s next? 
Terms of the agreement were not fully disclosed, including which disease areas or specific programs the collaboration will initially target. 1 The deal adds Eli Lilly to a growing list of large pharmaceutical companies turning to AI-native biotechs for delivery innovation, as sponsors look to extend LNP technology beyond its original mRNA vaccine applications into gene therapies, RNA interference, and other emerging modalities.

query: ("Qualcomm" OR "Qualcomm Incorporated") ("press release" OR "investor relations" OR earnings OR announcement OR investment OR expansion OR acquisition OR partnership OR Korea) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
Qualcomm to Unite Regional V2X Standards Under Global V2X Solution
Highlights: Qualcomm ® V2X chipsets to support the 760 MHz ITS Connect standard utilized in Japan, further extending a globally interoperable platform across major V2X deployments worldwide. Qualcomm advances globally interoperable V2X solutions to help accelerate deployment of connected safety technologies and help reduce road fatalities. Toyota welcomes Qualcomm’s efforts to foster broader industry collaboration toward a Zero-Accident society. Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. today announced that its Qualcomm ® vehicle-to-everything (V2X) chipsets will support nearly all major regional V2X deployments worldwide through a single platform. As the latest expansion of this capability, Qualcomm V2X chipsets will support the 760 MHz ARIB-T109 standard, bringing native compatibility with Japan's V2X band alongside the 5.9 GHz band already supported. These advancements are designed to reduce the need for region-specific hardware, lower deployment complexity, and accelerate the deployment of V2X technologies that can improve safety for drivers, passengers, and vulnerable road users (VRUs), including pedestrians, cyclists, and motorcyclists. V2X is a unique component of the vehicle safety stack, providing real-time awareness of hazards beyond a vehicle's line of sight while meeting the stringent security and reliability requirements of safety-critical applications. V2X enables direct communication to detect hazards around corners, through obstacles, and beyond visible range, enhancing safety for vehicle occupants and vulnerable road users. Recognizing the potential of connected safety technologies to help reduce road incidents, Qualcomm Technologies and Toyota recognize the importance of broad industry collaboration in advancing Vision Zero, the global initiative to eliminate traffic fatalities and serious injuries through greater industry collaboration, interoperability, and adoption of connected safety technologies. Achieving this vision requires collaboration among automakers, technology providers, governments, and infrastructure stakeholders. V2X can play a critical role in advancing this vision by providing reliable real-time communication to help improve safety for all road users, enable cooperation with smart infrastructure and augment the vehicle’s advanced driver assistance system as the only non-line-of-sight sensor. Through investment in globally interoperable V2X technology, Qualcomm Technologies aims to accelerate adoption with scalable solutions that can have a positive impact on road safety in all geographies and that can support additional use cases as vehicles and transportation systems continue to evolve.   “V2X has the potential to play a transformative role in road safety, but realizing its full impact requires solutions that can scale globally and operate across regional ecosystems,” said Nakul Duggal, Executive Vice President and Group General Manager, Automotive, Industrial and Embedded IoT, and Robotics, Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. “By extending our V2X technology abstraction to support Japan's 760 MHz standard, we are helping enable more interoperable and globally deployable V2X solutions. As adoption of V2X technology continues to grow, we are taking an important step toward accelerating the deployment and advancing a shared Vision Zero goal with Toyota and other stakeholders across the industry to help eliminate road fatalities.” “Toyota welcomes Qualcomm Technologies’ efforts to foster broader industry collaboration toward a zero-accident society,” said Keiji Yamamoto, Chief Officer, Digital Information and Communication Group, Toyota Motor Corporation, and Chair of ITS Japan. “Road accidents remain a global challenge that cannot be solved by any single company, industry sector, or region alone. Eliminating traffic accidents requires the collective efforts of automakers, technology providers, governments, and infrastructure stakeholders. We highly appreciate Qualcomm Technologies’ continued investment in innovative technologies and its leadership in bringing together stakeholders across the mobility ecosystem to help advance toward zero traffic accidents and Mobility for All.”

content_text:
Can Qualcomm's PickNik Acquisition Strengthen Its Robotics Edge?
Zacks Equity Research 
October 20, 2026 2 min read 
QCOM 
+2.93% 
AMD 
+13.15% 
NVDA 
-3.54% 
AVGO 
+8.70% 
Qualcomm Incorporated QCOM is strengthening its position in the rapidly evolving robotics market through its proposed acquisition of PickNik Robotics, a developer of advanced robotics software. The transaction aligns with Qualcomm's strategy to expand its footprint in physical artificial intelligence (AI), edge computing and intelligent robotics.
PickNik is recognized for its stewardship of MoveIt, a widely adopted open-source robotics manipulation framework built on the Robot Operating System (ROS). The platform supports motion planning, manipulation and robotic control across industrial automation, service robotics and emerging physical AI applications. The transaction, subject to customary closing conditions, could strengthen Qualcomm's ability to offer integrated hardware and software solutions. 
Transaction Rationale 
The buyout is expected to enhance Qualcomm's Dragonwing Robotics platforms by integrating MoveIt and PickNik's commercial MoveIt Pro software. This combination could enable developers to leverage Qualcomm's AI processing, connectivity and heterogeneous computing capabilities alongside advanced motion planning and real-time robotic control.
The integration is also expected to extend to Arduino platforms, beginning with VENTUNO Q boards. This could make advanced robotics development more accessible to a broader developer community while accelerating the transition from prototypes to commercial deployments.
Importantly, Qualcomm intends to maintain MoveIt as an open-source framework supporting third-party hardware. This approach could encourage wider ecosystem participation and strengthen developer engagement, potentially boosting adoption of its Dragonwing platforms. 
Physical AI Opportunities Support Long-Term Diversification 
The planned acquisition complements Qualcomm's broader efforts to diversify beyond smartphones into automotive, industrial IoT and edge AI markets. Its March 2026 collaboration with NEURA Robotics to advance cognitive robotics and humanoid applications further underscores its growing focus on physical AI.
Combining PickNik's software expertise with Qualcomm's power-efficient computing capabilities could improve its competitive positioning as demand for intelligent automation increases across industrial and commercial applications.
However, the acquisition's financial terms remain undisclosed, limiting visibility into its immediate earnings contribution. Integration challenges, competition in robotics computing and uncertain commercialization timelines could also constrain near-term benefits. Stiff competition from NVIDIA Corporation NVDA, Broadcom Inc. AVGO and Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. AMD further strains its margins.
Nevertheless, PickNik's established developer ecosystem and robotics software capabilities could help Qualcomm expand its addressable market and deepen customer engagement. Successful integration may strengthen QCOM's position in next-generation robotics while supporting its long-term diversification strategy.

Arkema Inaugurates New Acrylic Acid Purification Unit 
Arkema has opened a new acrylic acid purification unit at its Carling production site in France, deploying a new process that improves energy efficiency by 25 % and reduces carbon intensity by 20 %. The EUR 150 million investment is part of the company’s broader decarbonisation programme . 
20 October 2026 
Arkema

Save in bookmarks 
Arkema's new acrylic acid purification unit at the Carling site in France marks a significant step in the company's decarbonisation investment programme. 
Source: Arkema 
Advertisement:
Arkema has inaugurated a new acrylic acid purification unit at its Carling site in Saint-Avold, France. The unit operates on a new process and is located at one of Europe’s major acrylic monomer production facilities. Carling produces acrylic monomers used in performance coatings, adhesives, water treatment, and other advanced materials. 
According to Arkema, the new unit improves the energy efficiency of the purification process by 25 % and reduces the carbon intensity of site operations by 20 %. The company also states that the new technology optimises resource and waste management and significantly reduces solvent consumption. Arkema describes the investment as placing the Carling plant among reference sites in the industry, aligned with the highest operational and environmental standards. 
EUR 150 Million Investment Targets Decarbonisation of European Acrylic Production 
The project was decided in 2023 and was partly funded by the French State through the France 2030 programme, operated by ADEME and funded by the European Union via NextGenerationEU. Thierry Le Hénaff, chairman and chief executive officer of Arkema, commented: “With an investment of nearly €150 million, this new unit represents one of Arkema’s largest industrial projects in France. It will contribute to the Group’s ambitious climate plan, underpinned by a dedicated investment program supporting Arkema’s decarbonization, with a cumulative amount that could reach €400 million over the 2022-2030 period.” 
The inauguration ceremony was attended by Le Hénaff and Stéphane Séjourné, executive vice-president of the European Commission for Prosperity and Industrial Strategy. The event was held on the same day as the Critical Chemicals Alliance General Assembly, which brought together European industrial leaders and policymakers to address challenges related to sovereignty, competitiveness, and decarbonisation. 
European Industrial Policy and the Role of Low-Carbon Acrylic Materials 
Séjourné underlined the broader political significance of the investment: “Europe must keep its chemical industry. There can be neither industrial sovereignty nor strategic autonomy if we allow the essential building blocks of our economy to leave. Carling is showing the way forward: nearly EUR 150 million invested to produce in Europe, using less energy and generating less carbon, while building on decades of industrial know-how. This is exactly the model we want to promote: decarbonizing without deindustrializing, investing in our regions, and making our industrial hubs the driving forces of our future.” 
Arkema states that the unit is part of its decarbonisation investment programme and supports what the company describes as its ambitious climate plan. The company adds that the investment strengthens its position in the low-carbon acrylic materials market in Europe.

title: HyProMag USA deploys third mobile system - Recycling Today

content_text:
HyProMag USA deploys third mobile system
Several technology and recycling firms in the United States and Canada have collaborated to invest in mobile systems to process printed circuit boards and hard drives.
“The deployment of our third Inserma system as a mobile processing unit represents an important step in the development of the Dallas-Fort Worth project,” says Julian Treger, CEO of CoTec Holdings.
Photo courtesy of Intelligent Lifecycle Solutions 
By
Brian Taylor, Senior Editor 
Published October 20, 2026
Listen to article 
/ 
A coalition of firms in the United States and Canada, some with ownership stakes in each other, have now deployed three mobile hard disk drive (HDD) separation system designed to recover rare earth element (REE) and magnet materials from discarded electronic components.
Canada-based Mkango Magnetic Materials Ltd. says HyProMag USA LLC, in which it owns a stake, has announced the deployment of its third Spanish-made Inserma Anoia S.L. HDD separation system to be used as a mobile processing unit, “expanding HyProMag USA’s processing and customer engagement capabilities across the U.S.”
Adds Mkango, “The deployment further strengthens HyProMag USA’s partnership with Intelligent Lifecycle Solutions (ILS) and supports the expansion of a scalable nationwide platform for the recovery and recycling of rare earth magnets from end-of-life HDDs.”
ILS is based in Nevada and has processing capacity there and in South Carolina, according to Mkango.
Also involved is HyProMag USA co-owner CoTec Holdings Corp., a Canada-based firm that says it “integrates breakthrough technologies with strategic assets to unlock secure, sustainable, and low-cost supply chains.” 
Mkango says feedstock inventories currently under contract and in storage, together with active procurement programs undertaken by the companies involved, “continue to strengthen the feedstock platform and are expected to support initial commissioning and ramp-up activities” at a planned HyProMag USA Texas Hub facility in the Dallas-Fort Worth scheduled to open in 2028.
The Canadian company says Delaware-based HyProMag USA also has completed commercial sales of recovered printed circuit board (PCB) material to downstream smelter partners, generating revenue that supports the acquisition and retention of magnet-bearing feedstock inventory.
“The deployment of our third Inserma system as a mobile processing unit represents an important step in the development of the Dallas-Fort Worth project,” says Julian Treger, CEO of CoTec Holdings.
“Together with continued progress in feedstock sourcing and commercial PCB recovery, it strengthens our operating platform and expands our ability to engage directly with customers across multiple end markets,” adds Treger.
Remars Graham Davy, Managing Director of ILS , “The focus of the ILS team has been on demonstrating that HDDs can be efficiently processed into separate, marketable material streams. The mobile unit allows us to work directly with customers at their facilities, supporting trial programs, demonstrating material recovery performance and creating opportunities to secure additional feedstock supply.”
The companies say they are tapping into diversified feedstock channels “across industrial, health care, government and IT asset disposition sectors.”
