Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook 
Bookmark 
A logo of Applied Materials (reprsentative image) NEW DELHI: Materials engineering major Applied Materials on Thursday announced a collaboration with Intel Corporation to accelerate the development of chipmaking innovations for next-generation transistors, interconnects, and advanced packaging technologies . 
The joint effort brings together capabilities from Applied's EPIC Center in Silicon Valley and Intel's R&D campus in Hillsboro, Oregon, to shorten time-to-market for advanced semiconductor technologies essential to artificial intelligence computing. 
"Applied and Intel share a decades-long history of deep collaboration focused on pushing the boundaries of materials engineering to advance the semiconductor roadmap," said Gary Dickerson, president and CEO of Applied Materials. 
Dickerson added that bringing teams together at the EPIC Center will deepen the partnership and accelerate transistor, interconnect, and packaging innovations required for future AI computing demands. 
"The demand for AI computing is driving the need for major advances in performance, power efficiency, and packaging. Intel is focused on delivering those innovations and doing it in close collaboration with partners across the ecosystem," said Lip-Bu Tan, CEO of Intel. 
Tan added that Intel looks forward to expanding its work at the EPIC Center to accelerate the transition of semiconductor technologies from the laboratory into high-volume manufacturing in the United States. 
Teams from both companies are collaborating on next-generation materials, process technologies, and device architectures targeting AI workloads across front-end and back-end-of-line advancements, including interconnect scaling. 
The partnership also covers advanced packaging technologies for Foveros-based 3D stacking, aimed at delivering higher interconnect density, improved power delivery, and enhanced thermal performance for high-performance compute platforms supporting emerging agentic AI workloads. 
"With the chipmaking roadmap becoming more complex at each process node, accelerating innovations in semiconductor devices, interconnects and packaging requires deeper collaboration across R&D and manufacturing," said Dr. Prabu Raja, president of the Semiconductor Products Group at Applied Materials. 
"Accelerating our R&D to keep pace with the rapid buildout of AI infrastructure is critical to delivering the technology, manufacturing excellence and foundry services our customers expect from Intel Foundry," said Naga Chandrasekaran, executive vice president, chief technology and operations officer and general manager of Intel Foundry. 
Chandrasekaran added that the EPIC Center provides an environment where engineering teams can collaborate at higher velocity to accelerate materials development and process innovations. 
Scheduled to become operationally ready this year, Applied's EPIC Center is designed to reduce commercialisation timelines for breakthrough technologies, providing chipmakers with early R&D access and faster learning cycles for high-volume manufacturing transfer.

Arkema inaugurates its next-generation acrylic acid purification unit in Carling
Download the PDF 
Arkema has inaugurated a new acrylic acid purification unit featuring an innovative process at its Carling site in France. This facility positions the Group among the most competitive players in Europe and contributes to the decarbonization of the European chemical industry. It is part of Arkema’s decarbonization investment program and supports the implementation of its ambitious climate plan.
The inauguration ceremony for the new unit was held in the presence of Thierry Le Hénaff, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Arkema and Stéphane Séjourné, Executive Vice-President of the European Commission for Prosperity and Industrial Strategy.
The ceremony took place on the same day as the Critical Chemicals Alliance General Assembly, which brought together European industrial leaders and policy-makers to discuss the key challenges of sovereignty, competitiveness, and decarbonization.
With an investment of nearly €150 million, this new unit represents one of Arkema’s largest industrial projects in France.
It will contribute to the Group’s ambitious climate plan, underpinned by a dedicated investment program supporting Arkema’s decarbonization, with a cumulative amount that could reach €400 million over the 2022-2030 period.” 
Thierry Le Hénaff, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Arkema.
“Europe must keep its chemical industry. There can be neither industrial sovereignty nor strategic autonomy if we allow the essential building blocks of our economy to leave. Carling is showing the way forward: nearly €150 million invested to produce in Europe, using less energy and generating less carbon, while building on decades of industrial know-how. This is exactly the model we want to promote: decarbonizing without deindustrializing, investing in our regions, and making our industrial hubs the driving forces of our future.” 
Stéphane Séjourné, Executive Vice-President of the European Commission for Prosperity and Industrial Strategy. 
The Carling site is one of the leading acrylic production facilities in Europe. It produces acrylic monomer s used in performance coatings, adhesives, water treatment and other advanced materials.
The new unit improves the energy efficiency of the purification process by 25% and reduces the carbon intensity of the site’s operations by 20%. The innovative technology deployed also helps optimize resource and waste management while significantly reducing solvent consumption.
Thanks to this investment, the Carling plant is positioning itself among the reference sites in the industry, aligned with the highest operational and environmental standards . It also strengthens Arkema’s leadership in the low-carbon acrylic materials market.
This project has been decided in 2023 and has been partly funded by the French State as part of the France 2030 program, operated by ADEME, and funded by the European Union – NextGenerationEU.

PLAINSBORO TOWNSHIP , N.J. , Oct. 7, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Veolia today celebrated the completion of the Princeton Meadows Wastewater Treatment Facility with a ribbon-cutting ceremony, marking a major investment in resilient infrastructure, environmental protection and long-term water sustainability. 
Serving approximately 11,000 residents and businesses, the new facility features climate-resilient infrastructure, advanced ultraviolet disinfection technology, high-efficiency biological treatment and energy-efficient equipment. These systems are designed to enhance treatment performance, withstand extreme weather and meet increasingly stringent environmental requirements.
The project also builds on Veolia's 55-year history of water reuse at the site. Since 1971, the site has supplied Middlesex County with 1.4 billion gallons of reclaimed water for irrigation at a county golf course, helping conserve local water resources.
"This next-generation facility exemplifies Veolia's commitment to environmental security, public health and sustainable infrastructure," said Nadege Petit , CEO of Veolia in North America . "It combines significant capital investment, advanced treatment technology and climate-resilient design to provide reliable service to the community for decades to come, while continuing our longstanding commitment to water reuse. This milestone marks the latest chapter in more than five decades of work at the site and reaffirms our commitment to applying our expertise to address challenges more effectively, in collaboration with local stakeholders."
The facility treats 475 million gallons of wastewater and reuses 32 million gallons – the equivalent of 48 Olympic sized swimming pools – of reclaimed water annually. Built for greater climate resilience, the new plant is located on higher ground outside the original 100-year floodplain, helping protect critical infrastructure from flooding.
"The original Princeton Meadows facility served the community well for more than five decades, but it was aging and located in a vulnerable floodplain," said Kendra Morris, CEO of Veolia Regulated Water in North America. "Rather than simply upgrade the existing plant, we reimagined it. This facility is designed to meet today's needs, anticipate future environmental requirements and preserve our commitment to water reuse. Investing in infrastructure also means investing in the community."
The ribbon-cutting ceremony brought together representatives of Veolia , the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities , the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection , New Jersey State Elected Officials, Middlesex County , the Township of Plainsboro , and project partners, including J. Fletcher Creamer & Son and HDR.
The ceremony included recognition from United States Senator Andy Kim , who provided a Certificate of Congressional Recognition for the project, as well as a joint resolution from the New Jersey State Senate and General Assembly celebrating Veolia's milestone.
The $58 million Princeton Meadows project is part of Veolia's broader investment in New Jersey . Through its GreenUp program, the company invests more than $150 million annually statewide to support water quality, reliability and long-term environmental sustainability for the 1.1 million customers it serves in New Jersey .
As part of the celebration, Veolia also announced a $10,000 contribution to the Plainsboro Recreation Department's Water Science & Sustainability Education Program. The contribution supports opportunities for local students to learn about conservation and environmental stewardship.
ABOUT VEOLIA Veolia, a global leader in environmental services, works every day to build ecological security for the benefit of public health and the competitiveness of industries and regions. With 215,000 employees across five continents, working closely with local communities, and thanks to its cutting-edge technologies, the group cleans up pollution, reduces carbon emissions, and regenerates resources through concrete solutions that combine its expertise in water and water technologies, waste – including hazardous waste management, and local energy. In 2025, the Veolia group served 110 million people with drinking water and 97 million with sanitation, produced 45 million megawatt hours of energy, and treated 64 million tons of waste. Veolia Environnement (Paris Euronext: VIE, Fortune 500, SBF 120) generated consolidated revenue of €44.4 billion in 2025. 
In North America, Veolia is a leading environmental services provider with more than 15,000 employees working at over 500 locations. It's the largest private water operator in the U.S., a leading water technology provider, and a hazardous waste and pollution treatment leader. It is uniquely positioned in the American market with a leadership role in improving water quality and removing pollutants offering a full spectrum of water, waste, and energy management services and technology, including water and wastewater treatment, commercial and hazardous waste collection and disposal, energy consulting and resource recovery. www.veolia.com - www.veolianorthamerica.com

Quantum BioPharma (NASDAQ: QNTM) Enlists Thermo Fisher’s Clinical Research Business to Launch Phase 2 Lucid-MS Trial
Edgenewswire 
October 7, 2026 • 2 min read 
New agreement moves innovative Lucid-MS treatment from planning into execution.
Proprietary platform is designed around a novel neuroprotective approach that targets demyelination rather than solely modulating the immune system.
Thermo Fisher’s clinical research business is a leading global contract research organization, with impressive expertise in central nervous system and MS studies.
Most multiple sclerosis (“MS”) drugs work by quieting the immune system. A new partnership shines the spotlight on a different approach — protecting the nerve’s own insulation — and sets up that treatment for a rigorous clinical test. Quantum BioPharma (NASDAQ: QNTM) , a biopharmaceutical company developing therapies for neurodegenerative and metabolic disorders, has signed a Study Start-Up Agreement with the clinical research business of Thermo Fisher Scientific. The contract covers implementation of the phase 2 trial of Lucid-MS, Quantum’s lead drug candidate for MS.

content_text:
Renishaw Expands Miskin Site as Demand Drives Manufacturing Growth 
October 7, 2026 
This year, engineering technologies business, Renishaw, is celebrating the 15th anniversary of the purchase of its Miskin site in South Wales, and the completion of the first phase of a further £70 million development of the facility. Announced in 2022, this is the largest capital investment project in the company’s history, which will ultimately double the size of the Miskin site, giving the company space to expand manufacturing capacity to meet rising demand for its world-leading precision metrology, additive manufacturing and position measurement products.
Renishaw has been committed to the manufacturing of its own products since its formation and uses many of these products within its machining facilities. Whilst much of its production is performed in the UK, at its Miskin, Stonehouse and Woodchester sites, it has carriedout the assembly of metrology products in Ireland since 1981, and also has a significant operation in Pune, India.
Renishaw completed the acquisition of the 193-acre site, situated to the west of Cardiff, from RobertBosch Ltd in September 2011. It started modest operations in May 2012 with a single production shift, having refurbished around 15% of the 416,000 sq ft (38,675 sqm) total building space, which primarily consisted of two large production halls. By the time of the formal opening of the facility in October 2012 by then First Minister of Wales, employee numbers were around 25, compared to around 950 today. Following the completion of the first development phase (Hall 3), usablespace has grown to 617,000 sq ft (57,350 sqm) and will total 880,000 sq ft (81,765 sqm) once Hall 4 is completed and operational, establishing the Miskin facility as one of the UK’s largest advanced manufacturing sites.
Renishaw has continued to invest throughout its tenure, with around £150 million spent to date on acquiring the site, refurbishing legacy buildings, developing the new halls, and installing advanced manufacturing equipment. The latter currently includes 134 CNC machine tools producing around one million parts per month, three PCB assembly lines, robotic assembly and automated warehousing, with more equipment on order to support customer requirements.
Manufacturing Capacity to Support Future Growth 
The latest phase of development demonstrates Renishaw’s long-term confidence in the UK and its commitment to creating highly skilled jobs and supporting economic growth for years to come.
Hall 3 is used to manufacture Renishaw’s metal additive manufacturing (AM) systems, AGILITY coordinate measuring machines (CMMs) and also houses a multimillion-pound automated storage andretrieval warehousing system. The company is currently experiencing strong demand for its AM systems, notably from the aerospace and defence (A&D) sector, and is also seeing growing demand for its high precision multi-sensor CMMs used to inspect complex components, including applications in the energy and Aerospace & Defence sectors.
Hall 4 was constructed as a shell building, with its future utilisation dependent on sales demand and capacity requirements. Due to exceptional demand for Renishaw’s position encoders from manufacturers of semiconductor equipment,driven by the growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), some of that additional capacity is now required, and Hall 4 will be partially occupied over the coming months. To support customers in this important sector, the company is also increasing its capital expenditure on equipment, especially new machine tools, electronics production and automated assembly.
Steve Oakes, Director of Position Measurement, said, “ Our encoders are used at all stages of the semiconductor production process, from manufacturing silicon wafers to packaging and testing individual devices. The semiconductor sector is highly cyclical, and we are currently seeing a ‘super cycle’, which is driving very high levels of investment across the entire supply chain. ”
A Focus on Sustainability 
Beyond increasing manufacturing capacity, the development of the new halls has been designed to deliver long-term operational and environmental benefits, supporting Renishaw’s wider commitment to achieving Net Zero greenhouse gas emissions across Scopes 1 and 2 by 2028. The company’s long term ambition is for all buildings at the Miskin site to operate at Net Zero, and both new halls have been designed to achieve Net Zero Carbon in Operation.
The high-performance buildings require significantly less energy than conventional industrial facilities, reducing operating costs and carbon emissions from the outset. Enhanced insulation in the walls, roofs and floors delivers thermal performance well beyond current building regulation requirements, while high-performance glazing minimises heat loss and reduces the energy required to maintain comfortable indoor conditions throughout the year.
Heating and cooling are provided by highly efficient electric heat pump systems, which generate multiple units of heating or cooling energy for every unit of electricity consumed. The system delivers approximately four units of heat and six units of cooling per unit of electricity, making it substantially more energy efficient and lower in carbon emissions than conventional gas-fired systems.
A key feature of the Miskin expansion is its extensive use of on-site renewable energy generation, delivering an estimated 200 MWh of clean electricity each year. Where additional electricity is required, renewable energy tariffs are used to further reduce the site’s carbon footprint.
The Miskin expansion has provided valuable opportunities to develop the skills of Renishaw’s apprentices and graduate engineers who have played an active role throughout the project. They have gained first-hand experience of delivering a major industrial development, and project engineering apprentices were embedded within the design teams responsible for the new development, contributing to layout planning, coordinating with multiple business functions, attending regular site visits and supporting the design of office and workshop facilities.
Commitment to The Future 
The expansion of the Miskin site represents a major long-term investment in UK manufacturing, sustainability and skills development. It reinforces Renishaw’s commitment to South Wales and the UK while providing a modern, low-carbon manufacturing environment that showcases the best of British engineering. As the site continues to evolve, the new facilities will play a vital role in supporting innovation, reducing carbon emissions and creating high-quality employment opportunities for years to come.
Jim Long, Director of Group Manufacturing, said, “ The strong growth we are currently seeing has highlighted the importance of in-house manufacturing and the control it gives us in meeting our quality, cost and delivery targets. This commitment to manufacturing is exemplified by the investment that we have made in Miskin over the past 15 years and I would like to thank the many people from across our business who have supported the development of this world-class facility.” 
He continued, “ A key aim of our facilities is to create an attractive and enjoyable working environment that inspires employees while creating a world-class environment that impresses visitors and presents a positive image of manufacturing.” 
Long concluded, “ The significant ongoing investment by our Board to increase our production capabilities demonstrates a huge vote of confidence in our manufacturing operations and people, at an exciting time for the business.”

title: Lilly Korea’s Retevmo gains reimbursement for RET-driven lung, thyroid cancers - Korea Biomedical Review
query: ("Eli Lilly and Company" OR "Eli Lilly") (Korea OR Korean) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
이전 기사보기 
다음 기사보기 
Lilly Korea’s Retevmo gains reimbursement for RET-driven lung, thyroid cancers 
바로가기 
복사하기 
본문 글씨 줄이기 
본문 글씨 키우기 
스크롤 이동 상태바 
Eli Lilly Korea's Retevmo (selpercatinib) has gained reimbursement in Korea for RET fusion-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and RET-mutant medullary thyroid cancer, opening reimbursed access to a mutation-specific therapy from the first-line setting.
Eli Lilly Korea’s Retevmo has gained national health insurance coverage in Korea for first-line treatment of RET fusion-positive non-small cell lung cancer and RET-mutant medullary thyroid cancer. (Credit: Eli Lilly Korea) 
The reimbursement, effective last Thursday, covers Retevmo for patients with locally advanced or metastatic, stage IIIB or higher, nonsquamous RET fusion-positive NSCLC.
Coverage also applies to adults and children aged 12 or older with progressive advanced or metastatic RET-mutant medullary thyroid cancer (MTC) requiring systemic therapy. In both settings, reimbursement is available from first-line palliative treatment onward.
Retevmo is a selective RET inhibitor designed to target RET alterations, including gene fusions and point mutations. Lilly Korea said it is the first and only RET-targeted treatment available in Korea for RET fusion-positive NSCLC and RET-mutant MTC.
The reimbursement fills a gap for patients whose tumors test positive for RET alterations but previously had no reimbursed therapy specifically targeting the oncogenic driver.
The Ministry of Health and Welfare said RET fusion-positive NSCLC accounts for about 1 to 2 percent of lung cancers, with fewer than 300 patients estimated in Korea.
The distinction is particularly important because identifying a driver mutation can affect the choice of first-line therapy. Patients with RET-driven lung cancer have historically been treated largely with regimens developed for broader NSCLC populations when access to selective RET inhibition was limited.
Evidence supporting first-line use of Retevmo in NSCLC comes from the phase 3 LIBRETTO-431 trial, which compared selpercatinib with platinum-based chemotherapy with or without the PD-1 inhibitor pembrolizumab in previously untreated advanced RET fusion-positive NSCLC.
Median progression-free survival (PFS) was 24.8 months with selpercatinib compared with 11.2 months in the control group, translating into a 54 percent reduction in the risk of disease progression or death. The objective response rate (ORR) was 84 percent with selpercatinib and 65 percent with control treatment.
The trial also carries relevance for patients with brain metastases, a major concern in RET fusion-positive lung cancer. Selpercatinib is designed to penetrate the central nervous system (CNS), and the study reported an intracranial response rate of 82 percent among evaluable patients with baseline brain metastases.
Professor Ahn Jin-seok of the Division of Hematology-Oncology at Samsung Medical Center (SMC) said the reimbursement would allow physicians to recommend mutation-matched therapy from the first-line setting rather than relying primarily on conventional systemic treatment.
“Until now, even when a RET alteration was identified, the targeted treatment was outside reimbursement, leaving patients dependent on general anticancer therapy,” Ahn said. “This reimbursement closes that long-standing gap.”
He added that the change could be particularly meaningful for patients who already have brain metastases at diagnosis and previously had limited treatment options.
Retevmo also demonstrated an advantage over established multikinase inhibitors in RET-mutant MTC, a rare form of thyroid cancer that accounts for less than 1 percent of thyroid cancers.
The phase 3 LIBRETTO-531 trial enrolled patients with progressive, advanced RET-mutant MTC who had not previously received a kinase inhibitor and compared selpercatinib with either cabozantinib or vandetanib.
At 12 months, 86.8 percent of patients receiving selpercatinib remained progression-free compared with 65.7 percent of those receiving cabozantinib or vandetanib. Selpercatinib reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 72 percent, with a hazard ratio of 0.28.
Professor Park Young -joo of the Department of Internal Medicine at Seoul National University Hospital (SNUH) said advanced or metastatic MTC remains difficult to treat despite thyroid cancer generally being associated with a favorable prognosis.
“Patients with RET point mutations can have a poor prognosis, and there has been substantial unmet need for effective targeted treatment,” Park said.
She said the reimbursement should reduce the financial burden on patients and expand access to treatment that has demonstrated significantly improved clinical outcomes over previous standard therapies.
The coverage also places greater importance on genomic testing in both diseases because eligibility for Retevmo depends on identifying the relevant RET alteration before treatment.
Kwon Mi-ra, an executive overseeing Lilly Korea’s oncology business, described Retevmo as an example of precision medicine centered on the genetic driver of a tumor rather than solely on its organ of origin.
“With reimbursement finally in place after a long wait, we are pleased that more patients in Korea will be able to benefit from this approach,” Kwon said.

title: Cognex Acquires RealSense to Expand into Robotic Perception Market - Vision Systems Design
query: ("Cognex" OR "Cognex Corporation") ("press release" OR "investor relations" OR earnings OR announcement OR investment OR expansion OR acquisition OR partnership OR Korea) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
Cognex Acquires RealSense to Expand into Robotic Perception Market
Cognex Corporation has announced a $500 million acquisition of RealSense, aiming to diversify its product offerings and enter the robotic perception market, a key growth area in machine vision.
Jim Tatum 
Oct. 6, 2026
2 min read 
Add Us On Google 
Key Highlights
Cognex's acquisition of RealSense marks a strategic move into the rapidly growing robotic perception market.
The $500 million deal is financed through Cognex's existing cash reserves, with additional investments in employee retention and incentives.
Both companies aim to leverage their combined strengths to serve a broader industrial customer base globally.
Image/Cognex
6ac403f33f45089d8a6f05a5 Cognex Real Sense Image 
Cognex Corporation (Natick, MA, USA) has entered an agreement to buy RealSense (San Francisco, CA, USA) for $500 million.
The deal, announced in a press release Sept. 22, is part of Cognex’s plans to diversify its products and offerings by entering the robotic perception market, according to Cognex CEO Matt Moschner.
"RealSense represents a compelling strategic expansion for Cognex into robotic perception, one of the most attractive adjacent markets in machine vision," Moschner said. 
Nadav Orbach, Chief Executive Officer of RealSense said in the press release that joining Cognex gives RealSense “access to a global industrial customer base and go-to-market reach that would have taken us years to build on our own. This is a combination that makes both businesses stronger.” 
According to the press release, Cognex will acquire RealSense for approximately $500 million, financed entirely from existing cash and investments on its balance sheet. In addition, Cognex also expects to provide a three-year, $56.5 million cash retention program at target for RealSense employees, subject to performance modifiers, and to grant restricted stock units valued at approximately $50 million under Cognex's existing 2023 Stock Option and Incentive Plan dependent on the grant-date share price. 
The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026
“Cognex believes that robotic perception and these robotic systems are the future, a very new style of automation, that's here to stay,” Moschner said. “But we don't view it as an either, but an ‘in addition to.’ What's exciting is both of those things can coexist. We want to serve customers across both of those areas and. And we see that as key to our long-term growth ambition for Cognex.”

Bayer to invest $2.2B in Ohio pharmaceutical facility
The drugmaker plans to develop a “flexible, modular campus” with advanced digital and automation technologies. The first phase is set to be ready in 2031.

A rendering of Bayer's manufacturing plant slated for New Albany International Business Park in Ohio. The company plans to invest $2.2 billion in the project.
Courtesy of Bayer
Listen to the article

This audio is auto-generated. Please let us know if you have feedback .
Dive Brief: 
Bayer will invest $2.2 billion to build a pharmaceutical manufacturing facility in New Albany, Ohio, with a plan to make drugs for oncology, cardiovascular and renal care, the Germany-based company said Friday. 
Bayer plans to develop a “flexible, modular campus” that combines drug substance and drug product manufacturing and leverages advanced digital and automation technologies, according to a news release. The site is expected to create 600 jobs. 
The first module, designed for drug substances, is scheduled to be ready in 2031, and the second module for drug products will follow in 2034, Bayer said. No construction date was disclosed, but more than 1,500 jobs are expected to support the project. 
Dive Insight: 
The manufacturing site coming to New Albany is part of Bayer’s U.S. growth strategy. The biotechnology giant has spent more than $7 billion over the past five years expanding its U.S. pharmaceutical manufacturing and research and development operations. 
“The facility will be a strong strategic addition to our global Product Supply Network,” Holger Weintritt, head of product supply at Bayer’s pharmaceutical division, said in a statement. “As we continue to invest in our existing manufacturing sites around the globe, our planned presence in Ohio will further enhance our ability to serve our markets with greater resilience and reliability.” 
A spokesperson with Bayer did not immediately respond to a request for comment seeking details about the size of the New Albany facility, construction timeline or incentives the project may be eligible for. 
JobsOhio, a private, nonprofit economic development entity created by the state to foster corporate investment deals, said Bayer is looking to acquire a job creation tax credit from the Ohio Department of Development and JobsOhio assistance for the project. The company plans to make the details public at a later date. 
Ohio beat out several states for Bayer’s project, Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, said in a statement. Proximity to a growing biomanufacturing industry in the Columbus, Ohio, region as well as workforce readiness were key to the state’s appeal. Bayer plans to use the Ohio Life Science Training Center, which is under construction and set to open next summer, to train people for operator and technician roles at the plant. 
The investment comes as the Trump administration looks to bolster domestic manufacturing and reshore production across industries through a mix of tariffs and major investment deal promotion. 
Eli Lilly, AstraZeneca, Pfizer and other pharmaceutical companies have pledged tens of billions of dollars toward manufacturing expansions and research and development, according to an investment database on the White House’s website . 
Bayer said the New Albany site will complement its U.S. pharmaceuticals headquarters in Whippany, New Jersey, as well as operations in Pittsburgh; Berkeley, California; Cambridge, Massachusetts; Durham, North Carolina; and San Diego, California. 
Last year, Bayer completed a 70,000-square-foot expansion to its largest over-the-counter drug facility in Myerstown, Pennsylvania, as part of a $44 million investment. It also invested $250 million on a cell therapy production plant that opened in Berkeley in 2023.

TOPPAN to Showcase Color Data Traceability Concept at BioJapan 2026
Delivering color data reliability and consistency across R&D and manufacturing in the bio and life sciences sectors
Tweet 
Color Data Traceability Concept 
Tokyo – October 6, 2026 – TOPPAN Inc. (TOPPAN), a TOPPAN Group company and wholly owned subsidiary of TOPPAN Holdings Inc. (TYO: 7911), will participate in BioJapan 2026 at Pacifico Yokohama from October 7 to October 9.
First held in 1986, BioJapan is the world's oldest biotechnology exhibition. Held concurrently with Regenerative Medicine JAPAN and healthTECH JAPAN, it serves as one of Asia's largest partnering events, bringing together corporations, startups, academia, and research institutions to drive global open innovation.
At the TOPPAN booth (BioJapan 2026, Booth C-37), TOPPAN will introduce its color data traceability concept based on its proprietary color management technology. 1 In R&D and manufacturing across the bio and life sciences—spanning healthcare, food, and environmental applications—subtle color changes in culture liquids and reagents serve as critical indicators for evaluating quality and status. However, digitally storing and standardizing color information has historically been challenging, leading to subjective visual evaluations, reduced reproducibility, and hindered data utilization. To address these needs for objective color data management, TOPPAN leverages its proprietary Color Management System (CMS) based services to accurately record and analyze rich color information, ensuring data reliability and consistency to drive quality control and digital transformation (DX).
Additionally, at the exhibition TOPPAN will host a luncheon seminar at Annex Hall (F204) on new frontiers in medical applications utilizing extracellular vesicles (Japanese).
Exhibition Highlights
Color Data Traceability Concept 
TOPPAN will share its new platform to ensure the reliability and consistency of color-related data in bio and life science R&D and manufacturing. Subtle color variations in test reagents and samples serve as vital evaluation criteria. TOPPAN's color data traceability concept digitizes color information directly from test samples, mitigating risks such as evaluation discrepancies caused by sample fading or ambient lighting differences, as well as data tampering or manual recording errors. By establishing an environment for reliable color data acquisition and management, TOPPAN aims to provide standardized evidence suitable for academic presentations, research papers, and quality assurance.
CAM-FIT™: Digital Image Color Correction Software Free from Environmental Lighting Effects 
TOPPAN will showcase inspection and manufacturing DX solutions powered by CAM-FIT™, a software program that restores an object's true color regardless of shooting conditions (such as lighting variations, shadows, or contrast differences). By utilizing CAM-FIT™, users can accurately save objective color information from image data that was previously susceptible to environmental inconsistencies. This enables advanced color management and data application via digital imagery, including for use in remote medical assessments, as well as color tracking/information sharing for products and research samples.
Quantification Technology for Lateral Flow Assays via Smartphone App Powered by CAM-FIT™ 
TOPPAN will demonstrate technology and a smartphone application that can be used to quantify detection results by correcting images of paper-based lateral flow assay 2 test strips using CAM-FIT™. As a practical application, TOPPAN will showcase its proprietary technology for detecting extracellular vesicles (exosomes) 3 via immunochromatography, 4 joint research initiatives, and the Exorapid-qIC™ Extracellular Vesicle Immunochromatography Kit—a research reagent kit utilizing this patented technology, commercialized by Dai Nippon Toryo Co., Ltd.

title: India serves as engineering, digital hub for Veolia: APAC executive V-P - Business Standard
query: ("Veolia" OR "Veolia Group") (Korea OR Korean) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
India serves as engineering, digital hub for Veolia: APAC executive V-P
Veolia sees India as an engineering and digital hub, with rising demand for industrial water, wastewater recycling and municipal water solutions driven by infrastructure and high-tech sectors.
premium 
Irshaad Hakim, executive vice-president (V-P), Asia-Pacific (APAC), water technologies
Prachi Pisal Mumbai 6 min read Last Updated : Oct 05 2026 | 11:58 PM IST
Listen to This Article
French environmental services company Veolia, which recorded consolidated global revenue of €44.4 billion in 2025 (about ₹4.37 trillion, based on an exchange rate of €1 to ₹98.52), has been present in India since 2000 and is looking to expand its business as infrastructure investment and demand for water treatment and reuse solutions grow across sectors. Irshaad Hakim , executive vice-president (V-P), Asia-Pacific (APAC), water technologies, Veolia, told, told Prachi Pisal in a virtual interview that the company sees big opportunities in industrial water, wastewater recycling, and municipal water, with sectors such as semiconductor and data centre emerging as key drivers of demand. Edited excerpts:
What are your expansion plans for India?
The scale of infrastructure being built is phenomenal. What India has to navigate is constructability — building where land is limited, and sites are difficult — and that is driving innovation that is unique to India. We recently secured 15-year operating contracts in Mumbai. Some of these projects are under construction, while others are already commissioned.
We’re also seeing strong demand from high-tech industries. As water-intensive sectors such as semiconductor expand, we provide ultra-pure water and wastewater recycling, which we call “waste to wafer”, to close the water cycle. Data centres are also creating a massive market for water reclaim and reuse, which will be central to strengthening India’s water security.
Across APAC, which segments do you see offering the biggest opportunities?
The biggest growth right now is driven by reshoring, particularly in microelectronics and advanced manufacturing. Chip production needs ultra-pure water, and as production intensifies, its wastewater has to be treated and recycled. That requires specific expertise, and it is a fast-growing sector across APAC. Data centres are another major area.
India stands out in industrial water and hazardous waste, with zero liquid discharge requirements and large manufacturing corridors for chemicals, pharmaceuticals, and life sciences — areas where we bring expertise. Hydrocarbon processing, chemical processing, and food and beverage are also key drivers.
Across all these markets, municipal transformation remains fundamental. Mature APAC markets need to optimise the assets they already have, while growing markets such as India need to build new ones through public-private partnerships (PPPs) and large-scale urban water distribution and drinking water production.
How does the India opportunity compare with other major APAC markets?
Developed markets such as Japan, South Korea, and Australia are focused on getting more capacity out of existing infrastructure, while growing markets such as China and India are investing heavily in new infrastructure.
China’s growth is concentrated in data centres, microelectronics, and Coal-to-X, while India’s infrastructure development and stringent regulatory requirements are expected to drive demand.
India also uniquely combines value engineering with advanced digital engineering. It serves as an engineering and digital hub for Veolia, supporting its APAC and global operations. That allows us to deploy next-generation smart systems, including artificial intelligence and our Hubgrade digital solutions, much faster across the region and helps mature markets such as Japan, South Korea, and Australia get more from the infrastructure they already have.
Where is Veolia investing across APAC?
Our priorities follow where demand is moving fastest: advanced manufacturing, digital infrastructure, and industrial water reuse, alongside the transformation of municipal water. To support that, we’re investing heavily in the next phase of our Wuxi factory in China, as well as in our engineering teams and manufacturing facilities in India.
What challenges are you facing in the APAC markets?
Challenges vary by market. In India, unlike mature APAC markets, projects face bankability constraints due to low municipal water tariffs. Water is often undervalued: people will pay far more for bottled water than for what comes out of their taps, yet even a 10 per cent tariff increase meets strong public resistance. That makes projects harder to finance and slows the PPPs that could hasten investment.
China and India have made progress on regulation, particularly tighter discharge requirements. But in parts of Southeast Asia, bureaucracy, bottlenecks, and uncertainty over whether policies are enforced or are merely guidelines can delay projects. In India, land acquisition and approval processes can also take longer than in markets such as Singapore, which slows the scaling of critical infrastructure.
What impact are you seeing because of the West Asia war?
In the first half of the year, some customers deferred projects because they were uncertain about when the situation would end. In the second half, customers have accepted this as the new normal and are making decisions accordingly, and we are seeing growth as a result.
Most customers now understand how tariffs will and won’t impact them, and countries are taking their own steps to manage them.
Our model is “in-region for region”, so cross-border tariffs have had very limited impact on us.
Do you see policy-level support rising, particularly in India?
There’s a lot of discussion about putting the right frameworks and incentives in place. The conversations have definitely started, and India has a lot to be proud of. Its wastewater discharge requirements are already among the most stringent in the region. If India can move that fast on discharge standards, it can move faster in other areas too. It can be done; stakeholders need to come together and focus on the right outcome.
APAC accounts for 10 per cent of Veolia’s global revenue. How do you see that share evolving in the coming years?
Given the investments flowing into APAC and India, we expect that share to increase. How fast it grows depends on how quickly decisions are made. Where government-led projects move slowly, revenue will build more slowly.
Looking at combined business growth across China, India, Southeast Asia, and Oceania, Veolia’s growth rate in APAC is strong. We expect the region’s share to grow quite rapidly over the next five to six years.
India is a high priority under GreenUp, Veolia’s strategic plan to accelerate ecological transformation. We have ambitious targets, and we are investing in our people in India to deliver them.
Are you open to joint ventures (JVs), acquisitions and inorganic growth?
Yes. Mergers and acquisitions are part of how Veolia grows, and we pursue opportunities that strengthen what we can offer customers. Partnerships matter just as much, and our allies include JVs and consortia, both incorporated and unincorporated.
How would you compare the APAC market with other global markets?
APAC has both advantages and challenges. With China and India among the world’s most populous countries, the region has a much larger pool of engineering talent. The challenge is keeping that talent engaged.
Another challenge is scaling startups. In the Americas and Europe, startups scale faster, with more capital behind them. We need to close that gap so that technology developed here advances faster and reaches other markets.
APAC is uniquely positioned, particularly because much of the investment in Southeast Asia and India is coming from global companies. That helps as we navigate today’s geopolitics. And with the world’s largest population and a growing middle class, the region’s infrastructure needs will only increase, which is positive for our business.

Proterial Builds 30,000-TPA Metglas Plant in India - Transformer Localization Moves Upstream
Oct 5, 2026 
4 minute read.
Leave a Comment 
Highlights 
Proterial and SSEL are building a 30,000-tonne-per-year Metglas amorphous alloy ribbon plant in Sri City, Andhra Pradesh, targeting October 2026 startup.
India currently consumes an estimated 60,000–70,000 tonnes of amorphous material annually; a planned second phase could nearly eliminate import dependence within three to five years.
Metglas transformer cores reduce standby power consumption to roughly one-third that of conventional electrical steel, making them critical to India's grid efficiency goals.
India's DGTR has opened an anti-dumping investigation into amorphous metal imports from China, Japan, South Korea, and Russia, adding policy urgency to domestic production.
The venture fits a broader Indian industrial strategy: localize advanced materials, connect them to downstream manufacturing, and reduce logistics and import exposure at scale.

GE HealthCare agrees to acquire SOFIE Biosciences in $945m deal
The cash deal to acquire the PET radiopharmaceuticals CMO from Trilantic North America is expected to close in H1 2027.
Ross Law 
October 5, 2026 
Share
Copy Link 
Share on X 
Share on Linkedin 
Share on Facebook 
Under the deal, GE HealthCare will inherit SOFIE Biosciences’ US network of 15 CMO sites and its theranostics-focused contract development and manufacturing organisation (CDMO) site. Credit: Anne Czichos/Shutterstock.com 
GE HealthCare has agreed to acquire SOFIE Biosciences, a contract manufacturing organisation (CMO) specialising in positron emission tomography (PET) radiopharmaceuticals, from Trilantic North America in a $945m deal.
Under the all-cash transaction, which is anticipated to close in H1 2027, GE HealthCare will inherit SOFIE’s US network of 15 CMO sites and its theranostics-focused contract development and manufacturing organisation (CDMO) site.

Broadening GE HealthCare’s footprint in the US radiopharmaceutical industry, the imaging giant stated that the acquisition will help drive patient access to novel radiopharmaceuticals such as its existing line of F-18 radioactive diagnostic agents, including Flyrcado, that are used in PET imaging.
SOFIE already manufactures GE HealthCare’s Flyrcado, a myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) radiopharmaceutical that obtained US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval in September 2024.
Radiopharmaceuticals are drugs that contain a radioactive isotope combined with a targeting molecule such as a peptide to aid in the diagnosis and treatment of diseases including cancer and Alzheimer’s disease. 
Meanwhile, SOFIE’s acquisition will give GE HealthCare’s pharmaceutical diagnostics (PDx) segment the ability to participate in other high-growth areas outside its own product portfolio, the company stated.
In a research note, Navann Ty, senior analyst at BNP Paribas Equity Research, called GE HealthCare’s acquisition a “solid addition” to its PDx segment that may help with “supply and ramp up” of Flyrcado. 
Kevin O’Neill, president and CEO of the PDx segment at GE HealthCare, commented: “The PET radiopharmaceutical market is expanding rapidly with the introduction of innovative radiotracers and advances in precision care, including the growing adoption of targeted therapies.
“As part of GE HealthCare, SOFIE Biosciences is expected to grow in the low double digits and enables us to participate across the radiopharmaceutical value stream, meeting customer demand through a mix of GE HealthCare owned and partner facilities.
“We will leverage our scale and expertise in radiopharmaceutical manufacturing across the US, Europe and Japan to further invest in and grow SOFIE Biosciences, helping improve patient access, strengthen reliability of supply, and support the next generation of precision care products.”
Once GE HealthCare’s acquisition closes in H1 2027, SOFIE Biosciences will continue to operate as an independent manufacturing partner to its customers, supplying its existing product portfolio, including products from other leading radiopharmaceutical providers.
SOFIE’s president and CEO, Patrick Phelps, commented: “With Trilantic North America’s support, we have significantly expanded our capabilities and scale, and we share GE HealthCare’s ambition to improve patient outcomes by delivering on the promise of radiopharmaceuticals as we look ahead to our next phase of growth.”
GlobalData analysis reveals that while the PET imaging agent market was valued at $2.1bn in 2025, it lags behind single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), which was valued at $4.7bn. However, between 2025 and 2035, PET agents are projected to grow at a CAGR of 4.6%, representing a growth rate 5.5x higher than the projected growth of SPECT agents.
To meet the anticipated uptick in the PET market, Siemens Healthineers completed a $43.6m expansion project at its PET Detector Center in Tennessee in September, readying the site to meet rising customer demand for PET/computed tomography (CT) scanners used alongside radiopharmaceutical agents.

title: GE HealthCare to acquire SOFIE Biosciences establishing a final mile footprint for PET radiopharmaceutical supply in the U.S. - GE Healthcare
query: "GE HealthCare" ("press release" OR "investor relations" OR earnings OR announcement OR investment OR expansion OR acquisition OR partnership OR Korea) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
GE HealthCare to acquire SOFIE Biosciences, establishing a 'final mile' footprint for PET radiopharmaceutical supply in the U.S.
October 05, 2026
Broadens GE HealthCare's footprint in the U.S. radiopharmaceutical industry, drives patient access to F18 labeled Positron Emission Tomography (PET) radiopharmaceuticals and enhances exposure to new high-growth areas
Pharmaceutical Diagnostics (PDx) continues to partner with other established Contract Manufacturing Organizations (CMOs) to drive and expand patient access to its radiopharmaceutical portfolio, while SOFIE Biosciences continues to supply PET products from other leading radiopharmaceutical providers
Provides U.S. rights to FAPI-74, a Phase III pipeline PET radiotracer with pan-cancer imaging potential, aiming to be among the first-to-launch in a large and fast-growing market 1 
Radiopharmaceutical manufacturing at a SOFIE Biosciences site
Chicago, IL — October 5, 2026 — GE HealthCare (Nasdaq: GEHC) today announced a definitive agreement to acquire SOFIE Biosciences, a leading U.S.-based CMO for PET radiopharmaceuticals, from Trilantic North America, for a purchase price of $945 million paid in cash. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to closing conditions, including regulatory approvals, at which time SOFIE Biosciences will become part of GE HealthCare’s PDx segment.
The acquisition of SOFIE Biosciences establishes a footprint for GE HealthCare in the time-critical ‘final mile’ of U.S. PET radiopharmaceutical supply, while also enabling PDx to participate in other high growth areas outside its own product portfolio. With a U.S. network of 15 CMO sites operating 21 cyclotrons, and a theranostics-focused Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization (CDMO) site, this acquisition broadens GE HealthCare's footprint in the U.S. radiopharmaceutical industry, while driving reliable patient access to novel radiopharmaceuticals. It also further enables GE HealthCare’s ability to provide solutions along every step of the theranostics pathway, from cyclotrons to imaging technology, digital workflow tools and radiotherapeutics infrastructure.
“The PET radiopharmaceutical market is expanding rapidly with the introduction of innovative radiotracers and advances in precision care, including the growing adoption of targeted therapies. As part of GE HealthCare, SOFIE Biosciences is expected to grow in the low double digits, and enables us to participate across the radiopharmaceutical value stream, meeting customer demand through a mix of GE HealthCare owned and partner facilities. SOFIE Biosciences has a highly skilled team with deep expertise serving U.S. customers, including manufacturing our Flyrcado™ (flurpiridaz F18 injection) product,” said Kevin O'Neill, President & CEO of the PDx segment at GE HealthCare. “We will leverage our scale and expertise in radiopharmaceutical manufacturing across the U.S., Europe and Japan to further invest in and grow SOFIE Biosciences, helping improve patient access, strengthen reliability of supply, and support the next generation of precision care products."
PET radiopharmaceuticals are used in precision medicine to visualize metabolic and molecular activity and, increasingly, to deliver targeted therapies across a range of disease areas. F18 labeled PET radiopharmaceuticals have a 110-minute half-life, with PET CMOs playing a crucial role in enabling timely and reliable patient access, both to existing and pipeline products. Industry-wide, the radiopharmaceutical pipeline is growing rapidly, with approximately 20 PET radiotracers and over 30 radiotherapeutics currently under development. 2 These include SOFIE Biosciences’ Phase III F18 Fibroblast Activation Protein Inhibitor (FAPI) asset, FAPI-74, for which GE HealthCare already holds outside-of-U.S. rights. FAPI has the potential to further expand an already fast-growing global PET imaging market, and is showing strong potential for diagnostic and theranostic use across a range of oncologic and non-oncologic indications. 
GE HealthCare will continue to drive and expand access to its existing proprietary F18 radiopharmaceutical products, while advancing its pipeline of new products, both through SOFIE Biosciences, and PDx’s other established CMO partners across the U.S. 
Serving SOFIE Biosciences’ Customers 
Following the transaction close, SOFIE Biosciences will continue to operate as an independent manufacturing partner to its customers, supplying its existing product portfolio, including products from other leading radiopharmaceutical providers.
Patrick Phelps, SOFIE Biosciences co-founder, President & CEO, said, “As demand continues to increase for F18 products, and pipelines for new diagnostics and therapeutics continue to expand, joining GE HealthCare marks an exciting step in our journey as a leading U.S. CMO. With Trilantic North America’s support, we have significantly expanded our capabilities and scale, and we share GE HealthCare’s ambition to improve patient outcomes by delivering on the promise of radiopharmaceuticals as we look ahead to our next phase of growth.”
Ted Rosenwasser, Partner, Trilantic North America, said, "We are incredibly proud of what Patrick and the SOFIE Biosciences team have accomplished during our partnership. SOFIE Biosciences has grown significantly, investing in its network and manufacturing capabilities to help meet growing demand and enable increased and reliable patient access to critical products. GE HealthCare's legacy and global expertise make it a natural partner to support SOFIE Biosciences’ continued growth and help expand access for U.S. patients to novel diagnostic and therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals.”
GE HealthCare’s Pharmaceutical Diagnostics segment is a global leader in imaging agents used to support 140 million procedures in 2025, equivalent to four patient procedures every second. For more than 40 years, GE HealthCare's imaging agents have been routinely used across care pathways to support diagnosis. 
Financial Benefits 
GE HealthCare estimates that the transaction will be accretive to revenue growth, Adjusted earnings before interest and taxes margin* and Adjusted earnings per share* in the first full year of ownership.
Advisors 
For GE HealthCare, BofA Securities, Consello Financial LLC and Solomon Partners Securities LLC served as financial advisors.

title: Corning Glass Waveguide Substrate for CPO Scaling (OFC 2026) - Simple Tech Trend
query: ("Corning" OR "Corning Incorporated") (Korea OR Korean) after:2026-10-01 before:2026-11-01
content_text:
Paper Analysis | Integrated Glass Waveguide Substrate with Surface-Coupled Photonic Chips for Massive CPO Scaling
Oct 5 
3 min read 
Updated: Oct 7 
Introduction 
With the explosive growth of artificial intelligence (AI), data center demand for high bandwidth and low power has reached a tipping point. To shorten electrical signal paths and reduce loss, moving optics inside the electronic package — co-packaged optics (CPO) — has become an inevitable trend. Yet precisely and quickly integrating silicon photonic integrated circuits (PICs) onto high-density circuit substrates while keeping coupling loss low has long been a major pain point for volume production. Corning's answer is a glass substrate with embedded ion-exchanged (IOX) waveguides that uses evanescent coupling to try to clear the last mile to CPO volume manufacturing. 
Source for Readers 
Title : Integrated Glass Waveguide Substrate with Surface Coupled Photonic Chips for Massive Scaling of CPO 
Authors : Lars Brusberg, Seong-ho Seok, Tim Grygiel, et al. 
Affiliation : Corning Optical Communications (research centers in Germany, Korea and the US) 
Venue : OFC 2026 © Optica Publishing Group 2026 
In-Depth Figure Analysis 
Figure 1: Integrated Glass Waveguide Substrate Architecture 
This figure shows both the macro vision and the micro structure of CPO: 
Fig 1a : a glass substrate with 16 PICs arranged around an ASIC. This layout keeps electrical trace length under 13 mm, maximizing transmission efficiency. 
Fig 1b & 1c : the heart of the paper — ion-exchanged (IOX) waveguides embedded inside the glass substrate, with flip-chip assembly via gold bumps in an etched cavity. 
Why it matters : it proves the optical interface (waveguides) and electrical interface (gold bumps) can sit on the same surface and be assembled simultaneously, with placement time under 5 minutes per PIC — critical for high-volume manufacturing. 
Figure 2: Test Vehicle Design and Coupling Efficiency Simulation 
Fig 2a : a surface coupler designed with eigenmode expansion (EME) simulation, transferring light between the IOX waveguide and a SiN waveguide. 
Fig 2b : the data show that with a SiN taper length of 2–3 mm, coupling loss drops below 1 dB while tolerating lateral offsets of up to 3–4 µm — well within the comfortable precision range of automated assembly tools. 
Fig 2c & 2d : the fabricated glass interposer, including a 16-waveguide array, alignment marks and electrical pads inside a 22 µm-deep cavity. 
Why it matters : this defines the process window and proves glass substrates can provide low-loss ( 
Figure 3: PIC Assembly Results and Performance Measurements 
Fig 3a–3c : viewed through the back of the glass substrate, the optical adhesive fills uniformly without overflow, and alignment accuracy is held within 1 µm. 
Fig 3e & 3f : measurements of the assembled electro-optical system show C-band coupling loss of about 3–4 dB, while pure optical assembly tests bring loss below 1.5 dB, with the best point even under 1 dB. 
Why it matters : it validates electrical integrity (a daisy-chain test across 96 gold bumps with resistance as expected) and the thermal stability of optical transmission. 
Conclusion 
Corning's results this time are impressive. The glass substrate is no longer just a "transparent support" but a "functional carrier" with high-density optical and electrical interconnect capability. 
Volume-production potential : optical alignment used to demand extreme precision and time; by relaxing tolerance to 3–4 µm through evanescent coupling and completing single-PIC assembly in 5 minutes, Corning delivers a qualitative leap in throughput. 
Higher bandwidth density : shrinking waveguide pitch to 50 µm would let a single module deliver up to 8 Tb/s of bandwidth density (400G per waveguide), squarely matching the appetite of next-generation AI clusters. 
Simpler packaging : electrical and optical interfaces are completed in the same assembly step, reducing process complexity, and glass's coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) is a closer match to the chips, a major advantage for long-term thermal stability. 
In short, if this technology makes it into the supply chain, it will dramatically lower the barrier to CPO, turning "optics replacing electrical links" from a lab slogan into a cost-effective solution that can actually be deployed.

$2.2B Bayer plant will be Ohio's largest-ever international healthcare project 
The Statehouse News Bureau |

A rendering of Bayer's planned processing and manufacturing facility in New Albany 
A historic $2.2 billion investment is coming to central Ohio from the German pharmaceutical and biotechnology company Bayer. 
The processing and manufacturing plant will make drugs to treat cancer, heart disease and other conditions. It’s the state’s largest ever international healthcare project and the largest German direct investment in Ohio history, said Gov. Mike DeWine.
“This was a big investment by New Albany, but also JobsOhio. I think JobsOhio has put $30 million in this, and you're going to see people trained right here and there will come out and go right into Bayer," DeWine told reporters at the company's announcement. 
Bayer is also expected to get an incentive from the Ohio Tax Credit Authority at a later date.
The Bayer plant is estimated to bring 1,500 construction jobs and 600 permanent jobs. The first production unit on the 200-acre plant is planned to come online in five years. Bayer CEO Bill Anderson said construction should begin by the middle of next year, and hiring of technical teams and other workers will start soon.
"I would expect that 90-plus percent will be from Ohio," Anderson said. And that's just the way we do things. When we when we set up shop in a community, we chose that community. If we wanted people from someplace else, we would have gone there."
Also at the event DeWine was asked about attending the funeral for a Haitian student in Springfield who died by suicide last month after losing temporary protected status. DeWine said as parents who lost their 22 year old daughter Becky in a car crash in 1993,, they empathize with the parents of 20-year-old Pierre Damas Bell. 
"We have some understanding of the great trauma and the sorrow that they face," DeWine said. "So this will be parent to parent. No politics. Fran and I just want to be there for the family."
The funeral was held Saturday afternoon, at the same time as a rally for U.S. Sen. Jon Husted featuring President Trump. The Trump administration ended TPS for Haitians in July, telling those immigrants they need to self-deport along with $2,600 stipends or wear ankle monitors while their cases are processed.

title: Onsemi Synaptics Acquisition Turns to Cash After the Original Deal Lost Value - remio
